The contest between Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson has played out mostly on the airwaves, with tens of millions of dollars flooding the state. But the handful of debates between the career politicians managed to print some viral moments -- none to the advantage of Jackson, the former Senate President. At the last debate, Oct. 15 in Bangor, Jackson repeated his claim that Collins votes with President Donald Trump 96% of the time. Collins said the figure covers about a third of Senate votes and put the real number near 72%, Maine Public reported. When a protester interrupted, Collins said he was "obviously one of Troy's supporters." [Jackson replied, "Oh shut up."](https://substack.com/redirect/4fcb28fb-38b7-46c3-bf9c-990963d3b5e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) That comment quickly had millions of dollars spreading it throughout the media, along with a delightful jingle reminding voters of _The Robinson Report 's _exclusive report on Jackson's consanguinity proclivity.
Jackson was also dogged throughout the campaign by financial improprieties first reported by The Maine Wire in August 2023. The revelations centered on a house Jackson and his second cousin purchased in Augusta in 2019 with a [Federal Housing Administration-insured mortgage](https://substack.com/redirect/9506f3cb-4cdf-402c-b124-0b3fd4cbfe46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that required him to make it his principal residence within 60 days, while he represented Allagash in the Maine Senate. "This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," Jackson told the Press Herald in September 2023. He and his cousin, Lana Pelletier, sold the house in December 2021 for $323,000 ($107,000 more than they paid). In October 2023, the Ethics Commission [voted 5-0](https://substack.com/redirect/9f0a196d-eec9-414d-a0e8-3d1bc9291dbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to take no further action on a complaint about the Allagash address on his campaign filings; however, the commission's minutes said mortgage questions belonged with other authorities. Jackson has not been charged with a crime in connection with the mortgage, but the statute of limitations has yet to run out.
Republican ads focused on Jackson's son, Chace Jackson, who [lobbied for the Resurgam Group](https://substack.com/redirect/51fa52d6-898e-4c31-8a8b-6a32cc43eaec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a firm founded by Jackson's former chief of staff, B.J. McCollister. The Senate Leadership Fund had spent more than $4 million by early September on ads about the son's lobbying. Chace Jackson's 2024 disclosure showed clients paid Resurgam $182,500. Asked at the first debate whether payments to his son's firm influenced his decisions, Jackson said his son [had done nothing wrong](https://substack.com/redirect/ace83d13-f79f-4b91-b925-e32972f12035?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which was an odd response considering his son's not the one running for the U.S. Senate.
Jackson's campaign committees reported $26.9 million in receipts from July 7 to Oct. 14, $25.3 million in spending, $1.6 million in cash and $700,952 in debts, according to the Federal Election Commission. Collins' campaign reported $25.4 million in receipts for the cycle, $24.2 million in spending and $2.7 million in cash on its Oct. 22 filing. AdImpact counted about $218 million in broadcast ads booked for the general election as of Oct. 28, $126.1 million on Collins' side and $89.7 million on Jackson's.
### The Blaine House
Virtually everyone in Maine, with a few curious exceptions, believes Hannah Pingree, the nepo-baby of Rep. Chellie Pingree and chief policy guru to outgoing Gov. Janet Mills, will win going away. Charles has polled at 36% or 37% in all three Siena surveys, and Bennett at 8%. UNH found a similar gap, Pingree 51% to Charles 40%. Siena found 51% of unenrolled voters backing Pingree, and about one in 10 Collins voters backing her too.
Pingree's coronation was baked almost the moment Republican Bobby Charles clinched the nomination on the strength of cringe-worthy ChatGPT memes that baby boomers fall for every time and a broader Republican field that was divided between serious alternatives. Charles, 66, a lawyer from Leeds, won the Republican primary in seven rounds with 38% of first choices.
The dagger to the heart of Charles's campaign, though, was a discursive and creepy remark about his personal policy on abortion, which is likely the best piece of video Planned Parenthood ad makers will ever have in their arsenal. On the conservative side, Charles irked fellow Republicans by running a vicious primary campaign with nasty personal attacks all the way to the bitter end, and then he further inflamed antipathy by donning his naval uniform like a Halloween costume and subsequently failing to produce his DD-214. He never did produce the document, for what it's worth, and the Navy tells me they can't find it either.
Pingree, 50, of North Haven, has had a distinguished career as the daughter of a do-nothing congresswoman in a deep blue district and the erstwhile stepdaughter of the pervert mustache attached to billionaire financier S. Donald Sussman. Pingree led Gov. Mills' policy office for six years and, despite that miserable record of failure, the ranked-choice formula ensured that even though Nirav Shah got the most votes, Democrats didn't have to cede their power to the Indian guy.
Rick Bennett was also in the race, but the most noteworthy aspect of his quixotic campaign is the raging debate about whether his tan is real. Despite his astonishing good looks, no one has yet figured out why he ran -- or whether the tan is real.
Pingree's campaign reported $4.98 million in contributions and $4.88 million in spending, according to the Maine Ethics Commission's disclosure system as of Nov. 2, which includes her reports filed through Oct. 27. It showed $77,411 in cash, $202,376 in debt and a $70,000 loan. Charles reported $2.04 million in contributions, $1.78 million in spending, $237,268 in cash and a $280,000 loan balance, with reports filed through Nov. 1. Bennett reported $964,133 in contributions, $891,499 in spending and $63,811 in cash, with reports filed through Oct. 23.
#### ME-CD2
In the 2nd District, LePage, a two-term former governor, and Dunlap, [the state auditor](https://substack.com/redirect/52526559-e868-4928-82f2-642859d71e89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and former secretary of state, are running to replace Democratic Rep. Jared Golden, who [did not seek reelection](https://substack.com/redirect/9f062834-ef7a-45c8-9d21-f6d457eb1634?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The district voted for Trump three times while sending Golden to Congress since 2018. Dunlap beat Joe Baldacci and the thirstiest candidate since Alex Hammer (aka Jordan Wood) in the Democratic primary.
Republicans hold the U.S. House by four seats, and Democrats count this seat in their path to a majority. UNH surveyed 793 likely voters in the district. Its September poll had Dunlap ahead by six, so the race swung 11 points in six weeks in UNH's numbers. Most other polls came from Democratic-aligned firms. Tulchin Research had Dunlap up four in mid-October; a Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee poll in August had LePage up one.
LePage's committees reported $3.3 million in receipts, $2.45 million in spending and $848,224 in cash through Oct. 14, according to the FEC. Dunlap reported $2.96 million in receipts, $2.52 million in spending and $443,968 in cash.
#### ME-CD1
In the 1st District, Democratic Rep. Chellie Pingree, Hannah Pingree's mother, faces Republican Ron Russell, a retired Army colonel from Kennebunkport, for the second time. UNH had Pingree ahead 65% to 32% among about 840 likely voters. Pingree reported $551,078 in receipts, $646,707 in spending and $320,049 in cash through Oct. 14, according to the FEC. Russell reported $214,096 in receipts, $219,953 in spending and $8,364 in cash. Russell's a happy warrior, but the math of ME-CD1 means Pingree would face a more serious threat from Che Guevara.
### The State House
At the state house level, Democrats hold the House of Representatives and the State Senate. Republicans need a net gain of three seats to win the House. In order to win a majority of the combined House and Senate, which would be necessary for Republicans to select an Attorney General, Secretary of State, State Treasurer, and State Auditor, Republicans would have to pick up a combined seven seats.
A House majority takes 76 of 151 seats. Republicans hold 73 and need a net gain of three. In 2024, three House races were decided by a combined 60 votes.
House Republican Leader Billy Bob Faulkingham, R-Winter Harbor, is expected to graduate up to a State Senate seat, leaving a power vacuum behind in the House that has been filled during the campaign season by Republican Minority Leader Katrina Smith. However, at least three other incumbent or likely victorious GOP reps have their eyes on the top spot, whether that's as a new minority leader or holding the gavel as House Speaker, including Rep. Kenn Fredette, R-Newport, who has previously served as a legislative leader and was recently the GOP lead on the appropriations committee.
The Senate has 20 Democrats, 14 Republicans and Bennett. A majority takes 18, so Republicans need a net gain of four. Republican insiders are more focused on maintaining at least one-third of the Senate than they are on growing the caucus, but there are indications an internecine leadership struggle could break out over discontent with how the minority has handled campaign fundraising and campaign spending.
Republicans last held the House in 2012 and the Senate in 2016.
### The Two Paths
Depending on how the final election tally pans out, Maine is looking at two future paths.
One path would mean two to four more years continuing down the roller coaster of despair Mainers have been riding for the entirety of the Janet Mills administration.
That means more Somali welfare pirates looting our paychecks, Chinese drug cartels destroying our houses to sicken Americans with pesticide-laced dope, liberal NGO profiteers littering the streets with HIV-positive syringes in the name of "harm reduction," and vacant-brained Democrats with glassy-eyed SSRI stares who condescendingly tell us we just have to pay a little more of our "fair share" because the transvestite factories and racial grievance academies we used to call schools have run out of money.
The other path would mean at least some semblance of resistance from Republican lawmakers and perhaps -- perhaps -- a return to the LePage Era spine that rejected Augusta's self-enriching culture of corruption.

All eyes will be on Maine's U.S. Senate race as Sen. Susan Collins' fight against Troy Jackson may determine who controls Washington, D.C., while Paul LePage aims to flip a Dem-held House seat. Nov 3 | | | | | | | | | | | Maine voters go to the polls Tuesday to bring a merciful end to Election Month. For just 18 months or so, the inundation of junk mail and ominous television ads will disappear. In place of the overt attempts to seize power by monied interests, Mainers will be subjected to the repercussions of how those monied interests wield that power. Polls close at 8 p.m. If you haven't voted yet, you can look up your polling location . If you need an interpreter to help you translate "needle exchange clinic" into Somali, you can try Abdullahi Ali's cellphone... This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Outside groups have poured more than $190 million into Maine's federal and state races, according to a Maine Wire review of independent-expenditure filings with the Federal Election Commission through Nov. 2 and the Maine Ethics Commission through Nov. 1. Independent expenditures are ads, mail and canvassing paid for by groups that by law may not coordinate with the candidates. | | | | ---|---|--- | Oct 30 | The Senate race drew $148.2 million, $141.2 million of it in the general election. Groups spent $74.5 million against Jackson and $13.7 million for him. They spent $38.6 million against Collins and $7.3 million for her. Another $11.1 million went against Platner before he withdrew, most of it in the general-election period. The biggest spenders were , at $39.1 million, mostly against Jackson; WinSenate at $38.1 million, mostly against Collins; and Pine Tree Results PAC at $31 million against Jackson and Platner. In the 2nd District, outside groups spent $26.2 million, $24.5 million of it in the general election. Groups spent $13.2 million against Dunlap and $1.7 million for him, and $9 million against LePage and $598,293 for him. A committee filing as HMP spent $9 million against LePage. One filing as CLF spent $7 million and Safety & Affordability PAC $5.3 million against Dunlap. The 1st District drew almost nothing: one $10 expenditure for Pingree, by the Sierra Club, in FEC records. State races drew $18.5 million in independent expenditures reported to the Ethics Commission through Nov. 1, including primaries. The governor's race accounted for $12.4 million over the 2026 cycle, including the primaries. Counting only spending dated June 10 or later, after the primary, groups spent $3.09 million against Charles and $345,994 for him, $700,306 for Pingree and $636,343 against her, and $283,680 for Bennett. Restoration of America PAC Maine spent $3.97 million, nearly all of it backing Garrett Mason in the Republican primary. Pine Tree State Prosperity spent $2.71 million against Charles between Sept. 18 and Oct. 23. Legislative races drew $4.7 million: $2.35 million in House races and $2.34 million in Senate races. Across all non-governor state filings, including legislative, county and district attorney races and $1.4 million with no office listed, groups reported $4.4 million in support of candidates and $1.7 million in opposition. The Maine Democratic Party was the largest spender, at $1.39 million in Senate races and $532,410 in House races. Prosper Maine PAC, Lead Maine Action and The House Republican Fund led Republican-aligned spending in House races. As I've said multiple times on Maine Wire TV, I think the whole polling industry is a walking zombie. The technological habits of Americans have outpaced the methodological improvements of those firms who purport to measure public opinion. The whole industry is in crisis, but they won't admit that their polls are mostly worthless because that would be bad for the bottom line. Nonetheless, here are the horse-race stats guys like Nate Silver are still talking about: Democrat Troy Jackson led Republican Sen. Susan Collins 51% to 45% in the final New York Times/Portland Press Herald/Siena poll, released Sunday. In the governor's race, Democrat Hannah Pingree led Republican Bobby Charles 49% to 37%, with independent Rick Bennett at 8%. A University of New Hampshire poll released the same day found former Gov. Paul LePage ahead of Democrat Matt Dunlap in the 2nd Congressional District, 52% to 47%. As is tradition, it bears repeating that polls missed Collins' strength once before. In 2020, every public poll listed by RealClearPolitics showed ex-House Speaker Sara Gideon ahead. Collins won by 8.6 points, 51% to 42.4%. Gideon drifted off into ignominy. Collins, who has served 30 years, is the only Republican senator seeking reelection in a state Trump lost in 2024. Her campaign strategy appears to have been to project normalcy in juxtaposition to the guys with Nazi tattoos, porta-potty masturbation fantasies, children with their cousins, and more pay-to-play scandals than you can count. While Collins has been securing funding for rural Maine hospitals, cutting ribbons at fire stations, and smiling through the vanilla motions of being a politician, Jackson has been posting awkward bubble tea Instagram videos and fending off allegations of corruption from all corners. Jackson, 58 and on his sixth pacemaker, was hand-picked by party insiders after the Democratic nominee, Graham Platner, was browbeaten into dropping out of the race by CNN's Jake Tapper and rape allegations. Despite Maine Democrats taking a pass on Jackson in the earlier gubernatorial race, he was the favorite pick of the 800 or so lobbyists and consultants who jury-rigged an impromptu replacement process. Democratic delegates named Jackson the nominee at a Bangor convention on July 25. | | | | ---|---|--- | Oct 27 | The contest between Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson has played out mostly on the airwaves, with tens of millions of dollars flooding the state. But the handful of debates between the career politicians managed to print some viral moments -- none to the advantage of Jackson, the former Senate President. At the last debate, Oct. 15 in Bangor, Jackson repeated his claim that Collins votes with President Donald Trump 96% of the time. Collins said the figure covers about a third of Senate votes and put the real number near 72%, Maine Public reported. When a protester interrupted, Collins said he was "obviously one of Troy's supporters." That comment quickly had millions of dollars spreading it throughout the media, along with a delightful jingle reminding voters of The Robinson Report 's exclusive report on Jackson's consanguinity proclivity. Jackson was also dogged throughout the campaign by financial improprieties first reported by The Maine Wire in August 2023. The revelations centered on a house Jackson and his second cousin purchased in Augusta in 2019 with a that required him to make it his principal residence within 60 days, while he represented Allagash in the Maine Senate. "This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," Jackson told the Press Herald in September 2023. He and his cousin, Lana Pelletier, sold the house in December 2021 for $323,000 ($107,000 more than they paid). In October 2023, the Ethics Commission to take no further action on a complaint about the Allagash address on his campaign filings; however, the commission's minutes said mortgage questions belonged with other authorities. Jackson has not been charged with a crime in connection with the mortgage, but the statute of limitations has yet to run out. Republican ads focused on Jackson's son, Chace Jackson, who , a firm founded by Jackson's former chief of staff, B.J. McCollister. The Senate Leadership Fund had spent more than $4 million by early September on ads about the son's lobbying. Chace Jackson's 2024 disclosure showed clients paid Resurgam $182,500. Asked at the first debate whether payments to his son's firm influenced his decisions, Jackson said his son , which was an odd response considering his son's not the one running for the U.S. Senate. Jackson's campaign committees reported $26.9 million in receipts from July 7 to Oct. 14, $25.3 million in spending, $1.6 million in cash and $700,952 in debts, according to the Federal Election Commission. Collins' campaign reported $25.4 million in receipts for the cycle, $24.2 million in spending and $2.7 million in cash on its Oct. 22 filing. AdImpact counted about $218 million in broadcast ads booked for the general election as of Oct. 28, $126.1 million on Collins' side and $89.7 million on Jackson's. The Blaine House Virtually everyone in Maine, with a few curious exceptions, believes Hannah Pingree, the nepo-baby of Rep. Chellie Pingree and chief policy guru to outgoing Gov. Janet Mills, will win going away. Charles has polled at 36% or 37% in all three Siena surveys, and Bennett at 8%. UNH found a similar gap, Pingree 51% to Charles 40%. Siena found 51% of unenrolled voters backing Pingree, and about one in 10 Collins voters backing her too. Pingree's coronation was baked almost the moment Republican Bobby Charles clinched the nomination on the strength of cringe-worthy ChatGPT memes that baby boomers fall for every time and a broader Republican field that was divided between serious alternatives. Charles, 66, a lawyer from Leeds, won the Republican primary in seven rounds with 38% of first choices. The dagger to the heart of Charles's campaign, though, was a discursive and creepy remark about his personal policy on abortion, which is likely the best piece of video Planned Parenthood ad makers will ever have in their arsenal. On the conservative side, Charles irked fellow Republicans by running a vicious primary campaign with nasty personal attacks all the way to the bitter end, and then he further inflamed antipathy by donning his naval uniform like a Halloween costume and subsequently failing to produce his DD-214. He never did produce the document, for what it's worth, and the Navy tells me they can't find it either. Pingree, 50, of North Haven, has had a distinguished career as the daughter of a do-nothing congresswoman in a deep blue district and the erstwhile stepdaughter of the pervert mustache attached to billionaire financier S. Donald Sussman. Pingree led Gov. Mills' policy office for six years and, despite that miserable record of failure, the ranked-choice formula ensured that even though Nirav Shah got the most votes, Democrats didn't have to cede their power to the Indian guy. Rick Bennett was also in the race, but the most noteworthy aspect of his quixotic campaign is the raging debate about whether his tan is real. Despite his astonishing good looks, no one has yet figured out why he ran -- or whether the tan is real. Pingree's campaign reported $4.98 million in contributions and $4.88 million in spending, according to the Maine Ethics Commission's disclosure system as of Nov. 2, which includes her reports filed through Oct. 27. It showed $77,411 in cash, $202,376 in debt and a $70,000 loan. Charles reported $2.04 million in contributions, $1.78 million in spending, $237,268 in cash and a $280,000 loan balance, with reports filed through Nov. 1. Bennett reported $964,133 in contributions, $891,499 in spending and $63,811 in cash, with reports filed through Oct. 23. ME-CD2 In the 2nd District, LePage, a two-term former governor, and Dunlap, and former secretary of state, are running to replace Democratic Rep. Jared Golden, who . The district voted for Trump three times while sending Golden to Congress since 2018. Dunlap beat Joe Baldacci and the thirstiest candidate since Alex Hammer (aka Jordan Wood) in the Democratic primary. Republicans hold the U.S. House by four seats, and Democrats count this seat in their path to a majority. UNH surveyed 793 likely voters in the district. Its September poll had Dunlap ahead by six, so the race swung 11 points in six weeks in UNH's numbers. Most other polls came from Democratic-aligned firms. Tulchin Research had Dunlap up four in mid-October; a Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee poll in August had LePage up one. LePage's committees reported $3.3 million in receipts, $2.45 million in spending and $848,224 in cash through Oct. 14, according to the FEC. Dunlap reported $2.96 million in receipts, $2.52 million in spending and $443,968 in cash. ME-CD1 In the 1st District, Democratic Rep. Chellie Pingree, Hannah Pingree's mother, faces Republican Ron Russell, a retired Army colonel from Kennebunkport, for the second time. UNH had Pingree ahead 65% to 32% among about 840 likely voters. Pingree reported $551,078 in receipts, $646,707 in spending and $320,049 in cash through Oct. 14, according to the FEC. Russell reported $214,096 in receipts, $219,953 in spending and $8,364 in cash. Russell's a happy warrior, but the math of ME-CD1 means Pingree would face a more serious threat from Che Guevara. The State House At the state house level, Democrats hold the House of Representatives and the State Senate. Republicans need a net gain of three seats to win the House. In order to win a majority of the combined House and Senate, which would be necessary for Republicans to select an Attorney General, Secretary of State, State Treasurer, and State Auditor, Republicans would have to pick up a combined seven seats. A House majority takes 76 of 151 seats. Republicans hold 73 and need a net gain of three. In 2024, three House races were decided by a combined 60 votes. House Republican Leader Billy Bob Faulkingham, R-Winter Harbor, is expected to graduate up to a State Senate seat, leaving a power vacuum behind in the House that has been filled during the campaign season by Republican Minority Leader Katrina Smith. However, at least three other incumbent or likely victorious GOP reps have their eyes on the top spot, whether that's as a new minority leader or holding the gavel as House Speaker, including Rep. Kenn Fredette, R-Newport, who has previously served as a legislative leader and was recently the GOP lead on the appropriations committee. The Senate has 20 Democrats, 14 Republicans and Bennett. A majority takes 18, so Republicans need a net gain of four. Republican insiders are more focused on maintaining at least one-third of the Senate than they are on growing the caucus, but there are indications an internecine leadership struggle could break out over discontent with how the minority has handled campaign fundraising and campaign spending. Republicans last held the House in 2012 and the Senate in 2016. The Two Paths Depending on how the final election tally pans out, Maine is looking at two future paths. One path would mean two to four more years continuing down the roller coaster of despair Mainers have been riding for the entirety of the Janet Mills administration. That means more Somali welfare pirates looting our paychecks, Chinese drug cartels destroying our houses to sicken Americans with pesticide-laced dope, liberal NGO profiteers littering the streets with HIV-positive syringes in the name of "harm reduction," and vacant-brained Democrats with glassy-eyed SSRI stares who condescendingly tell us we just have to pay a little more of our "fair share" because the transvestite factories and racial grievance academies we used to call schools have run out of money. The other path would mean at least some semblance of resistance from Republican lawmakers and perhaps -- perhaps -- a return to the LePage Era spine that rejected Augusta's self-enriching culture of corruption. Tune in to Maine Wire TV at 4 p.m. for the news of the day followed by our special election livestream at 8 p.m. EST when the polls close. Good morning, everybody. It is Election Day.
**First things first:** If you still need to find your polling location or see what is on your ballot, visit [VOTE411, from the League of Women Voters](https://substack.com/redirect/f271ba61-63aa-40d7-b931-e716ea56549f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Enter your address to find your voting information. You can also check with your local **Board of Elections.**
Hopefully, you already have your plan. If you don't, **get it together and go vote.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bb927e8a-ade8-470b-8262-526fa9118765?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Going into today, there are a couple of things on my mind that I want to pass along. This election, in my opinion, is a litmus test for much more than control of Congress.
It is about character. It is about promises. It is about whether people care more about their party or the people representing them.
And when the results come in, it will be about understanding what voters actually said.
* * *
## Trump's Promises Versus Reality
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/407ded97-9e81-4f08-86d9-436014155ed2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Donald Trump got a second chance as president of the United States. He made some bold promises, including two that people could easily understand: **no more forever wars and lower costs.**
Look at where we are.
The war with Iran has now lasted more than eight months. What was supposed to be a quick military operation has become another prolonged conflict in the Middle East, with American service members deployed overseas and families wondering what comes next.
Meanwhile, the war has driven up energy costs. You feel it at the pump. Businesses feel it buying diesel to transport goods. Those costs work their way into the prices you pay at the store.
Lower costs and no more forever wars. Those were the promises. But we have a different reality.
At the same time, Trump's family businesses have **generated billions** from cryptocurrency ventures. His name is attached to everything from cell phones to digital assets and stablecoin ventures.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/8b0b6ba3-3e21-4075-ab2b-7294c0b63301?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bloomberg counted more securities trades by Trump or his money managers than by all of Congress combined.
People struggling to fill their gas tanks are watching a president whose business interests keep expanding.
Will voters who supported him in 2024 hold him accountable for that? Will they compare what he promised with what he delivered? Or does the party affiliation matter more?
**Today, we find out.**
* * *
## Ohio's Seventh District Is a Character Test
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f3766376-2c24-4944-9aa4-3325f4406b69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here in Ohio's Seventh District, we have another version of that question.
Max Miller is someone I know well. The domestic violence allegations surrounding him involve multiple women and accounts reaching back roughly two decades. Miller denies the allegations.
Some of the most shocking revelations came this summer amid the fallout from his divorce and child custody dispute.
The response reached his own party. Republican Senator Jon Husted called on Miller to resign and leave the race. Republican Senator Bernie Moreno said Miller was unfit to serve.
These are Ohio's two Republican senators.
Now voters have to make their own decision.
In a district Trump carried by roughly 11 points in 2024, will Republicans and independents join Democrats in deciding that character matters more than keeping a Republican in the seat?
How much are people willing to overlook for their party? At what point do they say that the person asking to represent them has crossed a line?
**That question is on the ballot, too.**
* * *
## The Polling Gets Its Test
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/742e7852-63f9-46ab-84c6-d5385add623b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then there is the question I have been writing about throughout this election: Can we trust the information being put in front of us?
The polls. The headlines. The predictions. The confidence that a massive blue wave is coming.
Have pollsters accounted for the electorate correctly? Have the media explained the uncertainty, or have they turned close races into confident narratives? Are readers being shown the margin of error with the same enthusiasm as the favorable headline?
The president's party usually loses House seats in a midterm election. History favors the opposition, but it does not guarantee a change in control. I expect Democrats to take the House. The Senate remains another major question.
If the enormous Democratic sweep people have been predicting fails to materialize, we need to go back and examine the information that shaped those expectations.
Who got it wrong? Why? Who repeated numbers without examining them? Who sold certainty where there was uncertainty?
And if Democrats win the House and Senate, great. Then we hold them accountable for what they do with that power.
Winning an election does not finish the job.
* * *
## A Vote Against Trump Is Not Automatically a Vote for Democrats
A friend of mine voted Republican down the ballot in 2024. He told me he is voting entirely Democratic this time, out of spite.
He does not suddenly love the Democratic Party. **No.** He wants to get back at Trump.
It is a protest vote.
I have seen Republicans online say similar things. Other people I have spoken with say they are crossing party lines because they believe the other candidate has better character.
Those votes can produce the same result on election night while coming from very different places.
Democrats need to understand that distinction.
If someone votes for your candidate because they are furious with Trump, you have won their vote for this election. What happens after that is still an open question.
Will they stay? Will they return to voting Republican in the next presidential election? Have their policy preferences changed, or have they reached their limit with the people currently running the Republican Party?
A Democratic victory could reflect enthusiasm, rejection, or some combination of both. The party needs to figure out which.
* * *
## What Are Voters More Afraid Of?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b770c08d-2d24-4e73-b7f9-6ccac438ee87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Mayor Zorhan Mamdani
This is also a test of the Democratic Party's competing visions.
There are establishment Democrats, progressive Democrats, and the Democratic Socialists of America. They have different ideas about what the party should become, and Republicans have spent plenty of money trying to make socialism the reason voters reject all of them.
Will that argument work?
Are voters more afraid of the word "socialism" than they are of high gas prices, another prolonged war, and uncertainty about what comes next?
Just before Election Day, Tucker Carlson claimed that the administration could be days away from launching a nuclear strike on Iran. That is an unverified claim, but it is the kind of warning now entering people's conversations as they prepare to vote.
Think about that atmosphere.
[| | | | | Tucker Carlson
---
@TuckerCarlson
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran. The target would be Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence claims the Iranian government has restarted its...
| 1:47 AM * Nov 2, 2026 * 46.1M Views18.3K Replies * 51.3K Reposts * 275K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/35dd6307-6c1e-4ee0-b328-d7a72e3a136c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
People are weighing their bills, the economy, war, and the possibility of further escalation. At the same time, campaigns are telling them that the real threat is the other party's ideology.
Which concern wins?
And if voters reject the Republican message today, what exactly are they embracing?
Are they moving toward Democratic policies? Are they rejecting Trump personally? Are they rejecting what his Republican Party has become?
Those questions matter long after the victory speeches.
* * *
## What Today Will Tell Us
Here is how I sum it up.
Does character still matter? That is on the ballot.
Do promises matter? That is on the ballot.
Can we trust the polling and the information being sold to us? That gets tested today.
Are Democrats gaining support, or are Republicans losing it? That distinction is on the ballot, too.
I will be watching the results come in with you, breaking down the races and looking at what we can actually learn from them.
### **Go vote.**
And to all the candidates of character asking for the opportunity to represent their communities: **Good luck.**

Peter,
I'll be honest with you... I'm not great at asking for money. It's the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn't spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn't become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That's really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it's going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. I couldn't just sit there.](https://trk.email.repdailyred._)
But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don't have a massive machine behind me. I don't have someone who can write blank checks on a whim.
[I just have normal folks like you.](https://trk.email.repdailyred.__Q)

I didn't spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf. And when I came home, I didn't become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals. That's really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it's going in the wrong direction most days. But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don't have a massive machine behind me. I don't have someone who can write blank checks on a whim. I know things are tight right now. I see it at the grocery store just like you do. But if you can spare even $5 to help keep a Navy Vet and a Nurse Practitioner in this fight, it would mean the world to me. | | | | | Please, help us hold the line. \- Jen | I would not be where I am today without the help of my incredible and faithful supporters like you. Because of your support, I can keep fighting to make our country stronger. In the northern part of our district, "The Depot" is universally understood to refer to the Anniston Army Depot. It's a big deal. Just under 4,000 people work there, most of them U.S. Government employees, and it's a major economic asset to five counties.
The Depot was established in 1940 on more than 10,000 acres just outside the Calhoun County seat. It was built to store ammunition, and very few people outside the US Army and North Alabama had heard of The Depot until 2003, when it was designated as one of the facilities where the United States would destroy its chemical weapons stockpiles. That mission ended in 2011.
When I started campaigning, I almost instantly heard, "You know, Mike Rogers saved The Depot." The story goes that if Mike Rogers had not been in Congress, some evil politician, probably a Democrat, would have closed The Depot, and thousands of jobs would have been lost. In a community that had already lost Fort McClellan, Rogers saving The Depot would have been a VERY big deal. There's just one problem: it never happened. ....

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
The day is here. Tomorrow is election day, a chance for us to make history and change the direction of our nation.
I have seen a change over the last year. Now, everywhere we go, people want to stop and talk about our ideas and policies. Some are still entrenched in their thinking, but so many others want to engage.
And I've heard many, many times, "I've never voted for a Democrat before, but I'm going to vote for you."
I want to thank everyone who has been a part of this campaign. Your support from day 1 has been the backbone of our efforts. You have held us up through some hard times and stepped up before we even knew to ask for help. We would not be here without you.
This campaign was born on June 15, 2025, the day after the first No Kings protest. That was 505 days ago. I always knew I would be writing this at the bottom of a newsletter at some point, but now that it's here, it feels strange.
We are 1 day away from the general election.
Be Well. Thank You All.
We will talk soon.

Lee

clean_body: You Don't Want to Miss This | | | | | == | | | CAMPAIGN UPDATE | | | | | Things To Remember: Recheck your polling place here: == Make sure you have a photo ID. If you are told you are not eligible to vote, DO NOT LEAVE YOUR PRECINCT. ASK FOR A PROVISIONAL BALLOT. CAST YOUR VOTE, THEN ASK FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO CERTIFY YOUR BALLOT. They must provide you with a provisional ballot and instructions on how to certify it. DO NOT LEAVE YOUR PRECINCT WITHOUT VOTING. If you're not comfortable with anything... anything at all... ask to speak with the precinct supervisor. Explain the problem. Don't leave until you're satisfied. Again, if you're not comfortable, ask to speak to the precinct supervisor. Finally, keep this number: 1-833-468-6832. It is the voter hotline at "I Will Vote," and they support voting in Alabama. Call that number if you have any worries. Then DM me on social media. I'll keep an eye on things as best I can. | | | MAKING HISTORY | | THE WEEK AHEAD | | Sign Waving and Happy Hour Park near El Patron Restaurant in Tiger Town, we will wave signs on the corner of Fredrick Rd and 280, then we'll have Happy Hour at El Patron, first round is on Lee. 🗓️ November 2 🕓 4:00 P.M. The corner of Fredrick Road and 280, Auburn AL | | | VOTE!!! Bring your yard sign and add it to the others at least 30 feet from the door. 🗓️ November 3 🕓 7:00 A.M. -7:00 P.M. 📍 Find your polling place on the Alabama Secretary of State Website == | | | | THE WEEK BEHIND | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | In Case You Missed It | | BLOG POSTS | == In the northern part of our district, "The Depot" is universally understood to refer to the Anniston Army Depot. It's a big deal. Just under 4,000 people work there, most of them U.S. Government employees, and it's a major economic asset to five counties. The Depot was established in 1940 on more than 10,000 acres just outside the Calhoun County seat. It was built to store ammunition, and very few people outside the US Army and North Alabama had heard of The Depot until 2003, when it was designated as one of the facilities where the United States would destroy its chemical weapons stockpiles. That mission ended in 2011. When I started campaigning, I almost instantly heard, "You know, Mike Rogers saved The Depot." The story goes that if Mike Rogers had not been in Congress, some evil politician, probably a Democrat, would have closed The Depot, and thousands of jobs would have been lost. In a community that had already lost Fort McClellan, Rogers saving The Depot would have been a VERY big deal. There's just one problem: it never happened. .... | == | A Few Things to Think About | | | | | FROM THE NEWS | == Three Democratic candidates, along with the wife of Lee McInnis, joined to talk about their experience and what they would like to happen in their respective offices if elected. | A CALL TO ACTION | This won't be a year when we can sit back and expect everyone else to do the work. If you want to change the direction of the country, you have to get into the game. If you can help us with any of these efforts, drop us a note, and we will be in touch. Here is what you can do to help us win in November: | Make a plan to vote: Tell everyone you know to vote, offer rides to the polls, THEN VOTE. | | One Last Thought Until Next Week | | | The day is here. Tomorrow is election day, a chance for us to make history and change the direction of our nation. I have seen a change over the last year. Now, everywhere we go, people want to stop and talk about our ideas and policies. Some are still entrenched in their thinking, but so many others want to engage. And I've heard many, many times, "I've never voted for a Democrat before, but I'm going to vote for you." I want to thank everyone who has been a part of this campaign. Your support from day 1 has been the backbone of our efforts. You have held us up through some hard times and stepped up before we even knew to ask for help. We would not be here without you. This campaign was born on June 15, 2025, the day after the first No Kings protest. That was 505 days ago. I always knew I would be writing this at the bottom of a newsletter at some point, but now that it's here, it feels strange. We are 1 day away from the general election. Be Well. Thank You All. We will talk soon. Hey folks,
Election Day is here. Today, Ohio decides whose voice is louder: working people or billionaires.
When I launched this campaign, I told you the air was getting toxic for Ohio families. I told you that the system is rigged.
Ohio deserves a leader who fights for you. Winning this campaign is the first step in doing that.
I hope you are proud of the role you are playing in setting our campaign up for victory.
This has been the honor of my life. I feel so lucky for every conversation out on the road, every phone call, every message on here and every reply you've sent us.
I'm grateful.
This is what I wrote to you on the day that I launched my campaign for U.S. Senate, if you'd like to take a trip down memory lane.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/0620c6e3-a221-4942-8bce-0ea0486f664b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# **I 'm Running for U.S. Senate. Here's Why.**
Every day, I wear the same pin on my lapel.
It's a small yellow canary, given to me by a steelworker at a Workers' Memorial Day rally in Lorain.
In the early 20th century, coal miners would carry a canary underground with them. If the air turned poisonous, the canary detected it first so the miners knew to get out, before it was too late.
They didn't have a union strong enough, or a government that cared enough, to warn them. To protect them.
Through organizing and years of hard work, _that changed._
And not just on mine safety. We fought for - and won - safer workplaces, fair wages, Social Security, Medicare, civil rights, and voting rights. We made progress that generations before us could only dream of.
But right now, the air is getting toxic again for working people. Alarm bells are ringing.
Wages aren't keeping up. The cost of everything - groceries, housing, health care - keeps climbing. And the same forces that fought against fair pay and safer workplaces all those years ago are back at it. They're rigging the rules to benefit their wealthy donors and corporate special interests.
Ohioans feel like the system is rigged against them._And it is._
**I never planned to run for office again.**
**But when I see politicians in Washington working for the rich and powerful instead of the people who make this country run, I just can 't sit on the sidelines.**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d010676a-df37-4c39-b90a-2bd883f1d58a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=5574704&post_id=223211658&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIzMjExNjU4LCJpYXQiOjE3OTM3MDgzNDgsImV4cCI6MTc5NjMwMDM0OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTU1NzQ3MDQiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.FbuxHUGz2EEJQoNq9U_nJQ7n_zKgU5xF9fdoUP4ggqc)
**That 's why today, I'm announcing my campaign for U.S. Senate.**
Because I've seen what our country - and the Senate - can look like at its best. What it looks like when workers are at the table, not on the menu.
For me, this isn't about left vs. right -_it 's about which side you're on; who you fight for and who you're willing to stand up to._
This moment demands champions for our working families. Because whether you punch a clock, swipe a badge, work for tips, or care for a family member - you deserve the tools you need to build the life you want.
Not just to put food on the table, but to build a good life for your family.
Not just to afford rent, but to afford a home, in the community you want to live in.
Not just to have a job, but a career with great wages, strong benefits, and dignity.
The people who make this country work deserve their fair share. And at this moment when workers are struggling - we need leaders in Washington who will put them first.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0620c6e3-a221-4942-8bce-0ea0486f664b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So I'm asking you to join me. If you're ready to join my campaign from Day One, consider **[making a donation to power our movement](https://substack.com/redirect/0620c6e3-a221-4942-8bce-0ea0486f664b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** or forwarding this to a few friends.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=5574704&post_id=223211658&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIzMjExNjU4LCJpYXQiOjE3OTM3MDgzNDgsImV4cCI6MTc5NjMwMDM0OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTU1NzQ3MDQiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.FbuxHUGz2EEJQoNq9U_nJQ7n_zKgU5xF9fdoUP4ggqc)
This moment is our canary. Its warning is loud and clear.
What we do next is going to depend on all of us.
Are you with me?
\- Sherrod
Before you click away!
Our resources are zeroed out. We've allocated every dollar that came in the door to reach voters before polls close tonight. That means our accounts will be empty (or maybe even a little in the red). That's on purpose. **But it 's also taking a big risk.**
If the result is too close to call and Sherrod's fight continues beyond tonight, we won't have the resources we need to wage it. Outside groups have shown they're willing to spend ungodly sums to buy this seat. We can only expect they'll do the same with Senate control still on the line.
**[If you have the means and would like to help get out ahead of that, make a donation right now.](https://substack.com/redirect/0620c6e3-a221-4942-8bce-0ea0486f664b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

## Tennessee Voters Head to the Polls
Tennesseans are [casting ballots today](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykzzuO6yAUgOHV2F0sDiY8CorbpMttp0Q8DjYShsgcOcruRzNbmAX8v_R9Pd3Tl1ra9t8faImya_geFYnwdFgxUukt-U8uWFPPe2_99M1xxuUN4MZW5yOVC53wc7KBg_EizmhBmVUxAWDm3d5Z0ErfE2o0KuUQvQrRxBQwACSh5mJ_hgBsBWB6lYs0OmuZwOuU5ZrzJBimQv1caEfC1nAMxFw__cJzif2Yq92JXmNa_038MfHH6GOhtmz9mvhj61cnpDafNr3epdYypJoE2w5f6m9Of7Rfln8HAAD__wWlb64) in the state and federal general election, and polling places and hours, which vary by county, are listed on the state's GoVoteTN site. At the top of the ballot is an open race for governor between Republican Marsha Blackburn, Democrat Jerri Green, and independents David Hatley and Lauren Pinkston, plus a [U.S. Senate seat and all nine U.S. House seats](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAQgOHT4C4RMyBsFxSv8auSaqUtrYkZYiQCFh7Fyu1X3its_-sr_u_bfKOUU3ne6cVeJM6Fjz2zCLeZMy-Sagn0iYlzqHGtpTYqM2p0F4CLNjMtkt48W-qCfyCMZJeOPfSj6bUFGLvVs8WR6IGjdgsGGIA0m8FYt4S-Dw_skj9BAG0A9GDc1Y1DHFwAGkJ0JkZlNYcktV1lZeFSeN-ZY_7UN7frUl9d9qvItivzT-GkcDqO42yfjblstHHbz0zh9B-dwunr3jUftiPlnHbXK6ufL0r5l5I_fnh7_AkAAP__MChyHA) under a new congressional map. Voters will also decide state legislative races, and [three proposed constitutional amendments](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OrDAQhE9jMiP_gIHAwUvI5qUbIg_dHiwZG9m9oLn9ign2Apt01Prqq_p6LA8XYkiv_25HS-SXhFeNSIRlwYgrhZzAvX3ACNlvOeXi0qKEMlxKLvTiVgonLp1rwD6VnFy3NmjlMOlBdFJOzWafIIQf176D_gmq0wrM5DSIaZBy7AfTBHsDpRRaSjFq05pp9KMB6UbwRnvPOoEQKJeWNiRMCWtF9PGdTyztmvcm2o3oqEz_Y2pmar6uq3Uf-7tQf_8wNd8xTM1S3EczNf-y-JkJS-WAawDk3hFyzY-Sj1wR-JpTpUDfN9BF7nZMsGOiytTcFAvHFWIM1QysE6_dhfiRoj8uelr1EwAA__8pJovf) on bail, a state property tax ban, and crime victims' rights. More than [1.28 million Tennesseans voted early](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu2zAQRE9DdTS4K0YmCxZp1P20KQVKXFrEp7kGtbbh2wdKkQukHTzMDN7vr-Urllra7Ve8UxDJS6P3UUmE-kKVNincUvzkQjVx3rlxj21Bg5MG0GZc4iblRYuNQworgo92GyjA1Y9XYwH8sAdAl3Ia0dLqV2-AVp_ij2g3SmmjzQ4lnIUAZgQwbpwuk3fZTQmiS3kac1bWUCrC_SI7CbVGx0GU64df1C8b34cadpHHocafCmeF8z-oMn_zU05I4XzuKJwBFM4GFc4Ue_3oF0tpNy3P3vgpWvhxaNDo7jquZ-Ddtz527qI5azTgtLDEqnAeekiPd6m1HNNVWXO7x1L_PpL_1PkK-CcAAP__bOiKOQ), about 45% more than in 2022. Questions can go to the state's Election Day hotline at 1-877-850-4959.
## Mayor Orders Study of Nashville General
Mayor Freddie O'Connell [formed a vision committee](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2u3CAQBeCnwR0rfnzZpXCRxt1Nm9KaNcMaCZgVzNrx20dOkRdIOxp9Ouf8-l6-IeVUXz-h4MQcl4pHz8iMbcGMKyeqAc6YMAeKG1VqUBejjJNaS2UXWDntuIwwhOlptIdxHXDSd2_vatTaD9tkvTfRae29VSo6uH9Zb56IaEbtolNDmi5Qa2W1Vg_rbs4_4sMFDY8QnY1RjApDYmo33pCxVuwdMeaTdmy3lcqQp4353YX9IcwszHwcx-2qsm5QK-av60mY-ToJM3cGRmHmf5Qwc4A9hU5VrvSpfAozFzipSVrpErKM1EqXK5WSmBElk8TfUFJFGT_8aSgpygp921POKF9YsUGWG_V3YshDm8L7SDmn7u5iVK8CKf_Nzv85_D6ZPwEAAP__h-idJw) to study Nashville General Hospital's future, including whether the city's public hospital should stay at its current site or move. The committee will also examine the hospital's teaching partnership with Meharry Medical College and how to keep public costs manageable, and O'Connell said he has no predetermined outcome. Nashville General has operated on Meharry's campus since 1998 and [provides about $60 million in uncompensated care each year](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOke2ITYULv6GLn97JVrsNazk2BFeyOXtT9wrXDejkUYz39djfgAlyut_eKJjjnPGd03IjPuMCT1TyQE-kTCFEreSyw551lIboZSQ3Qye6cS5hza4RasRet-iU3bsrOyVGtvN-fsYjb3LBayyRoIeB68G6_veaNSoW3JXoVKyU0oOnbmZcYiDCQqGEE0XY9NLDMRlv_GGjDljrYgxfcqJ-82XZ5vcxvyqTfev0VOjp1i-lb2SRk_XpUZPqXhIl4W6nZQSihUz7pCqgJXyKpaDUrjE6-AqPOwoIAfhS2VBWcTijyqgCk_8ERE8VsG0biyWI6zI7e7C600pUTW26eX6BEq_4_iPZE-nfwIAAP__eFSQTA), the mayor said. The move follows a turbulent stretch for the hospital, including its CEO's [2025 resignation after an audit raised concerns about spending](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb9GOw0PHEYLim3sZtstzVMeAwmCgTdj_PvN7C9sfZN7cs7PY3lgiCE9v3Enw-yWRGeNxExloUgbh5wsXi5QtNn5nHLBtEghdQfQCbXgxuFNy4CtNauECYetJQP3Sd3FADC13tA6oCapLdCGcpoGYdFt8gZSWaW1aIP5HAIIBSBGpXs9jW7UFnC0TivnmkGQDZxLz56YUqJaiVy88ptKv-W9jcYzH7VRX42cGzmf59lf6HP-rI2cP1qNnHe8cul8PkJ6ditV7o5ca1gjde7Fr0KduAlQIPXUe95jW4w9zhBjqPreDOK5Y4h_QP5nrbeRvwEAAP__cQR_3Q).
## Heavy Rain Threatens Wednesday Commute
A strong cold front will bring [heavy rain to Middle Tennessee](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOpDAQRU9jMiOXoQ0EDjYh6003RNW43FgydsuuBXH7ERPMBSb-T09P_99zeWKIIb3_4k6W2S-JzhqJmcpCkVYOOTm8fKDost9yygXTopU2EkCqbsGVw0FLj42zLw0T9mtDFoapG1QPMDWbfYEjgtegAQAehhBG10_gaDVePeDRBHsLAVQHoMbOtGYa_Wgc4Oi86bwXvSIXOJeWN2JKiWol8vHKB5V2zXsT7cb8qaL7I_Qs9HyeZ3vW_bhHoefbL_QMIPSstNCzD6WyxEiF5UnIGxXp8JKh1v_k5EZ4XLJgSB5jlLwVwht0ieqN7bmkkN5yD85Fkj9JQs9Nse5zhhhDNYPo1XvHEL8b-ZcHH1Z_BQAA___0H5Ho) Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, prompting a First Alert Weather Day. Forecasters [expect 1 to 2 inches of rain](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL3O3CAURJ8Gd7b4W4wLijTuNm1K6y5c1igYVnBla98-cl7hK0cjzRydP8_tCSmn8v4NBzqiuBW8ekYibBtm9JRqCfCNCXOoca-lNiib5NKMQoxcbeApnbhpGIJ7SbGA9gM6MS9q5lqIZdhdeJiwPJDPCxrhpVKSh1cEbeXDKqv9kNw9KARXQnCrzGQWG60JAmyIRsXINMeQqLaJdiQsBXtHjPlbT2yTr8eQ3U706Uz9YnJlcr2ua7r-tnKXd0SgHdu4I4ScCnYmVypjrA09dGJyLfXE44VtlOMNw-Q6NBc-V8o5dTMzzd8HpPz_jH5o6nTyXwAAAP__xdF9gA), with poor visibility and hydroplaning making Wednesday's morning commute hazardous. Rain chances in Memphis are about 85% on Election Day itself, while Nashville and East Tennessee should stay mostly dry until the front arrives. Cooler air settles in behind it, with highs falling into the upper 50s and low 60s across much of the state by the weekend.

Congress.

[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

In August 2026 the national debt passed $40 trillion.1 It was not
voted on. There was no ceremony. Most Americans found out from a
headline, if they found out at all.

Somebody has to absorb it

A debt that size does not simply sit there. It gets serviced,
refinanced, and eventually dealt with — and there are only three
ways to deal with it: raise taxes, cut spending, or reduce the real
value of what is owed by letting the currency weaken. The first two
require Congress to do something unpopular on the record. The third
requires nobody to do anything at all.

That is why the figure matters to a retirement account rather than
just to a budget committee. Every dollar in your IRA is a claim
denominated in the same currency the debt is denominated in.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.
If the obligation is managed down in real terms, that happens through
your savings, not around them.

The evidence is already behind us. It takes roughly $1.95 today to
buy what a dollar bought in 2000.2 Nothing was confiscated. The unit
was simply worth less each year, and savers holding it carried the
cost quietly.

Gold is the one asset in this conversation with no issuer. No
treasury can print it, no company can dilute it, no counterparty can
default on it. Central banks themselves have been buying more than a
thousand tons a year.3 They are not doing it for the yield.

You are allowed to hold physical gold inside an IRA. Most savers
have never been told that, because the firms holding their money do
not sell it. The free 2026 Gold IRA Guide walks through exactly how a
rollover from an IRA, 401(k) or TSP works, which metals the IRS
allows, how insured depository storage works, and the mistakes that
cost retirees the most. It is free and it takes about thirty seconds
to request.

clean_body: Don’t go to sleep on election night wishing you did more. | | | | Patriot, Don't go to sleep on election night wishing you did more. That's the standard our Turning Point Action team is holding itself to. Right now, they're all gas, no brakes, and I couldn't be more proud of them. Everything this team is doing is more than just showing up right before November, because that's not what actually wins elections. It's about building real connections while reaching voters where they are, in their neighborhoods. It takes years of preparation, with our door-knockers building relationships and earning trust. This is what my husband built Turning Point Action to do. Charlie wanted voting to become a habit for every America-loving patriot in this country, and our team is making that dream a reality, one front door at a time. Here's a look at what our team is doing on the ground right now: ✅ Hosting over 500 Super Chase events nationwide up until Election Day, activating people to chase votes in their own communities. ✅ Training and deploying 850+ full-time ballot chasers across key states, with the number increasing by the day. ✅ Making sure voters in key states have a plan to submit their vote, through the work of our Chase the Vote team. ✅ Working day and night at headquarters so our field teams have everything they need to identify and reach every possible voter. ✅ Calling, texting, and writing postcards to voters, and hosting community events to get out the vote. ✅ Developing the "Freedom Ticket" as a personalized voter guide for patriots to use at the voting booth in key battlegrounds. ✅ Building permanent infrastructure in the new "Red Wall" states of Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire. When I see this machine at work, I see Charlie's vision growing stronger across America. There's not much time left for our ballot chasers to reach every voter they can. I'm inviting you to join them in this final push across the finish line. Thank you for standing with the Turning Point family. Let's do the work to win. ## Election Day Opens With 56M Early Votes
Americans head to the polls today to decide control of Congress, with more than 56 million ballots [already cast early](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAUhJ_GdIv8B_YtXNyGbtOmtIx9vHsig5E5Ae3bR6yUJ0g7I83MN593fw9YcH18hAUc5epXOPcCRNA8FIiEdU3hRe172XKpgfYtNC-5HG9C3LjyIRIe4EWXXAaQoDpwwvxThg9aqe7ptM1z0nKYg1A5mjQEa0wGYcchj2mWHborTgiuhFBc2t4kwUEZa_RoxmA10xwSUm39V8WVnpDLqx7Q-liXrrgn0bYz9Z_JicnpPM9-neOFcflMTlstSBh3Jqf37l-sS4DQyut2VIKuubSdWAruo2GaP5aA5d1Af_vlcPInAAD__0W_d9M), about 24 million of them by mail. That is a midterm record, topping the [45.9 million early votes](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uhDAUhE8DnZH_FkPhIg3dpk2JHPt5eZHBlv0C2ttHu1dIOTPS6NP3dV_vDhMej0-3g6WY1wOuloAI6goJPGE-gntS_d1LTNlRK66uksuRCcG4Wp0nPGEVfbARQILqwQozK8NvWql-sxD0PLsxhHH6nuLsxtsNojYSdIh88lOP9nUnBFdCKC6nwQTBQZnJ6NGMbtKd5hCQch1-Mh60QUzPfEIdfN77ZDei0jr10cmlk8t1XcNF53vs5FJyQkLfOrm4HSp6x85M8Mp4sAK15YOBq-n56vF4sA2psQo-18CK88BirmzHQFD31lcbyoUpYRtNp_ljd5jeHPQ_e6eVfwEAAP__C8GHPg) cast before Election Day in 2022. Much of the jump came from in-person early voting. In the battle for control of the Senate, analysts are watching for results tonight in [six toss-up races](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO4zAQBNDTUJkMNimJdMBgE2XedEOBFltWL_gRyLY9vv1Ac4WJC_WAqn-35eYpUn789Qkdb2XJ-G4RmbEuGHFlKjn4D9dnOrZYPLfD10VJNfUAvdSLX5leuEAX3IaoUHfowFy1keOgdbc7OcLdKq2nUcJ9tMZ4hAAjSqvv5jpeO3InByA1gJbKXkwAidpYM0xm8nYQg8RAXOrlf6HMO27xU15YL2tJXXQ789GE_iPULNTMO-4U45kJNe8l4blIqHn16fD0yELNE9hxMLJvmD1jv5bMtcQ-UWCsqW_01XNp7Xmcva66cLwpRmqTEYN8JE8_fMe_O-zl1HcAAAD__87_fy4), all currently held by Republicans. They include Maine, where Republican Sen. Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson, and Texas, where Republican Ken Paxton faces Democrat James Talarico, as well as Senate races in Alaska, Ohio, Iowa, and Kansas. The Senate race in Michigan, where Republican Mike Rogers faces Democrat Abdul El-Sayed for an open Democrat-held seat, is seen as the GOP’s best chance to pick up a Democrat's seat. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to flip the Senate.
## Trump Floats Pardons for Musk, Staff
President Trump said he would [issue preemptive pardons](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO3SAQxvHT4I4nGLzYLii8itxtmhQpLQTDMwk2CObZ2pw-8uYIqUf6NL__z4_1w8YUj-d3u6OhkNcDr5aQCOuKCR3FfHj7SfW1l5CypVZsXUGA5lJyoVbrKJ64ys6bgAioOjRymNQg3nqlus0op9HBFMBqgQH0FISctPb6DexoneqiueekFEpKJWB8DF4KVMM49HrQduxZL9BHyvXxK8eDNgzpM59YHy7vXTIbUWlMzQwWBst1XY-9HfeNwYIHfzUGy61isGTasDJYvjj8zFfjlHmpmdAR31_tN_-H5KUix73cNt7IhsCLrT4f94qtfJ7hOf95D0wt2UXP1Lf3OyJe7QfW0lXjyxVTik0PrBfP3cb09S39X-PTwN8AAAD__4lOksM) to Elon Musk and members of his administration if Democrats win Congress today and follow through on threats to investigate them. _" I would if I needed to. Mark Milley, the Jan. 6 committee, and Biden's own family. Democrats have signaled they would probe Musk's run at DOGE, his companies' [federal contracts](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFy6yAQBuDToE4aWCSQC4rX0Pm1KTVYrGwSJDSwtka3z-BMTpDuL3Z3_m8_rtPVhRi2-3-3oqElTRseJSIR5gkjzhTS5t1J-bnuS0yOyu7yBBxUK0TL5eRmCi-cROPNgggoGzRCX6TmQy9l8zBcaLko3yt9G_2FD-AWqbwf_G0ZYfZjE0w9JwSXQkgOY6e94Cj1qHullRt71nP0gVLuPlPY6IFLPNMLczentYnmQbQXJv8xsAzscRzdszhK3p11gIEtlPLJwFYaA7unGCjMNf4Ka64lGFghGFgODOzb3P6g291ln7bSYkxbuz7LV-uCx7p3gUGJHhTnmoFtsvH7EWIMRWnW8_vqQnwXpb-992XgOwAA___89407), and Ukraine's Starlink access. Musk has spent some $474 million backing Republicans this cycle. Asked about talk of arresting him, Trump said, _" It's talk. But if it is talk, we'll have to protect them."_ Pardons cover only federal crimes, leaving state prosecutions, civil suits, and impeachment untouched.

body:

**Forward Party CEO Looks Back on Progress for Independent Movement on Election Day 2026** ******_Washington D.C. – November 3, 2026_** _–_ “The Forward Party is thrilled to have arrived at yet another important mile marker in our work of growing the Independent political movement on Election Day 2026. Forward candidates, affiliates, state campaign leaders, volunteers, and our national staff have so much to celebrate as we await poll results across the country. “This year, the Forward Party has continued to establish itself as a bona fide political party, building the infrastructure necessary to support candidates with voter engagement activities, door-knocking, technology, and our most precious political resource of staff and volunteers who power the work we do. “Forward Party is proud to support 31 official Forward Party candidates on the ballot this November, along with 23 federal endorsed candidates, 12 endorsed statewide candidates, 72 state legislative candidates and 69 local or county candidates totaling 176 across the country. We’re also thrilled to have over 254,000 supporters and over 25,500 volunteers who understand and believe in the mission of bringing moderates, conservatives, and progressives together to find shared ground for better solutions for the American people. “With several consequential races in play today, the Forward Party remains resolute in our work to bring constructive, consensus-based governance back into fashion at the local, state and federal level. The American people are facing a critical number of material issues that all deserve legislative attention and action. This recent era of political divisiveness and power hoarding, exacerbated by legacy party purity tests, must come to an end. We believe empowering and electing Independent candidates will pull legacy American political parties away from the political fringes, back toward constructive dialogue, in primary service to their constituents, not party bosses. “We are honored to be tasked with such an important role of helping guide our collective path back to consensus governance, and to those who support our work. We are eager about our next steps as an Independent political party, and for the Independent movement as a whole.”
---

body:
If we don't show up today, we lose...

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/19nVBfujecF?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
| | | | | | Peter,

**It all comes down to today...

** Polls are opening across New Hampshire, and this election will determine who represents our Live Free or Die State in Concord.

**Every vote matters** , and some races can come down to just a handful of votes.

**Do not sit this one out and let someone else decide what is best for you, your family, and your wallet.**

Get to the polls today and vote for the candidates who will stand up for your liberty!

Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire has put together a list of **155 liberty champions** who have signed The Pledge and committed to fighting for you.
[**Click here to take a look at the full list and make sure you know who is on your ballot.**](https://us.list-manage.com/EJWDaf3U7SR?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Q1OrAU_3ZZt?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
| | **Once you cast your ballot, help get others to the polls!**

Start a group chat.

Text your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers.

**Remind them that today is Election Day and encourage them to make their voices heard.**

Share our [list of endorsed candidates](https://us.list-manage.com/t7jgmE1isaJ?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70) so they can see who has committed to fighting for our values.

If we want real representation in Concord that works for us, we have to make our voices heard today. That starts with showing up.

[Find your polling location and voting hours here](https://us.list-manage.com/6noYveccqa3?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70).

If we don’t show up today, we lose...

LET’S WIN!

If you walk into my family's restaurant in Manchester on any given afternoon, you'll hear the same sounds I've heard my entire life: the clinking of coffee mugs, the hum of blenders, and the rhythm of neighbors talking in a booth. **It 's the sound of New Hampshire -- and the community that shaped me.**
My great-grandfather started his business 109 years ago. He was a Greek immigrant who didn't have much, but he believed that if you worked hard, treated people right, and gave back to your community, this country would give you a fair shot.
Long before I served in Congress, I was in the kitchen at the restaurant making homemade ice cream. In a year we'd churn out more than 35,000 gallons of it!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b36ee53c-9ebf-4b0d-861c-39161bf3f320?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Helping run my family's small business showed me the power of hard work and serving others.
But unfortunately the opportunity that my ancestors and others sought has never been further away, and Donald Trump and his administration are too busy cutting deals for their billionaire buddies to give a damn.
**I decided to run for Senate to change that.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b36ee53c-9ebf-4b0d-861c-39161bf3f320?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I've traveled across the Granite State on the campaign trail -- from the Seacoast to the North Country -- and the stories I hear are the same: People are working harder than ever and doing everything right but still seem to be falling behind.
The system isn't working. More often than not, it feels rigged for those at the top -- while the rest of us are just trying to scrape by.
**That 's why I'm running for Senate:** We deserve leaders who fight for all of us, not just the wealthy and well-connected. And it's about time that our economy works for everyone.
_I 'm also running to bring a new voice to the Senate and stand up for all Granite Staters._
Growing up in New Hampshire, I often wondered if there would be a place for me here -- if I'd be able to live openly and authentically in the state I love. I certainly never imagined I could one day be elected to public office as a member of the LGBTQ+ community.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b36ee53c-9ebf-4b0d-861c-39161bf3f320?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
After college I returned home to help run my family's restaurant and decided to run for the state legislature because I wanted to give back to the city and state that had given me so many opportunities.
And somewhat to my surprise, not only did my community accept me, they gave me their trust and sent me to Concord to serve them.
I'll never forget the first speech I made from the State House floor. At the time marriage equality was far from the law of the land, and the legislature was debating a bill that would have prohibited New Hampshire from recognizing same-sex marriages performed in other states.
I told my colleagues that the bill ran counter to the "Live Free or Die" spirit we're so proud of in New Hampshire and that we shouldn't be legislating based on fear or hate or trying to punish people for who they love.
Unfortunately the bill passed, and we lost that fight. _But we didn 't give up._
We persevered, and not long after the legislature passed a new bill recognizing civil unions between same-sex partners. And a few years after that, New Hampshire became the first state in the nation to legalize marriage equality through legislative action.
It was a remarkable turnaround that showed real progress is possible, and that's made an immeasurable difference in the lives of so many who call New Hampshire home - including my husband and me.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b36ee53c-9ebf-4b0d-861c-39161bf3f320?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**I 'm not running to make history -- I'm running to make a difference for every Granite Stater who feels like their voice isn't being heard by those who represent them.**
During this campaign the contrast between me and my opponent, John Sununu, has only grown stronger.
I've spent my time in Congress taking on tough fights. I'm ranked one of the most bipartisan members of the House because I'll always look for a chance to deliver results. But I'll also take on anyone to do what's best for New Hampshire -- regardless of political party.
_We 're seeing a different approach from Sununu and the Republican side._
The GOP sows extreme rhetoric and threatens our fundamental freedoms -- from attacks on reproductive rights to a Trump Administration that's more focused on helping billionaire insiders than lowering costs for families here in New Hampshire.
**We can 't go backward.**
I've beaten their dangerous agenda before. When I first ran for Congress in 2018, people said a Democrat couldn't hold a district like ours for more than a single term. We proved them wrong by staying grounded in our values.
Every day on the campaign trail, I feel that same momentum.
I see it in the seniors who pull me aside to talk about prescription drug costs, and I see it in the young people showing up to No Kings Rallies and getting involved in politics for the first time.
All of our work from the last 18 months has led up to this moment. Whether you knocked doors, made phone calls, chipped in what you could, or just shared our campaign's message with a friend, you've made an impact in this race. This grassroots team got us this far, and we're inches away from the finish line.
**I 'm ready for the work ahead. I'm ready for the big fights. And I'm ready to be a Senator who always has your back.**
Thank you for reading,
Chris
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b36ee53c-9ebf-4b0d-861c-39161bf3f320?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The GOP sows extreme rhetoric and threatens our fundamental freedoms -- from attacks on reproductive rights to a Trump Administration that's more focused on helping billionaire insiders than lowering costs for families here in New Hampshire. We can 't go backward. I've beaten their dangerous agenda before. When I first ran for Congress in 2018, people said a Democrat couldn't hold a district like ours for more than a single term. We proved them wrong by staying grounded in our values. Every day on the campaign trail, I feel that same momentum. I see it in the seniors who pull me aside to talk about prescription drug costs, and I see it in the young people showing up to No Kings Rallies and getting involved in politics for the first time. All of our work from the last 18 months has led up to this moment. Whether you knocked doors, made phone calls, chipped in what you could, or just shared our campaign's message with a friend, you've made an impact in this race. This grassroots team got us this far, and we're inches away from the finish line. I 'm ready for the work ahead. I'm ready for the big fights. And I'm ready to be a Senator who always has your back. Thank you for reading, Chris | | ---|---|--- P.S. We need every single Granite State voter to turn out and make their voice heard at the polls today. Head to to find your polling place, and remind your friends and family to vote, too! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Chris Pappas PO Box 313, Manchester, NH 03105 ? ?

| | [Heartland Journal ®](https://substack.com/@heartlandjournal)
