In Washington State, the return envelope comes with the postage prepaid. The voter signs, licks nothing, and trusts. What nobody prepays -- not the voter, not the state, not Congress -- is the solvency of the carrier. The ballot is paid for. The Post Office isn't. And every federal election now depends on the difference.
Start with the wound, because it was self-inflicted and dated. In December 2006, a lame-duck Congress passed the Postal Accountability and Enhancement Act, ordering the Postal Service -- in the words of its own annual report, "unlike any other public or private entity" -- to prepay seventy-five years of retiree health benefits in ten annual installments of $5.4 to $5.8 billion. No company on earth keeps books this way. The Service paid until it couldn't, defaulted in 2011, defaulted again, and kept defaulting until Congress repealed the mandate in 2022 -- after the ledger was already ruined (Tax Foundation; USPS annual reports).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/23da6f7a-94b4-4704-a15e-f3754339f593?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then the disease. First-Class Mail -- the profitable class, letters and bills -- peaked at 103.6 billion pieces in 2001 and has slid ever since: from 92 billion in 2008 to 46 billion in 2023, a fifty percent collapse (USPS Inspector General). Total mail peaked at 213 billion in 2006; the IG projects 71 billion by 2035. The 2025 loss: $9 billion. Email and online bill pay did this, and nobody subpoenaed them.
Then, onto the wounded carrier, the federal load. The National Voter Registration Act of 1993 made the mail the front door of registration; UOCAVA guaranteed soldiers their ballots; HAVA added the paperwork. Then came the Washington model: Oregon went all-mail in 2000, Washington finished its last county in 2013, and today eight states mail a ballot to every voter -- 84 percent of voters across Alaska, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, and Washington got theirs by mail in the last federal election (Sightline Institute). Federal law makes official election mail postage-free; states like Washington prepay the return envelope by statute (RCW 29A.40.091). And on August 14, 2020, the Postal Service sent letters to 46 states and the District of Columbia warning it could not guarantee ballots would arrive in time to be counted. Judges in Pennsylvania and a handful of other states extended receipt deadlines that fall -- the courts scrambling to stay ahead of the mailroom.
Here is the vulnerability, and it is not the fraud the cable networks argue about. It is arithmetic. A ballot is First-Class Mail -- the very class email ate -- riding a network cut to match a shrinking forecast, governed by one law that treats it as infrastructure and another that treats the Service as a business required to prepay a century. Article I, Section 8 built the post roads. Article I, Section 4 wrote the election rules. The two clauses have never met.
To survive, the carrier outsourced what it could. Air cargo went to FedEx for two decades at nearly $2 billion a year, then bounced to UPS in April 2024, mid-election-cycle (Reuters). From 2003 to 2009, the Service sorted and delivered the domestic parcels of DHL -- owned by Germany's Deutsche Post -- while the parent bled in America, $1.5 billion in 2008 alone, nearly $10 billion all told, then walked out in 2009 and tendered its remaining American packages to the Postal Service for final-mile delivery. The German company's exit cost was subsidized by the American public's postage monopoly. Then Amazon: the 2013 Sunday-delivery deal had USPS carrying boxes at rates Citigroup's analysts put roughly $1.46 a package below cost. The discount helped build the machine that emptied the malls that emptied the catalogs that filled the mail. Last year the Service delivered 1.7 billion packages for Amazon; this year the Wall Street Journal reports the company wanted to cut its postal volume by two-thirds as the contract came up, before an April renegotiation kept most of it -- while the stamp rises from 78 cents to 95. The Post Office built its biggest customer's moat at a loss, and the customer is circling the exits the same fall the ballots are stacked in the trays.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1cfe211a-d3c9-4ac0-a244-597a2fa937ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As for the staff: the documented version is uglier than the rumor and quieter. USPS hires citizens and green-card holders; nobody has shown a below-minimum-wage undocumented workforce inside the Service itself. What the record shows is the layer behind it -- highway contract routes, sortation subcontractors, temp-agency margins -- where the Service Contract Act sets the floor and the Postal Service's own contract clauses contemplate "underpaid employees," authorizing the Labor Department to withhold contract sums and pay them directly (DOL Fact Sheet 67C; USPS purchasing manual). A first-class institution running on second-class labor, with the difference booked somewhere in the lowest bid.
And that is why the federal elections did the most damage. A school board can be decided at the kitchen table; a presidency is decided in a few states by margins smaller than a sorting plant's daily output, and only one carrier can reach every doorstep in all of them. Washington works -- prepaid, fitted, counted early -- because a state can pay attention to one envelope. A federal election cannot pay attention to 155 million. The local system depends on the federal one; the federal one depends on a corporation Congress chose to bankrupt by statute in 2006 and to mourn by repeal in 2022.
Who decided? A conference committee at midnight in December 2006. A billion thumbs trading stamps for screens. A memo in Bonn. A pricing desk in Seattle. The ballot was prepaid. The carrier wasn't -- and "insufficient funds" is what the machine prints when a decision is made everywhere and signed by no one. Congress, if it wants its mail back, knows the return address: Article I.
Here's the ledger, by fiscal year (net loss under GAAP, per USPS annual reports):
| FY | Net loss | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 2018 | $3.9B | |
| 2019 | $8.8B | Jump of $4.9B; workers' comp discount-rate swings |
| 2020 | $9.2B | COVID cost surge |
| 2021 | $9.7B | Worst of the decade |
| 2022 | $1.4B | Distorted by the Postal Service Reform Act's one-time ~$56B gain (retiree health + pension liabilities shifted to Treasury); loss from operations was ~$950M |
| 2023 | $6.5B | |
| 2024 | $9.5B | Includes $2.2B workers' comp non-cash hit |
| 2025 | $9.0B | Delivered 3.7B fewer mail pieces; revenue up just $916M |
Total FY2018-FY2025: roughly $58-59 billion. (The PRC counts the cumulative deficit at $32.6 billion as of FY2024, offsetting $48.8B of accumulated losses against $16.1B in capital contributions.)
A couple of things worth flagging:
\- Every year loses, but the headline number is dominated by non-cash items -- workers' comp actuarial swings, CSRS/FERS unfunded-liability amortization (roughly $5.3-5.5B/yr combined in 2024-25). The "controllable loss" management reports is much smaller: $3.4B (2019), $1.8B (2024), $2.7B (2025). Brookings frames it the way your piece does: reported losses reflect "legacy obligations externally governed and funded from operating revenue" -- not just the economics of the mail.
\- GAO's line for the 2026 piece: USPS "has lost money every fiscal year but one since 2007" -- and the one exception (FY2022) only exists because Congress moved the liabilities off the books.
\- First quarter of FY2026: another $1.26B net loss, plus a new "retiree health benefits top-up" line item appearing -- the PSRA fix isn't holding.
Since the 2006 prefunding law took its first bites, the Service has lost money every year but one -- and the one profitable year was profitable because Congress finally paid a bill it had spent sixteen years forcing USPS to pay alone.

name: OnePA Team
subject: Our communities deserve a say in who holds power
body:
Find your polling place, get help with a ride, and keep these voter protection numbers handy. | |
---
Peter, **Today is Election Day, and we’re bringing the power of our communities to the ballot box.** Every conversation with a neighbor, every door knocked, and every person we help get to the polls builds our collective voice in the decisions that shape our lives. We organize because our families deserve affordable homes, strong public schools, clean air, and wages that cover the bills. Today, we have an opportunity to elect leaders who will fight alongside us for those demands. **Corporations and billionaires pour money into elections to put their interests first. Our power grows when working people turn out together and demand a government accountable to our communities.** If you haven’t voted yet, make time today. clean_body: Find your polling place, get help with a ride, and keep these voter protection numbers handy. | | Peter, Today is Election Day, and we’re bringing the power of our communities to the ballot box. Every conversation with a neighbor, every door knocked, and every person we help get to the polls builds our collective voice in the decisions that shape our lives. We organize because our families deserve affordable homes, strong public schools, clean air, and wages that cover the bills. Today, we have an opportunity to elect leaders who will fight alongside us for those demands. Corporations and billionaires pour money into elections to put their interests first. Our power grows when working people turn out together and demand a government accountable to our communities. If you haven’t voted yet, make time today. Check your polling location, figure out how you’re getting there, and reach out to someone who could use a reminder or a ride. Find your polling place and make your voice heard today. | | Need a ride to the polls? If you encounter trouble voting or have questions about your rights, contact Election Protection for help: English: 866-OUR-VOTE (866-687-8683) Spanish: 888-VE-Y-VOTA (888-839-8682) Arabic: 844-YALLA-US (844-925-5287) Mandarin, Cantonese, Korean, Vietnamese, Tagalog, Urdu, Hindi, Bengali/Bangla, and Punjabi: 888-API-VOTE (888-274-8683) Save these numbers before you head out, and share them with your family, friends, and neighbors. Hi friend, it’s Deb. Before polls close here in __ New Mexico, I want to take a moment to say thank you for your support.
I launched this campaign 630 days ago, and from day one, people across New Mexico have stepped up, stood together, and fought alongside me for a brighter future for our state. **None of this would have been possible without you.**
Together, we built a one-of-a-kind, history-making campaign. We turned out thousands of new voters, brought our message to every corner of the fifth-largest state in the country, and showed what’s possible when people come together around a shared vision for their home.
We sent a message loud and clear: **New Mexico is worth fighting for. Our families are worth fighting for. And every single New Mexican deserves a future full of opportunity.**
I will never take for granted the people who made this campaign what it is. Thank you for standing with me, believing in this vision, and reminding me every day why this fight matters.

Good morning, North Carolina! Today is Election Day and in about 12 hours, the polls will close across the state. This is our chance to change the direction we've been heading in. And this morning, I'm thinking about why so many of you stepped up to get us here.
Too often, North Carolinians have been left to bear the brunt of decisions out of Washington that hurt their families: reckless wars abroad, health care that costs too much and prices at the grocery store and gas pump that keep climbing. And still, North Carolinians don't give up. From the mountains to the coast, we find a way forward together.
I've seen so many North Carolinians work hard, look out for their neighbors and keep going when it's so easy to do otherwise. That's what stepping up looks like.
Some of you have been with me since my days as Governor, and some of you joined this fight a few months ago. Whenever you came aboard, I am grateful for and encouraged by every one of you. You have helped build something amazing.
Take a moment to look back on the last 15 months. Think about all of the phone calls, doors knocked on and donations that came from people who didn't have much extra to give. Every one of you made this possible.
When we started this campaign, I knew it would be the toughest race of my life. But I believe it's time North Carolina had a Senator who pays attention to working families and who puts the focus on people who've started to believe the American dream is out of reach.
I don't believe it is. I never have.
I've said many times I'm a prisoner of hope. I truly believe our best days are ahead of us, if we work toward it. It's why I've spent the last 15 months on the campaign trail. Every canvass launch, front porch conversation and community event has reminded me what this work is about, and your support has made me more hopeful with every mile.
Everything we've worked for has led to this final movement.
**If you haven 't voted yet, and you're already registered to vote, you can find your Election Day polling place [here](https://substack.com/redirect/db422ab5-b494-4fc9-94a9-f5e58744b682?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Please make a plan to vote, and bring a friend with you.
Then reach out to the people in your life. Text your family, check in on your neighbors and remind your community that their vote matters and that time is running out.
You've helped build something amazing, and together, we're going to flip North Carolina blue.
Let's finish this strong.
Roy

P.S. Anyone in line to vote at 7:30 PM will be able to vote. If you are in line when polls close at 7:30 PM, stay in line!

clean_body: Good morning, North Carolina! | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Nov 3 | | | | | | | | | | | | Good morning, North Carolina! Today is Election Day and in about 12 hours, the polls will close across the state. This is our chance to change the direction we've been heading in. And this morning, I'm thinking about why so many of you stepped up to get us here. Too often, North Carolinians have been left to bear the brunt of decisions out of Washington that hurt their families: reckless wars abroad, health care that costs too much and prices at the grocery store and gas pump that keep climbing. And still, North Carolinians don't give up. From the mountains to the coast, we find a way forward together. I've seen so many North Carolinians work hard, look out for their neighbors and keep going when it's so easy to do otherwise. That's what stepping up looks like. Some of you have been with me since my days as Governor, and some of you joined this fight a few months ago. Whenever you came aboard, I am grateful for and encouraged by every one of you. You have helped build something amazing. Take a moment to look back on the last 15 months. Think about all of the phone calls, doors knocked on and donations that came from people who didn't have much extra to give. Every one of you made this possible. When we started this campaign, I knew it would be the toughest race of my life. But I believe it's time North Carolina had a Senator who pays attention to working families and who puts the focus on people who've started to believe the American dream is out of reach. I don't believe it is. I never have. I've said many times I'm a prisoner of hope. I truly believe our best days are ahead of us, if we work toward it. It's why I've spent the last 15 months on the campaign trail. Every canvass launch, front porch conversation and community event has reminded me what this work is about, and your support has made me more hopeful with every mile. Everything we've worked for has led to this final movement. If you haven 't voted yet, and you're already registered to vote, you can find your Election Day polling place . Please make a plan to vote, and bring a friend with you. Then reach out to the people in your life. Text your family, check in on your neighbors and remind your community that their vote matters and that time is running out. You've helped build something amazing, and together, we're going to flip North Carolina blue. Let's finish this strong. Roy P.S. Anyone in line to vote at 7:30 PM will be able to vote. If you are in line when polls close at 7:30 PM, stay in line! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Roy Cooper PO Box 1190, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.
Upcoming events
As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Pittsburgh%20School%20board%20forum%208.5x11.png]
Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students.
Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader.
With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color.

Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. [https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/7237344C447445787878394747342B75584E47375A57552F745265427662334B544A4A36505A58657A5871474B7A5A6E53705571424758325657365969365747/editor_images/WCM%20logo.JPG] #CourtsMatter
This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/DelCo_2.png] We are hiring!
Let's provide civic education together!
We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania.
Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote!
Positions start at $20 an hour.
Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org]
EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org]
News You Can Use
There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
* New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pittsburgh-mayor-election-2025-candidates-quiz]

2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:
Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [https://penncapital-star.com/briefs/advocacy-groups-offer-training-for-pa-primary-poll-watchers/]
Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide/]
Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [https://fcfreepresspa.com/poll-workers-needed-for-pennsylvanias-2025-primary-election/]
6. Engage Your Elected Officials
Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise.
7. Vote in Every Election
Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility.
Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th!

clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed. The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error. Upcoming events As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls. [] Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students. Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader. With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color. When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] [] Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot. Your vote shapes our justice system! In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. # [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3248%2E5691347%2E6Dvl13)

Peter,
Do you remember this?
[](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261103-2-f&utm_campaign=em261103-2-f&t=2&akid=3248%2E5691347%2E6Dvl13)
In 2020, the pundits said flipping a Republican Senate seat in Georgia couldn’t be done. But we built one of the strongest voter mobilization programs in Senate campaign history — and alongside Rev. Warnock, **we won.** That victory won the Senate majority.
Now, the eyes of the nation are once again turned toward Georgia. And we _must_ win again. The future of our Republic depends on it.
_And just like last time, I can’t do it alone. It’s going to take ALL of us._
**So I’m asking for your help again, Peter:**
[**Will you please make a contribution to my reelection campaign today, of $5 or any amount that works for you?**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-nov26.ijcilw&refcode=em261103-2-f&utm_campaign=em261103-2-f&amount=5&t=3&akid=3248%2E5691347%2E6Dvl13)
2026 is our only hope to recover Congressional power and reverse our descent toward one-man rule.
And here in Georgia, I’m the only Democratic U.S. Senator running for reelection in a state Trump won.

body:

# Conforti Grassroots Newsletter
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

**A Message From Niki Conforti:**.Today is the day, and the future of Illinois’ 6th Congressional District is officially in your hands. As we reach the finish line on this November 3rd Election Day, I am urging every single resident who has not yet cast a ballot to head to the polls today and make your voice heard. For far too long, hardworking families in Cook and DuPage counties have been forced to deplete their savings just to get by under the failed, tax-and-spend policies of incumbent Sean Casten. We cannot afford another term of partisan messaging and appeasing special interests while our utility bills, grocery costs, and taxes skyrocket. If you haven’t already voted early or by mail, please take the time today to go to your local polling place, bring your friends and neighbors, and vote for sensible, common-sense leadership that puts our community first..From the bottom of my heart, thank you for the incredible support, energy, and grassroots momentum you have poured into this campaign from day one. Whether you displayed a yard sign on your lawn, walked alongside our team in summer parades, or simply took a moment to talk at your doorstep, your dedication has been the driving force behind everything we have built. Having lived in the 6th District for the majority of my life, I have always known how resilient and hardworking our neighborhoods are, and standing shoulder-to-shoulder with you throughout this race has been the honor of a lifetime..With your support, I am ready to take a strict "district-first" mentality to Washington, D.C., and immediately get to work bending the cost curve for Illinois families. Drawing on my professional background as an energy consultant and a former healthcare executive for twelve years, I will fight to cut burdensome energy regulations in favor of "speed to power" to lower your utility bills, and enforce strict medical billing transparency to foster competition and drive down healthcare costs. Furthermore, I will push for statutory federal spending caps to rein in the runaway national debt and stop tax hikes, incentivize the return of manufacturing and good-paying jobs to the 6th District, secure our southern border while fully backing our local police, and fiercely protect parental rights and fair play for female athletes under Title IX. Together, we will restore accountability to Congress—and after the polls close tonight, I hope to see you at our Official Election Night Watch Party at Salerno’s Pizzeria & Sports Bar in Hodgkins at 6:30 PM as we celebrate our shared vision for the 6th District!
---
| |
---
| |
### District-First Movement.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## Celebrating America’s 250th Birthday Across the District

## (May – July 2026)

---
| |
Walking alongside hundreds of supporters, veterans, and families during our local summer parades was an unforgettable highlight of this cycle. From kicking off the season at the 108th Elmhurst Memorial Day Parade and gathering at the Veterans Memorial in Wilder Park, to celebrating the 250th anniversary of the United States at the Garfield Ridge, Oak Lawn, Villa Park ("Stars, Stripes, and 250 Lights"), and Downers Grove Independence Day parades, the patriotic spirit and warmth of our communities were on full display.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
# Grassroots Conversations Over Coffee
---
| | **(June – August 2026)**
---
| | Some of the most meaningful moments of the campaign happened face-to-face with neighbors discussing real kitchen-table issues. Grabbing one-on-one conversations during "Coffee with Niki" at Krema Coffee in Tinley Park, and diving into solutions for skyrocketing utility bills at the Elmhurst American Legion energy forum reminded us daily why our "district-first" mission matters so much.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
# Momentum in Lombard & Autumn in Palos Park
---
| | **(August – September 2026)**
---
| |

As the campaign shifted into high gear, the energy at our August reception in Lombard with special guest Congressman Darin LaHood showed just how united Illinoisans are in fighting for fiscal responsibility. Shortly after, marching down 123rd Street with our dedicated volunteers at the Palos Park Autumn In The Park Festival Parade and meeting voters at the Oak Lawn VFW with the Worth Township Republican Organization gave our team the exact surge of momentum needed to carry us through to Election Day.

| | Friend,

**The polls are open.** After everything, it all comes down to today. Today, the voters of Wisconsin get the final word.

This is the moment we built for. To this one day, when the people, and _not the powerful_ , decide the future of our democracy.

So here is what I am asking of you. **Go vote.**
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/fBCzWeY6jj5?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

| The polls are open until 8 PM tonight. Find your polling place at [votejocasta.com/vote](https://us.list-manage.com/WK7q74izhsG?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7). When you get there, vote JoCasta Zamarripa for Secretary of State, and vote all the way up and down the ballot.

And then do one more thing. Bring someone with you. Call your family, text your friends, offer a neighbor a ride. Movements are not won by one vote. They are won by all of us, together, refusing to sit this out.
---
| Let's win this,

JoCasta Zamarripa
Democratic Nominee for Wisconsin Secretary of State
---
| | | | JoCasta Zamarripa is a lifelong Milwaukeean, a proud daughter of the city’s south side, and a dedicated public servant who’s never stopped fighting for working people. Born and raised in the very neighborhoods she now represents, JoCasta has spent her life pushing for progress that reflects the realities of everyday Wisconsinites.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/JQzsOBT7jZV?e=8d919f2092&c2id=0bdcb6d83cbc8b2aaf05afb952b88bb7)

She made history as the first Latina and first openly bi member of both the Wisconsin State Legislature and the Milwaukee Common Council. But JoCasta’s leadership is defined by more than her historic firsts—it's grounded in results. She served ten years in the State Assembly and is now in her second term as Alderperson for Milwaukee’s 8th District, where she’s led major efforts on affordable housing, small business licensing reform, and community development.

In 2025, she was the lead sponsor of the Housing Element Plan, a key step in addressing Milwaukee’s housing crisis by expanding affordable options and preventing displacement. Her approach is practical and persistent—building coalitions, navigating political challenges, and staying rooted in the neighborhoods she serves.

Now, JoCasta is running as a Democrat for Wisconsin Secretary of State to use the platform to fight for what matters: more funding for our schools so families aren’t forced into referenda every election, real housing relief for working people, and affordable child care that lets parents breathe.

| | Dear Fellow American, **Hillsdale College can reach and teach all of America for liberty because of people like you.** People **_like you_** who understand the importance of liberty. People **_like you_** who know that freedom requires sacrifice. People **_like you_** who love this country. And because of you, this June, we released _Revolutionary America_ to teach the true history of America’s founding to all who are willing to learn. Perhaps you saw it in theaters or on our website? But I have exciting news for you... **The free “Revolutionary America” online course is available now, and I want you to watch it today.** **Sign up for FREE at the secure link below:** **[https://info.hillsdale.edu/revolutionary-america-sign-up](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckcuq2zAQhp9G3tno5tvCi1I79NCTk1NCKV0ZRRo7A7JkdEnJ25dA8gJnO_Mxw__9f47zUaFFt36oDQaMcTbezHefwxIA1owGkk9XUBsE1GrmlDclYyUVs9IJbzBLVZih5qxbugIG1vaiZbRvZXEdoL6wS88kg75upDaskZeFMrVQ1rSXpStweNxjjAomKK9lJZqW0toI2bKuXvqaSJp3oxJU6CIaiNr7ffcWE-pY-bAWdrimtEcivhF-IPyAbvHVFa2NRlmowGTCDwFu3uaE3qlwL59ZyoirK_NOxCHCuoFL370BIkbKOyE-KJf82P8YT-M0nQlvctrm6HPQD2QPPu6gE7r1udrAYN6IGGFTaJ9DrbZd4eqIGAPc5pdE43WOEBDii_MugUtEjJ_T6fN9en_7Of09_Z5_teXb-Vy-JBVhMPs_tBZj0xJJ18erSvutSF-t7jbw_wEAAP__d9Cqyg)** The course includes never-before-seen interviews with the same professors and opinion leaders featured in the documentary. I hope you enjoy learning about our great country! Warm regards,Bill Gray ’01
Vice President

Peter, A lot of people are heading to the polls today. Whatever happens tonight, here’s something worth remembering. Your 2026 tax bill is going to come down to what you do in the next 58 days. Not Congress. **You.** Most people feel like taxes just happen to them. The W-2 shows up, the forms get filed, the check gets written, and you get back to work. It feels like there’s nothing you can do about it. But you’ve got more say than you think. You just have to use it before December 31. **If you do nothing between now and the end of the year:** You’ll pay whatever your tax return says you owe.
You’ll miss the deductions and strategies you never knew about.
And you’ll find out in April, when it’s too late to change a thing. **If you sit down with us before the year ends:** You’ll know exactly where you stand.
You’ll know which moves make sense for your situation and which don’t.
And you’ll have a clear plan to keep more of your money where it belongs. With your family. Bill Spadea recommends Tru-Fit for exactly this reason. [Book a complimentary game plan call with our team.](https://xtz223.keap-link008.com/v2/click/064f8ef4ce8f7968c61f338e168e3cfc/eJyNkMtqwzAQRf9l1lb9SnDsnQkhGCdZlHZdhKy0orIkpFGIG_zvHZc2qxa6vTo6lzs3QGm4wW6ABq74URQlJOClUE5Jg1trkIuv12K9yss8Aa3M-97b6KC5_fr5Dixxnm2qTQI4OUnM02O77bvT_uXQnXpCHfdU8i9RnVXZ3bM7tt0B5vlPsRwV7i7kDtCgj3KZNCiahc9eE_-G6EKTpoJraQY9PQg7pnhGfnWaG6PMazrZ6JmIAe3IKGeBXygOjM6hrGELR0XcORJ8n6mX00-dCiHKoaVteVWXVVFn5Wr-BFxOeJsBnhDoxH-qQjTH7I7pwbd8gg==) In 30 minutes, we’ll look at your real numbers and show you where you’re overpaying and what to do about it while there’s still time. body:
A final message from Brad Smith. Thank you for everything you've done. Today, let's finish what we started.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/0be7f1601f8c/officially-on-the-ballot-and-building-momentum-every-day-17461981?e=a4a0e00aa9)
---
| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
Hi Peter,

Today is Election Day, and polls are now open!
When I started this campaign, I never imagined the incredible support, dedication, and energy we would build together. Every door knocked, every dollar donated, and every conversation has brought us to this moment. I am deeply grateful to everyone who has been part of this journey.
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZxyBqLocBoK?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8)
| | Now, after months of hard work, it all comes down to one powerful action. **VOTE.**
**We can't expect change if we don't make one.**
If you live in Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District, I'm asking for your vote today, November 3. Make a plan, find your polling location, and make your voice heard.
**Find your polling location:**
[https://myvote.wi.gov/en-us/Find-My-Polling-Place](https://us.list-manage.com/1C_7tXT82KB?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8)
Polls are open until **8:00 p.m.** , and our work isn't finished until they close.
No matter the outcome, I am incredibly proud of what we've built together. Thank you for believing in this campaign, standing alongside me, and showing what's possible when we come together for our communities.
**Let's finish what we started.**

| Peter, It's finally Election Day, Peter. Everything we've built together in Louisiana will be put to test.
When the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act in Louisiana v. Callais and eliminated one of our majority-Black Democratic Districts, hundreds of thousands of Democrats from across the country rallied to our aid and picked our party up when it was at its lowest.
It gave us a spark of hope and a lift we so desperately needed. And the impact was immediately felt.
We built the largest organizing operation this state has ever seen, launched a statewide tour rallying voters in all 64 parishes, and set out to do what the experts said was impossible: flip Louisiana's U.S. Senate seat blue.

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell Fry Trump Endorsed U.S. Congressman SC-07 | | | == | | | Meet Russell: Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. Hey everybody, I wanted to share this video with you now that polls are open here in Ohio.
To Martin Sheen, thanks for helping us pull it off.
To you, thanks for believing in me and our message for Ohio, and fighting for it until the end.
-Sherrod
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9a5d0b34-541d-4f40-bc58-aa0c7c3f19cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
> _It 's always been Ohio against the world._
> _This Election Day, that 's never been more true._
> _Ohioans are tough, and when people count us out, we always prove them wrong._
> _From pioneers of the skies to travelers of the stars, Ohio is the birthplace of dreamers and doers - those devoted to something bigger than themselves._
> _We work hard, and when we 've given all we can, we push a little more._
> _We know nothing worth having is given. It must be earned._
> _But billionaires consumed by greed and corruption take and take and take, thinking we won 't fight back._
> _So you see, it still is Ohio against the world._
> _We 're standing up to billionaires and corporations, instead of standing with them._
> _We 're demanding a leader who takes on corruption._
> _And when the votes are counted, the message will be clear:_
> _When Ohio shows up to fight, we never back down._
* * *
Before you click away!
Our resources are zeroed out. We've allocated every dollar that came in the door to reach voters before polls close tonight. That means our accounts will be empty (or maybe even a little in the red). That's on purpose. **But it 's also taking a big risk.**
If the result is too close to call and Sherrod's fight continues beyond tonight, we won't have the resources we need to wage it. Outside groups have shown they're willing to spend ungodly sums to buy this seat. We can only expect they'll do the same with Senate control still on the line.

When I launched this campaign over a year ago -- almost no one gave us a chance.
I was a state representative most of Texas had never heard of, going up against a three-term governor with a lot of money in the bank. The early polls had us down 10 points. We got written off by _almost_ everyone.
Now, we've wiped out that entire 10-point deficit, and today we are leading Greg Abbott in multiple polls.
This has become one of the strongest, most competitive campaigns in the whole country.
**And today, we have the opportunity to do what so many people thought was impossible: elect a new governor and chart a better future for Texas.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02a7f50e-fbe6-4065-bb09-8f243190c8a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The outcome of today's election is the culmination of everything we've worked for.
Grassroots supporters like you are the reason we're in this position, and you're the reason we can finish the job and win this race.
Every ad we ran, every text we sent, and every door we knocked to get our message out only matters if we can get people to the polls today.
**So I 'm asking you to do one more thing: Get out and vote if you haven't already. Remind your friends, your family, and your neighbors now is the time for them to make their voices heard. Polls are open until 7 P.M. and you can find your polling location at [IWillVote.com/TX](https://substack.com/redirect/c281ce10-87be-4ed7-b289-9b16bcab9739?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
I'm running to save Texas schools, put money in your pocket, and end the Greg Abbott Corruption Tax that has meant we pay more while we get less.
**And after everything we 've accomplished together, I believe more than ever that a Texas where we can secure the American Dream is within our reach. One where working families come first, our public schools have the resources they need, and our government works for the people it serves.**
This race is ours to win. We're closer than almost anyone thought we'd be. **Now it 's time to turn that hope into votes and show the country what's possible when Texans come together.**
Let's finish this and take Texas back.
Thank you,
Gina
**P.S.[We're still mobilizing voters. If you can, please make a donation of $10 or more right now to help us get one final surge in grassroots support to get out the vote.](https://substack.com/redirect/71f07b82-d306-4d4d-87fa-1d673b6f0d3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

body:

| | Hello Peter,

Today is the day! After months of door-knocking, phone calls, conversations, and community gatherings, it all comes down to this: **Tuesday, November 3, is Election Day.** Polls are open from **6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.** , and if you’re in line by 7:30, you have the right to vote.
Thank you to every one of you who has given your time, your donations, and your belief in a better future for Ohio’s 8th District. Now let’s finish strong together.
**⚠️ Important: If You Have an Absentee Ballot, Do Not Mail It Today**
Ohio’s election law has changed, and there is no longer a grace period for mailed ballots. **Your absentee ballot must arrive at your county Board of Elections by 7:30 p.m. tonight to be counted.** A ballot mailed today will almost certainly arrive too late.
If you still have your absentee ballot:
* **Hand-deliver it to your county Board of Elections office** (or its official drop box) **before 7:30 p.m. today.**
* **Do not take it to your polling place.** Absentee ballots must go to the Board of Elections.
* Make sure the ID envelope is completed and signed.
* You can check your ballot status at **VoteOhio.gov**.

Please forward this to friends and family who voted by mail. One forwarded message could save someone’s vote.
**Vote the Entire Democratic Slate — Top to Bottom** Every race on your ballot matters. The people we elect today shape our schools, our roads, our courts, and our economic future. Please vote for the entire Democratic slate. Your ballot will show only the races for your own district.
**🇺🇸 Federal**
* **U.S. Senate:** Sherrod Brown
* **U.S. House, Ohio’s 8th District:** Vanessa Enoch

_If you live outside the 8th District, please support our Democratic congressional nominee in your district, including Greg Landsman (Hamilton County), Kristina Knickerbocker (Butler County), and Don Leonard (Miami County)._
**🏛️ Statewide (all counties)**
* **Governor & Lt. Governor:** Dr. Amy Acton & David Pepper
* **Attorney General:** John Kulewicz
* **Secretary of State:** Allison Russo
* **Auditor:** Annette Blackwell
* **Treasurer:** Seth Walsh
* **Ohio Supreme Court:** Justice Jennifer Brunner and Judge Marilyn Zayas

**Butler County**

| |

* Ohio Senate (5th District): Jeffrey Harris
* Ohio House (80th District): Katie Koehler Wagner

---

Not sure where to vote? Find your polling location at **VoteOhio.gov** or **IWillVote.com** , and remember to bring a valid Ohio photo ID.
---
|
---
| |
**🎉 You’re Invited: Election Night Watch Party!** Once you’ve voted, come celebrate with us as the results come in!📍 **Pike 2 Bar & Grill**, 10010 Springfield Pike
🕖 **Starts at 7:00 p.m.**
📞 (513) 938-PIKE
👉 **RSVP here:** [https://campaignhq.app/rsvp/electionnightwatchparty](https://us.list-manage.com/DdFCE4YoTMj?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
Great food, great drinks, and great people. Let’s come together and support our community! Bring your friends, your family, and your hope. Whatever tonight brings, we built something powerful together: a movement rooted in community, dignity, and opportunity for every family in the 8th District.
**Three Things You Can Do Right Now**
1. **Vote** , if you haven’t already.
2. **Text or call three people** and remind them to vote, especially anyone still holding an absentee ballot.
3. **RSVP** and join us tonight at Pike 2.

Thank you for standing with me and for believing that our district deserves leadership that listens, works hard, and puts people first. Let’s go make history today.
With deep gratitude and hope,

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | | Hello Peter, Today is the day! After months of door-knocking, phone calls, conversations, and community gatherings, it all comes down to this: Tuesday, November 3, is Election Day. Polls are open from 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. , and if you’re in line by 7:30, you have the right to vote. Thank you to every one of you who has given your time, your donations, and your belief in a better future for Ohio’s 8th District. Now let’s finish strong together. ⚠️ Important: If You Have an Absentee Ballot, Do Not Mail It Today Ohio’s election law has changed, and there is no longer a grace period for mailed ballots. Your absentee ballot must arrive at your county Board of Elections by 7:30 p.m. tonight to be counted. A ballot mailed today will almost certainly arrive too late. If you still have your absentee ballot: Hand-deliver it to your county Board of Elections office (or its official drop box) before 7:30 p.m. today. Do not take it to your polling place. Absentee ballots must go to the Board of Elections. Make sure the ID envelope is completed and signed. You can check your ballot status at VoteOhio.gov. Please forward this to friends and family who voted by mail. One forwarded message could save someone’s vote. Vote the Entire Democratic Slate — Top to Bottom Every race on your ballot matters. The people we elect today shape our schools, our roads, our courts, and our economic future. Please vote for the entire Democratic slate. Your ballot will show only the races for your own district. 🇺🇸 Federal U.S. Senate: Sherrod Brown U.S. House, Ohio’s 8th District: Vanessa Enoch If you live outside the 8th District, please support our Democratic congressional nominee in your district, including Greg Landsman (Hamilton County), Kristina Knickerbocker (Butler County), and Don Leonard (Miami County). 🏛️ Statewide (all counties) Governor & Lt. Find your polling location at VoteOhio.gov or IWillVote.com , and remember to bring a valid Ohio photo ID. | | | 🎉 You’re Invited: Election Night Watch Party! Once you’ve voted, come celebrate with us as the results come in!📍 Pike 2 Bar & Grill, 10010 Springfield Pike 🕖 Starts at 7:00 p.m. 📞 (513) 938-PIKE 👉 RSVP here: Great food, great drinks, and great people. Let’s come together and support our community! Bring your friends, your family, and your hope. Whatever tonight brings, we built something powerful together: a movement rooted in community, dignity, and opportunity for every family in the 8th District. Three Things You Can Do Right Now 1. Vote , if you haven’t already. 2. Text or call three people and remind them to vote, especially anyone still holding an absentee ballot. 3. RSVP and join us tonight at Pike 2. Thank you for standing with me and for believing that our district deserves leadership that listens, works hard, and puts people first. Let’s go make history today. I wanted to
take a moment to reflect on how far we’ve come.

But if you don’t have time to read a longer message and want to show your
support before the polls close, [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261103_2.o2o8TH&refcode=em20261103-2&t=1003&akid=9949%2E582294%2E-Hm4QV ]please chip in $5 or any
amount today.

I didn’t enter public service from a family of career politicians. My
roots are right here in Manchester, shaped behind the counter at my
family’s landmark restaurant.

Growing up working there taught me the value of hard work, accountability,
and serving our community. That’s the exact work ethic I wanted to bring
to Washington to fix a system that no longer works for everyday people.

Now in one of the most critical Senate races in the country, I’m ready to
keep being a voice for all Granite Staters.

We’ve come so far building a true grassroots movement across New
Hampshire, but the contrast in this race could not be clearer.

Our campaign is built by working people pitching in what they can when
they can, while John Sununu is backed by Donald Trump, MAGA billionaires,
and corporate PACs.

Sununu has sold out Granite Staters to corporate special interests like
Big Pharma and Wall Street and grew his net worth up to $35 million.
Granite Staters can’t trust him to fight for them as long as he can line
his own pockets.

With just hours left, everything comes down to this final stretch. I need
your help to make sure we have the resources to reach every last voter so
we can protect this open seat and flip the Senate blue in November.

Thank you,

Chris

Hi Peter, It's Election Day in Maine. Polls are open right now and close at 8:00 tonight.

Three things you can do before 8:00 p.m.:
1. **Vote.** [Look up your polling place here.](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=xDM_o8flxF55aheb-ums81BZNLEmacP4ToqJgnLf3XbSX2YMxRlcgLZ36yCbO9q0NommNHmbf9pvScXLbwCjsyk45_duXESIha5JhAFH-WE&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=election_day&n=1)

3. **Bring one more voter with you.** A spouse, a neighbor, a coworker — offer them a ride.

Whatever happens tonight, our campaign has been about getting a government that will deliver results. Making life affordable for Maine people. Lower energy bills. Housing families can afford it. Property tax relief. A state government that answers to Mainers.

Every vote will matter. Please make sure yours is one of them.

Thank you,

Rick

**I am asking everyone on this team to not only vote if you haven’t already, but to talk to everyone and anyone you can today and make sure they make their voices heard at the ballot box.**

Hi Peter, **🗳️ TODAY IS ELECTION DAY!** This is the moment we’ve been building toward all cycle. For months, Tennessee Democrats have been organizing in every corner of the state. Volunteers have knocked doors on city blocks and rural back roads, made call after call, and talked with their neighbors about what’s at stake. Grassroots supporters have powered every step. Now it all comes down to TODAY. **And the choice couldn’t be clearer.** 💰Republicans gave us higher costs. Democrats are fighting to bring them down.
📚Republicans left our public schools dead last in funding. Democrats are fighting to invest in them.

Today is Election Day, and the future of our great state is on the ballot.For years, Arizona has been a beacon of opportunity because voters have supported policies that empower families, protect taxpayers, promote educational freedom, and keep government accountable. Together, we have expanded school choice, kept taxes low, strengthened protections for victims of human trafficking, advanced criminal justice reforms, defended consumers, and worked to keep Arizona one of the best places in America to live, work, and raise a family.**But these accomplishments are not guaranteed to continue.** If Democrats gain control of the Arizona Legislature, many of the policies that have helped make Arizona successful will be at risk. There could be renewed efforts to restrict school choice options for families, increase government spending, expand regulations on businesses and job creators, and move our state in a very different direction. Republicans have fought to protect educational freedom, keep taxes low, support law enforcement, strengthen border security, and preserve the principles of limited government that have helped Arizona thrive.This election is about more than one race or one candidate. It is about the direction of our state for years to come. It is about whether Arizona continues to lead with freedom, opportunity, and personal responsibility, or whether we allow government to play a larger role in the decisions best left to families and local communities.**Every vote matters. Every voice matters.** 🗳️ **Where to vote**

Please return your early ballot to a polling location or ballot drop box before 7pm on November 3rd. If you take your early ballot directly to a polling location today in Maricopa County, you can present a valid ID to an election official to verify your identity and then, feed your early ballot into an on-site tabulator from 6am to 7pm. To find a list of acceptable ID’s, please visit [GetID.Maricopa.Vote](https://us.list-manage.com/yQUe1mEEKcU?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211) Those who participate in this option will have their vote included in election night results.Our state’s laws require all ballots to be received by 7:00 PM on Election Day to be counted.[**Maricopa County Voting Locations**](https://us.list-manage.com/kDHki7ENF4I?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)[**Voting Locations Outside of Maricopa County**](https://us.list-manage.com/19d4D3NMTTM?e=a7ab36849c&c2id=b6e4918ecaa4a9e494d38fc9e6fde211)
I strongly encourage you to vote in person at the polls today and bring like-minded family and friends with you. The decisions made in this election will shape the future of Arizona, and that future belongs to the citizens who participate.Let's keep Arizona strong. Let's keep Arizona free. And let's make our voices heard.It has been an honor to serve this state. Best,**Shawnna**

Prices rose half a percent in September alone. Whoever wins tomorrow,
that number stays.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvcG40VjU2cXgzbQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/qP2hpZHM9bmNBQmxGUTM5dDA2ZW9sc10/gaunwdQ/scq3ff775a6

YOUR IRA & 401(K) ISN'T ON THE BALLOT

Tomorrow you help pick who goes to (or stays in) Washington. One thing
isn't on your ballot: what your money buys.

Government figures out Thursday show prices rose half a percent in
September alone, and 3.6% over the past year.

When prices climb, the dollars in your savings buy a little less food,
a little less at the pharmacy, a little less of everything you live
on.

[Two grocery bags with prescription bottles on a kitchen table. A
label reading $100 in 2016 points to the left bag, full of bread,
apples, bananas and greens, with three pill bottles in front. A red
label reading Same $100 today: about $72 worth points to the right
bag, which holds much less, with two pill bottles. Caption: Your $100
from 2016 now buys about $72 worth.] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/s8p47e7fad8

Even Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said last week that when Americans look
around,

_"...THEY SEE THE PRICES ARE UP."_
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh

If you're retired, no boss hands you a raise to catch up. Your savings
just have to stretch further.

You can't vote on prices. But you can decide how your savings are
spread out [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXS4/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/sfja334b1e7

That's why savers near or in retirement can diversify part of their
savings into physical gold and silver.

From 1973 to 1979, when prices rose about 9% a year, gold rose about
35% a year. Silver soared too.

[Bar chart of average yearly rise from 1973 to 1979: prices rose
8.8% a year, gold rose 35% a year. Past performance is not a promise
of future results.] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/s8p47e7fad8

That's history, not a promise. Gold and silver have rough stretches
too, be very wary of anyone who says otherwise.

But through that long stretch of rising prices, gold and silver held
what money buys.

The free 2026 Ultimate Guide to Gold & Silver shows how you can add
gold & silver to your retirement savings (tax & penalty free) in three
simple steps.

It comes from Goldco, which has helped Americans protect their
retirement savings with gold and silver for over 14 years, earning
more than 8,000 - 5 star reviews, and an A+ rating from the Better
Business Bureau.

The guide is 100% free, available right now, and you can get it by
clicking here [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXTo/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/s1n7cb7a0e8

[The 2026 Ultimate Guide to Gold & Silver from Goldco, shown as a
printed book, an open page spread, on a phone and a tablet, and in a
Goldco folder] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e9192142/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDM/LbmNsd0VCSTA1cg/gaunwdQ/s8p47e7fad8

P.S. Whoever wins tomorrow, prices will still be up 3.6% over the

| Today’s the day, Minnesota! 🗳️

Go vote for your Republican ticket! Polls are open until 8:00 PM. Find your polling place at MNvotes.org.

After you vote, help us get others to the polls. Our final round of calls is loaded in Right Insight, and every call counts. Republicans win today if we show up!

On behalf of the MNGOP, our candidates, and myself, thank you. You made the phone calls, knocked the doors, gave donations, and spent countless hours helping our candidates win. Campaigns are a team effort, and we’ve had an incredible team.

We can’t wait to celebrate with you tonight at our Election Night Watch Party at the DoubleTree Minneapolis South in Bloomington. If you haven’t registered yet, sign up at MNGOP.com.

-Caleb Jungling

Hi Peter,Today is Election Day! There has never been a more critical time to make your voice heard.I’m so proud to be fighting every day in the halls of Congress to protect reproductive rights, push back on this administration's cruel immigration enforcement, and defend our democracy. We are on the brink of pushing through to a new era in Washington, breaking the GOP trifecta, and finally putting a check on the corrupt and cruel Trump administration. _But the outcome is no guarantee – it depends on all of us showing up today._ Here's how to cast your ballot:**VOTE IN PERSON TODAY
**Polls open at 7 AM and close at 8 PM. Every voter who is in line at 8 PM has the right to vote, so please stay in line! New Mexicans decide whether Deb Haaland governs the state that barred her people from voting until 1948. name: Brian Lenney
subject: Some people... lol
body:
ID Ed News just dropped a hard-hitting article this morning.

| |
---|---|---
|
# Some people... lol
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Nov 3
---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
ID Ed News just dropped a hard-hitting article this morning.

The guy who identifies as a reporter emailed me about my Pro-Tem announcement yesterday. Except, not really.

Because he went straight to asking me about some random X account's profile banner instead (because I DARED to retweet something they posted).

The something he got triggered over was this phrase: _**" some cultures are better than others." **_You know where I heard that argument originally? A black man, Thomas Sowell. So why did Sean the "reporter" try to paint me as racist for quoting a black man?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c6cf66c0-3909-478d-ad32-d45ccb507658?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Make it make sense Idaho Ed News!

Now, he could've asked me about anything. Like how Health and Welfare's books showed $433.6 million more cash than it actually had.

Or how the State Controller's office was off $102 million on revenue and $178 million on spending. Or why nobody was even checking those books against the Treasurer's books or the bank's.

Or the $72 million in IDHW grants that got sent to the AG for possible misuse, or illegal labor, or how PACs and lobbyists run the capitol, etc., etc.

But nay!

He didn't like me quoting a black man or the profile banner picture on some random X account's page and made the article about that.

(It's so 2021 of him, really)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9cee47c0-9ee7-4554-bb82-0a8381c5a2d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So, why the weak article?

Here's why: the Idaho Big Ed lobby tells ID Ed News what to do, what to write, who to attack, what articles to pull down (they did this to me) and everyone knows it.

So my guess is they're still mad at how we rammed through [the bill to curbstomp the teachers unions](https://substack.com/@brianlenney/p-192690802) a few months ago and that's why they sent their attack dog after me.
Guess that means I'm over the target.
Cheers,
Brian
**P.S.** If you haven't already go vote today. If you're in Idaho [here's where you can find your sample ballot](https://substack.com/redirect/3eeceb28-dd97-484b-ae0d-d2eaee716140?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I like to print it off and fill it out before I walk into the polls.
**P.P.S.** If you haven't read Sowell on race and culture, here's the trilogy he wrote on it. A great place to start:
1. "Race and Culture: A World View"
2. "Migrations and Cultures"
3. "Conquests and Cultures"

(C) 2026 Brian Lenney
[Unsubscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9icmlhbmxlbm5leS5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWN0aW9uL2Rpc2FibGVfZW1haWw_.XLoUs5jLrU6AWEfF4p8ab8RhpRTIGNKV6kJqLc9rRis?)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/375b799b-405c-4470-b9dc-8943929e63b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)[](https://substack..tgLxmDwThlNC_CGK8CbWI3_Ot4mgsPCa83BU55IF-8Y?)
