This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. strikes Iran 's Qeshm Island: The U.S. strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday as part of a series of unannounced attacks conducted in recent weeks, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials. The officials described the operations as defensive, claiming that Iranian forces had fired a surface-to-air missile at a U.S. fighter jet and launched another missile toward commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Washington has deliberately kept quiet about the strikes to avoid signaling a return to major combat operations, one official said. The revelations contradict President Donald Trump's public portrayal of the conflict as largely dormant. "We haven't been doing any fighting for months," he told reporters on Monday. He also denied plans to attack Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Tuesday that Tehran retains the right to self-defense until U.S. military attacks end "completely and permanently." The Israeli military denied involvement in the reported strikes. U.S. and Iran far from peace deal; Qatar intensifies mediation ahead of midterms: Iran and the United States far apart on an agreement to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, as Qatar intensified mediation efforts to prevent renewed escalation after the U.S. midterm elections. Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran on Monday night to discuss a revised proposal, with both sides expected to respond within 36 hours. Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said that both countries were reviewing the proposal. "If there were no glimmer of hope, there would be no negotiations," he said, adding that "as a mediator, we cannot lose hope." Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf that Tehran had delivered a "strong, rational response" to Washington. "The ball is now in Washington's court," he said. Meanwhile, Trump that Iran wanted a settlement "as soon as possible," and suggested a deal "could happen," even as he threatened to strike Iran's suspected nuclear facility at Pickaxe Mountain "in one hour." Vice President JD Vance said that U.S. negotiators engaged Iran in "a number of good conversations," adding that he felt "pretty good about the prospects" of reaching a negotiated settlement. IRGC claims capture of two U.S. spy drones over Qeshm Island: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Tuesday that its Aerospace Force brought down two U.S. MQM-170 reconnaissance drones over the southern island of Qeshm Island. To date, the IRGC claims to have captured four U.S. drones of this type. Three oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz; Indian sailor killed in separate ship attack: Three oil tankers naval mines and caught fire while traveling through unauthorized routes in the Strait of Hormuz, the IRGC said on Tuesday. The IRGC claimed that the vessels had switched off their identification systems before entering "restricted" waters, triggering explosions that left them burning along the strait's southern shores. Separately, on Monday, an Indian sailor was killed when the Indian-flagged cargo vessel MSV Al Jusufi came under attack near Limah, off Oman's coast. India's Shipping Minister that the remaining 13 crew members were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard. No actor has claimed responsibility for the attack. Talks with Saudi Arabia continue, Iran 's Araghchi says, calling for regional security without foreign forces: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Tuesday that Tehran harbors no hostility toward Gulf Cooperation Council countries, and that it seeks new regional security arrangements led by countries in the region, without foreign military involvement. In a on X referencing his interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi praised the "positive role" played by Qatar and Oman, and said that Iran continues its dialogue with Saudi Arabia. "Our goal is to reach new regional security arrangements established by the countries of the region themselves, away from any foreign military presence," he wrote. Palestine Four Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza: An Israeli drone strike on a police post near the College of Applied Sciences, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, three Palestinians and wounded several others on Tuesday, WAFA reported. One police officer was among those killed in the attack, to the Interior Ministry in Gaza. The ministry condemned the strike, saying that it was part of ongoing Israeli attacks on police and security forces in Gaza. Separately, a man died of wounds sustained in an earlier strike northwest of Khan Younis. Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed six Palestinians--five due to new attacks, and one due to wounds sustained in an earlier attack--and injured 27 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, has risen to 74,615 killed and 175,899 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,599 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,774, while 847 bodies have been recovered. Exclusive: Israel orders complete closure of Gaza crossing with Egypt, blocking aid and commercial goods: Israel informed the UN and Egyptian committee on Monday evening that it is imposing a "complete and comprehensive closure" of the Rafah crossing, blocking humanitarian aid, commercial shipments, food, fuel, and cooking gas entering Gaza through the Egyptian route, a senior Palestinian source involved in negotiations told Drop Site News. Israel claimed that alleged smuggling and "interference by government bodies in the Gaza Strip" were the reasons for the closure, the source said. The Egyptian route handles approximately 50 to 60 trucks daily, the source said, adding that "fuel and gas come entirely through this route." Under the October 2025 ceasefire agreement, 600 aid trucks are supposed to enter Gaza daily, but Israel has severely restricted deliveries, allowing an average of only around 200 trucks per day. The closure comes as Palestinians across Gaza face the onset of winter in makeshift tents and heavily damaged homes, with worsening food insecurity compounded by cuts to UN food assistance and rising prices. Read Abdel Qader Sabbah 's report on the dire conditions in Gaza for Drop Site . In Gaza, 42% of essential medicines, 50% of medical supplies depleted: Forty-two percent of essential medicines and 50% of medical supplies are completely out of stock, Gaza's Health Ministry said on Tuesday, bringing critical healthcare services closer to total collapse. The depletion of chemotherapy drugs, hormonal treatments, immunosuppressants, and clotting factors disrupted 55% of treatment protocols for thousands of patients, the ministry said, exposing them to life-threatening complications as Israeli restrictions obstruct treatment outside Gaza. Israel orders seizure of 11 acres of Palestinian land in occupied West Bank: Israeli authorities issued military orders to seize approximately 45 dunams (11 acres) of Palestinian land across the occupied West Bank. In the northern Jordan Valley, Israeli forces the seizure of seven dunams in Khirbet Al-Hadidiya to construct a military road, following earlier land seizures and the establishment of a settlement outpost in the area. In Jenin, two orders dated October 28 11.2 dunams in Deir Abu Daif and Qabatiya to construct roads and buffer zones around the Ganim and Kadim settlements, which Israel reestablished this year after evacuating them in 2005. Near Ramallah, another order 26.5 dunams in Deir Nizam, Umm Safa, and Atara for a road linking settlements. The orders, which remain in effect until the end of 2028, would expand Israeli military control, restrict Palestinian access to agricultural land, and strengthen infrastructure connecting Israeli settlements, the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said. Israeli forces demolish shops as settlers torch property across West Bank: Hebron: Israeli forces five shops belonging to a Palestinian resident, northwest of Hebron, on Tuesday, WAFA reported. Forces also the Al Jazeera correspondent Muntaser Nassar and more than 20 Palestinians during raids in Dura, reportedly binding and mistreating them before releasing them. In Yatta, south of Hebron, Israeli settlers set fire to two vehicles, an agricultural storage room, and a house under construction, and spray-painted racist slogans. Bethlehem: Israeli forces Palestinians harvesting olives in Khalayel Al-Louz, southeast of Bethlehem, and prevented them from continuing their harvest. Nablus: Israeli settlers a 60-year-old Palestinian man in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, leaving him hospitalized. In Majdal Bani Fadel, south of Nablus, settlers set fire to two vehicles parked outside Palestinian homes. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Israeli forces Luay Nawaf, head of the Ein Yabrud village council, after raiding his home east of Ramallah. Yemen Saudi coalition says it intercepted drone over Mecca; Ansarallah denies launching attack: The Saudi-led coalition on Tuesday that it intercepted a drone over the Mecca region. Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree denied that Yemeni forces had carried out any operations targeting Saudi territory that day, accusing Riyadh of fabricating the incident. Saree the allegation that the Ansarallah had targeted the Islamic holy city of Mecca "an old lie revived," claiming Saudi Arabia was attempting to distract from battlefield defeats. Saudi strikes kill 17 civilians; Ansarallah strike kills five civilians at health center: Saudi airstrikes killed 17 civilians over two days, most of them children, Sana'a Health Ministry said on Tuesday, accusing Saudi forces of targeting homes, residential neighborhoods, and markets. Separately, an Ansarallah ballistic missile struck Al-Saqiyah Health Center in Lahj province on Monday, killing five people, including three medical workers, and wounding 15 others, according to Yemen's Saudi-backed government. Saudi Aramco expands repeatedly attacked oil pipeline: Saudi Arabia oil giant Aramco expanding its East-West crude pipeline and developing additional export routes to bypass the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, CEO Amin Nasser said on Tuesday. Saudi Arabia aims to increase pipeline export capacity to as much as 10 million barrels per day, up from the East-West pipeline's current capacity of 7 million. The key pipeline has been attacked several times since September, with Saudi Arabia blaming an Iraqi armed group for a strike and Ansarallah claiming responsibility for others. Lebanon Israel again violates ceasefire in southern Lebanon: Israeli forces launched multiple attacks across southern Lebanon on Tuesday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Bint Jbeil: Israeli forces the outskirts of Bra'shit. Nabatieh: Israeli forces to homes in Zawtar Al-Sharqiya, and carried out an airstrike on the outskirts of Kfartabnit. Marjeyoun: Israeli forces an explosion in the town of Qantara, accompanied by machine-gun fire. France investigating Israeli attack on Beirut apartment building as possible war crime: Two judges in the crimes against humanity unit of the Paris Judicial Court were an Israeli airstrike on a 12-story residential building in central Beirut on November 26, 2024, that killed seven civilians, including the parents of French-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri, AFP reported. Cherri, whose parents were 87 and 77, filed a complaint this year with the International Federation for Human Rights. His lawyer described the judicial investigation as a first involving alleged Israeli war crimes in Lebanon. "What happened to my parents is not an isolated case," Cherri told AFP. "I hope this investigation will help break the impunity enjoyed by Israeli officials responsible for attacks against civilians in Lebanon and Palestine." U.S. News Midterm elections nationwide: U.S. voters will head to the polls on Tuesday with control of both houses of Congress on the line and with several key Senate races - in Michigan, Texas, Kansas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine and Alaska -- garnering particular attention. Recent polling indicates that Democrats are likely to take over the House and are leading in most (if not all) contested Senate races. Drop Site will be hosting a joint livestream with Breaking Points, available on both YouTube feeds; coverage begins at 6 p.m.. The Guardian: ICE re-arrests immigrants who won release from detention: The Guardian at least 20 cases of immigrants who won their release from detention and were later detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Immigrants have filed more than 91,000 habeas petitions since January 2025, per , more than during the past three administrations combined. Attorneys link many re-detentions to the Trump administration's push for third-country deportations, with more than 25,000 people already sent to third countries. Mamdani demands ICE stop using city property to stage operations: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani that ICE stop using city-owned lots during its enforcement actions. On Monday, the mayor's office sent a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin , acting ICE Director David Venturella , and New York ICE field office head Kenneth Genalo , saying "ICE has no right to use our property as a base for tearing families apart." The letter added, "if they keep coming back, we will see them in court." Mamdani's demand comes after ICE shot a man while he was in his car with his five-year-old son on October 8 in upper Manhattan. Supreme Court rejects Trump administration attempt to force California to set aside 20,000 mail-in ballots: On Monday, the Supreme Court the Trump administration's emergency application to set aside 20,000 mail-in ballots in California. The ruling was swift, coming hours after the administration filed an emergency request. The case follows the Justice Department's declaration in October that it had compiled a list of more than 20,000 likely noncitizen voters in California. That list appeared to be riddled with errors, according to California officials, with only 7,035 names carrying Los Angeles County addresses and others confirmed as U.S.-born citizens. Judge dismisses DOJ 's case against Harvard: Massachusetts U.S. District Judge Myong Joun Harvard University's motion to dismiss the Justice Department's case against it. The DOJ had accused the university of withholding admissions data from investigators seeking to determine if it was in compliance with the Supreme Court's 2023 ban on affirmative action in admissions. The government failed to prove that it had tried to resolve the dispute with the school before suing it, the court found. Joun did not rule on the merits of the case, meaning that the government can reopen its complaint once it addresses procedural deficiencies. Trump says he would consider preemptive pardons for Elon Musk, other allies: In a New York Post interview released Monday, President Trump supposed Democratic threats against Elon Musk , including arrest and nationalizing SpaceX, just "talk," but said "we just have to protect those people." Asked by columnist Miranda Devine about preemptive pardons for Musk and others, he said "I would if I needed to, sure," adding "I'd do it. I did it for J6," referring to clemency for more than 1,500 Capitol riot defendants. Democratic leaders have discussed investigating Musk's business practices, but have not called for his arrest. Musk, whose net worth hovers around $1 trillion, has spent nearly half a billion dollars on Republican candidates and groups during the 2026 midterms. NYT: Trump administration preparing to scale back pregnancy-related workplace protections: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, under chair Andrea Lucas , to narrow work accommodations for pregnant workers, the New York Times reported. As early as this month, the EEOC could release a proposal that scants the implementation of the 2022 Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, which covers such worker protections as bathroom and water breaks, reprieve from heavy lifting, and time off for prenatal care. The law includes accommodations for "related medical conditions," such as abortions, fertility treatments, and care for endometriosis and menstruation. FEMA directs disaster aid to Republican districts in California and Minnesota ahead of midterms : On October 30, the Federal Emergency Management Agency tens of millions of dollars to several Los Angeles, Calif., churches and to projects in or near vulnerable GOP Rep. David Valadao 's Central Valley district, the Washington Sun reported. The same day, FEMA funded one Minnesota project, a road in Rockville in House Majority Whip Tom Emmer 's district. The funds were released after Valadao worked with Speaker Mike Johnson 's office to pressure the White House and Office of Management and Budget for funds, most of which will repair a water district in the San Joaquin Valley. U.S. to remove South Africa, Rwanda from African trade program: Trump informed Congress and the governments of South Africa and Rwanda that the two countries are being cut from the African Growth and Opportunity Act, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Monday. He said the countries were removed for reasons related to "barriers that undermine American trade and investment and practices that pose a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests in the region." The Trump administration has accused South Africa, the program's top exporter, of "anti-white" policies, and criticized its stance on Israel and its ties with Iran. The U.S. sanctioned Rwanda's defense ministry last week over its support for the M23 rebel group in eastern Congo. New York child is first to die of measles in the state in 30 years: New York State health officials on Monday that a child in northern county of Lewis died after contracting measles. Gov. Kathy Hochul linked the death to Trump administration policies that she said eroded confidence in pediatric immunization. Lewis County recorded 15 measles cases by mid-October, all occurring in unvaccinated people. New York has recorded at least 178 cases this year, concentrated in about 10 upstate counties, with Amish communities particularly hard hit. Across the U.S. there have been 4,852 cases this year, more than double the number in 2025. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Exclusive: Al-Shabaab attack in Somalia kills four civilians: Drop Site contributor Mohamed Gabobe reports that Al-Shabaab, an Islamist rebel group, killed four civilians in Somalia's semi-autonomous Puntland region last week, according to two security officials. The dead were identified as Ikran Jama, Naima Ahmed, Jama Said, and Salma Mohamed. On the morning of October 27, Al-Shabaab fighters fired mortar rounds toward Galgala, a town in the Al-Madow mountain range, killing four people. Puntland troops returned fire on the rebels' position, using anti-aircraft guns to repel the attack, the officials said. Just days before the attack, Puntland's President Said Abdullahi Deni announced that the regional government would be launching a military campaign to remove Al-Shabaab from the mountains of Al-Madow. The United Arab Emirates and the United States are backing Somali operations, Gabobe previously for Drop Site. Exclusive: Turkish airstrikes against Al-Shabaab in Somalia kill two civilians: In response to an Al-Shabaab attack on Somali government troops last week, Turkey launched strikes targeting the rebels' military vehicles, Somali security officials involved in joint operations with Turkey told Drop Site contributor . The strikes killed two civilians and sparked anti-Turkish protests. On October 26, Al-Shabaab ambushed Somali government forces outside the town of Lego, in the country's Lower Shabelle region. Al-Shabaab detonated car bombs before firing weapons at the troops. Security officials declined to provide a precise number of military casualties, but told Drop Site that a "substantial" number of troops are unaccounted for. Following Monday's ambush, Al-Shabaab seized multiple military vehicles belonging to the Somali government that had been donated by Turkey, according to the officials. Turkish aircraft located some of the captured vehicles the following day, they said, using GPS tracking systems installed in the vehicles. One of the captured vehicles was located in an area called Jameeco. Turkish aircraft launched an airstrike that destroyed the vehicle. A civilian, 28-year-old Ibrahim Iidow Suxaaye, was working on nearby farmland when he was struck by shrapnel and killed, according to the officials. Al-Shabaab fighters took another seized vehicle to the Waberi neighborhood in Burhakaba district, where they eventually abandoned it, the officials said. A group of civilians were filming a TikTok video near the vehicle when a Turkish airstrike struck the area, wounding 23-year-old Mohamed Hassan Osman, who later died from his wounds, the security officials said. Russia attacks aid site, killing 31, and hospital, injuring 73: Russian forces "directly struck a city clinical hospital" on Monday night, damaging its cardiology department and injuring 73 people, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy . Russia also bombed an aid center in Zaporizhzhia, 31 people. Overnight on Monday, Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles, and 59 cruise missiles, mainly targeting the power grid, leaving more than 180,000 people without power in Zhytomyr and prompting scheduled outages in Odessa. Also on Monday, a Ukrainian drone attack in Russia's Yaroslavl province two workers at an oil refinery. UK increases wait time for most foreign workers seeking permanent residency to 10 years: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood changes to the UK's immigration rules on Monday, tying eligibility for permanent residency to income. People earning over 50,000 pounds ($67,000) will be able to apply for permanent status after five years, and people earning over 125,000 pounds after three years. Others must wait 10 years to apply. Exemptions were carved out for care workers earning at least 25,000 pounds, and for refugees arriving by new "safe and legal routes." Anyone arriving by a small boat or any other "illegal method," Mahmood noted, will have to wait 30 years to apply. Applicants will also be disqualified if they have a criminal record, lack English language proficiency, owe debt to the UK government, or show fewer than three years of national insurance contributions. Ebola death toll in central and eastern Africa tops 5,300; most cases in the Congo: The latest Ebola outbreak in central and Eastern Africa has 5,376 people, according to the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Two deaths have occurred in Kenya and Uganda each. The other 5,372 deaths occurred within the Democratic Republic of the Congo. There have been about 10,444 infections total across the DRC, Uganda, and Kenya, according to data from the Africa CDC--putting the fatality rate above 50%. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for the Bundibugyo strain. Attackers ambush police convoy in Nigeria, killing 8 personnel: An attack on a police convoy in Nigeria's northeastern Zamfara state at least eight Nigerian security personnel, Reuters reported. The dead include five police officers and three members of the state-backed Community Protection Guard. Police also said the attackers, identified only as "bandits," seized five AK-47 rifles and abducted several members of the police convoy; the number and their location are unknown. Northern Ethiopia conflict pushing health system toward collapse, WHO says: The conflict between Tigrayan rebels and the government has killed several civilians in recent days and strained medical facilities,** World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus on Monday. The fighting is pushing the healthcare system to the brink, he added. It is straining health care workers and medical supplies and services. Ghebreyesus warned that drone attacks and civilian casualties were becoming "more frequent" across Ethiopia. The WHO and other UN agencies are working to deliver supplies, he added, urging protection for civilians and health workers. Rubio talks reforms with Venezuelan officials: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco on Monday, with a State Department readout from the meeting saying that Washington reaffirmed Trump's "three-phase plan for Venezuela: stabilization, economic recovery and political reconciliation, and democratic transition." Rubio and Blanco discussed a potential framework for "free, fair, and credible elections" in the country, the readout said. It's Election Day, and we need EVERY Republican to show up and VOTE! The stakes couldn't be higher. The future of Nebraska, our communities, our families, and the conservative values that make our state great are on the ballot.
We've worked too hard and come too far to sit on the sidelines now. Elections aren't won by yard signs, social media posts, or polls. They're won by voters showing up at the ballot box.
Here's what you need to know:

name: Derek Merrin
subject: URGENT: The Polls Close at 7:30 PM. Have You Voted?
body:
Final Hours to Cast Your Ballot! Let Your Voice Be Counted!
| | | | |
---
| Friends,
We're down to the final hours of Election Day.
At 7:30 PM tonight, the polls close, and the opportunity to cast your ballot in this election comes to an end.
This election will help determine the future of Northwest Ohio and the direction of our country. Every vote cast today is a voice in that decision.
IF YOU HAVEN'T VOTED, THERE IS STILL TIME!
Polls remain open until 7:30 PM, and anyone in line by that time has the right to vote.
Don't let a busy schedule or a long day keep you from participating in one of the most important decisions our community makes.
If you've already voted, thank you. Your participation is what makes our democracy work.
We have spent months traveling Northwest Ohio, listening to families, meeting small-business owners, and discussing the challenges facing our communities.
Now, the decision belongs to the voters.
Don't leave your voice unheard. VOTE BEFORE 7:30 PM!
Thank you for your support, your encouragement, and your participation throughout this campaign.
Derek Merrin

Dear
Peter,
This past week, I had the pleasure of joining guest host Sam Peters on The Wayne Allyn Root show to discuss my campaign for Assembly District 37.

We covered a lot of ground during the interview, including the coming fight over tax increases, the Democrats’ dangerous attacks on our brave men and women in law enforcement and how they’re undermining our public safety, and the importance of rebuilding Nevada’s economy in a way that promotes economic liberty and prosperity.

Above all, we talked about what’s at stake this November — the competing visions between myself and my left-wing opponent, and why winning this race is so important to breaking the Democrats’ stranglehold on our state legislature.

I hope you’ll click below to take a listen ... and as always, I’d love any feedback or comments you’d like to provide!
https://andyfornevada.com/andy-matthews_sam-peters_8-28-20/
***

By the way, I was also honored this week to receive the endorsement of the National Rifle Association. I’ve long been a proud champion of the Second Amendment, and it’s an absolute thrill to have the support of our nation’s preeminent defender of the right to bear arms.

Especially today, with Nevada’s Democrats waging a relentless assault on our Second Amendment rights (for her part, my opponent received an “F” grade from the NRA), it’s more important than ever that we elect those who will unapologetically defend our Constitution. And you can count on me to do exactly that in Carson City.

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, this is the
last email you’ll receive from me before the polls close.

So first and foremost, I want to say this: Thank you.

Thank you for offering your time and your support to this campaign.

Thank you for your fight and your determination in these last ten months.

Thank you for defending our progress, our future, and our democracy.

And, well... thank you for putting up with a few (or in this week’s case, a
few dozen) fundraising asks to help us sprint through the finish line.

I’m about to head over to our Election Night watch party,
Derek. But we’re not done yet. In
fact, right after I finish writing this email, I’m going to call a few
more voters on the phone to make sure their ballots are in.

My entire team will be working until the moment polls close at 8PM too —
so I’m humbly asking you for one last favor.

This really is your last chance: Will you rush as much as you can to help
us turn out every last supporter across Pennsylvania and take down Donald
Trump’s movement of chaos, cruelty, and corruption here in the most
competitive battleground state in the country?

Here’s the link: [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23179?t=1001&akid=930%2E245147%2EiRuybo ]secure.actblue.com/donate/shapiro-november26-email

I’m truly grateful for your support,
Derek. Thanks for having my
back.

Josh Shapiro

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with supporters like you.

# **Today is Election Day. Let’s get out and vote!**
---
|
---
| Friend, Over the years, you've stood with me as we fought for more local energy production, prioritized taxpayers by holding the California High Speed Rail Authority accountable, and battled for every drop of water the Central Valley needs. All this happened because we voted for common sense at the ballot box! If you haven't voted yet, there's still time. Here's how: **Return your mail ballot.** Sign and date the envelope, then drop it at any official ballot drop box, vote center, or your county elections office by 8 p.m. If you mail it, it must be postmarked TODAY November 3. If you're mailing it on Election Day, take it inside the post office and ask for a hand postmark. **Vote in person.** Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day. Not registered? You can still register and vote the same day at any in-person voting location in your county. **Find your location.** Look up drop boxes and voting locations at [www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place](https://us.list-manage.com/YT_S7gPQbwL?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8), or track your ballot at [Where's My Ballot](https://us.list-manage.com/Nj1QRJdT3qF?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8). **Already voted?** Thank you! Now please do me one more favor: text, call, or remind three friends and family members to vote. Elections in the Central Valley are won by neighbors talking to neighbors. Every vote counts, and I'd be honored to have yours. Thank you for standing with me,

Congressman Vince Fong

The last 18 months have been an incredible journey.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=9971%2E582294%2E6ynZ6B)
It’s Chris Pappas. Election Day is officially here.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261103_4.d2vhGs&refcode=em20261103-4&t=2&akid=9971%2E582294%2E6ynZ6B)
Over the past 579 days, we’ve taken this campaign to every corner of New Hampshire.
Each of those days has brought me closer to the people who make this state so special.
I’ve heard their challenges: People are struggling.
Truck drivers and commuters are paying more and more at the pump. Small business owners are watching costs climb. Young couples are struggling to afford their first home. And seniors are being forced to make impossible choices about prescriptions and health care.
But I’ve also heard Granite Staters’ hopes for the future.
For their kid to go to college without a mountain of debt. To buy their first home and start a family. To rest easier at night knowing their family is taken care of.
I’m running to make New Hampshire more affordable for working families; protect Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid; safeguard abortion access; and stand up for the small businesses that are the backbone of our communities.
But I couldn’t do any of this without every Granite Stater who put their trust in me and helped build this campaign together. So before the results come in, I want to say thank you.
Whether you knocked on doors, made phone calls, put a sign in your yard, chipped in what you could, or talked to your neighbors about why this race matters – it all made a difference.
We’ve built a movement of people who believe in a freer, fairer future — and now that future is within our reach.
When you love New Hampshire, you don’t just talk about what makes this state special. You stand up and fight for the people who call it home.
Now let’s go win this.
– Chris Pappas
PS: Our team is still working hard on last-minute GOTV efforts across the state. **[If you can, send a donation of $5 or any amount right now to fuel our work. »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261103_4.d2vhGs&refcode=em20261103-4&t=4&akid=9971%2E582294%2E6ynZ6B)**

name: Yasmin at Swing Left
subject: With polls closing, here’s what we’re watching
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
This year, thousands of grassroots volunteers and donors came together to make Ground Truth happen.
#
Hi there,
**With polls beginning to close on the East Coast, I want to take a moment to reach out and say thank you.**
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3258?t=1&akid=3398%2E1562180%2EIxH4Kf)
Over the last year, thousands of grassroots volunteers and donors came together to make a new deep-canvassing voter contact initiative—Ground Truth—a reality everywhere.
That’s what makes this year’s work so important. We knew winning this election was the critical first step, not the end game. We built an innovative way for Democrats to campaign, one that brings candidates closer to the communities they want to represent and rebuilds trust to help persuade more people that Democrats will deliver for them.
As much as I wish I could tell the future, we don’t yet know what the election results will be. But I do know the work you did this cycle will be reflected in tomorrow’s outcomes and in elections for years to come.
Together, members of our community of more than 1 million people raised over **$22.6 million** to help elect Democrats in the most critical swing races and had more than **79,977 conversations** with swing voters.
Behind every one of those dollars and conversations are people.
**People, like a dad in Columbus** , who spoke to Matt, a volunteer who was knocking on doors with his own two kids, aged three and one. The voter shared that his son is on the autism spectrum, and getting him the services he needs is a constant struggle. He said he works 12-hour days and still can't get by. He always votes because he sees it as his duty to his kids. But he doesn't follow politics and hadn't decided on the Senate race. After talking about Republican cuts to education and Sherrod Brown's record for working families, the voter told Matt that Sherrod Brown is the kind of person he wants in the Senate.
**Then there was Araceli** , a voter who teaches English as a second language in California's Central Valley. She talked with one of our volunteers about prices, underfunded schools, and the lack of local jobs forcing people to commute to cities to find work. Over the course of that one conversation, she moved on the scale from a 5 to an 8 on voting for Democrats.
**And finally, there were voters like Kevin.** When a volunteer knocked, he said he wasn't sure about voting, because he'd never voted before and didn't know how. The volunteer's phone was dying, so they wrote the website down by hand: how to register and how to vote early. Kevin said the country is going the wrong way and called out the cost of living. He didn't know anything about the candidates. After hearing about Congressman Derek Tran, he said to put him down as a 9 for voting for him—then gave his number so someone could call back and make sure he got his ballot.
**By choosing to take action this year, you helped reach thousands of voters like these, and every one of those conversations brings our country one step closer to the future we all want to see.**
Whatever tonight brings, I hope you feel extraordinarily proud of what we’ve built together. Because nothing we accomplished this year ends with the midterm elections. Every dollar donated helped power campaigns and our organizing work in critical races. Every door knocked and voter conversation has given us and the greater Democratic ecosystem important learnings about voters for future election cycles. Every key win made possible by this work is ground gained in the tough presidential election ahead.
And every voter we engaged becomes someone we can talk to again, because the fight ahead begins on November 4th.
Because of you, this work matters now, and it will matter long after the polls close.
With gratitude,
Yasmin Radjy
Executive Director, Swing Left
P.S. Make sure to follow Swing Left on [**Instagram**](http://act.swingleft.org/go/3259?t=2&akid=3398%2E1562180%2EIxH4Kf) and [**X (formerly Twitter)**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3260?t=3&akid=3398%2E1562180%2EIxH4Kf), where tonight we’ll be giving live updates on the swing races we targeted this year—many of which will likely come down to tight margins.
And, once we have a clearer picture of the results across the country, we’ll be in touch with more analysis.

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261103-2&t=4&refcode2=3398_1562180_IxH4Kf&akid=3398%2E1562180%2EIxH4Kf)

There's a saying often attributed to Thomas Jefferson that I think about every election day.
"We do not have government by the majority. We have government by the majority who participate."
Whether Jefferson actually said this or it's a product of internet folklore is beside the point. I've long believed that democracy isn't a spectator sport. It requires us to show up.
Today, Americans will show up by heading to the polls while millions of others, including my parents, have already cast their ballots. I've spent enough time in politics to know how consuming elections can be. Regardless of who wins tonight, the work of making this country stronger continues tomorrow. We all have agency to shape this country to be the best that it can be, and that's not limited to just the ballot box.
That belief has shaped much of my work since leaving public office, and it was especially meaningful this week in Palm Beach, where my partner, Genine Fallon, and I hosted the inaugural gathering of _From Pentagon to Portfolio: Investing in Critical Technologies for American Resilience,_ a new leadership series we created from the ground up to bring together leaders in national security, finance, and emerging technology.
We launched this series with a conviction that America's national security and economic future are deeply intertwined. Some of the most exciting new technologies have enormous potential for both our military and the private sector. The problem is, these worlds don't talk to one another enough. Our goal is to bring these people together in the same room to help America stay competitive.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..BkN83LJUHJe7T2WDLlplL9sro0v2Mcpy4cSMTN5lowQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=223351188)
### **From Pentagon to Portfolio: Investing in American Resilience**
At The Palm House, I had the privilege of moderating a discussion with four leaders who understand the intersection of capital, innovation, and national security from very different perspectives: John Dunfee, CEO of JD Group Holdings; Justin Nahama, co-founder and general partner of The Veteran Fund; Sean Drake, founder and managing partner of Stony Lonesome Group; and Kaj Larsen, a former Navy SEAL, entrepreneur, and defense innovation investor.
The gathering also brought together leaders from Siebert Ventures and across the investment and national security communities, reflecting the range of perspectives Genine and I envisioned when we created the series.
We had a great discussion about some of the exciting dual-use technologies changing the way we live and defend our country. We also talked about how to separate real innovation from hype, and why so many promising companies struggle to secure the funding they need to succeed, a challenge known as the "valley of death."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f9e6515f-e5e3-4648-9ea3-acc1d65074a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For Genine and me, the most rewarding part of the evening was seeing an idea we'd dreamed up together finally come to life. What started as a conversation between the two of us has grown into a leadership series we're incredibly proud to have built together.
We're excited to continue the series on **December 3, when we 'll return to The Palm House in Palm Beach** for our next gathering. If you're an investor, entrepreneur, veteran, business leader, or someone interested in helping strengthen America's economic and national security future, we'd love to connect.
### **After Election Day, We 're Still Americans**
The timing of our inaugural gathering, just days before Election Day, was not lost on me. It's easy to forget how much we actually agree on, especially when it comes to wanting a stronger country and a better future for our kids.
I served in Congress as a Democrat, but before that, I served in the Army alongside Americans from every political background imaginable and at the time, was registered like most veterans - as an Independent. When you're leading soldiers in Baghdad, nobody asks whether the person beside them is a Republican or Democrat before trusting them with their life. What matters is character, competence, commitment, and the willingness to put the mission ahead of yourself.
That experience fundamentally shaped how I understand leadership. It doesn't mean our differences are unimportant or that we should avoid difficult debates. A healthy democracy depends on those debates. But it also depends on our ability to recognize that the people on the other side of a political disagreement are still our fellow Americans, and that our responsibility to the country continues long after the election results are announced.
Our evening in Palm Beach was a nice reminder that there's a lot of good work happening outside Washington. Every day, people are coming up with new ideas, building businesses, and finding ways to make a difference. I find that incredibly encouraging. There's so much talent and ambition in this country, and it's exciting to see what people can accomplish when they're given the chance. That work will continue tomorrow morning, regardless of who wins today. As I advise young Americans and my former colleagues in Washington DC, judgement day is more important than Election Day!
### **America 's Strength Requires More Than Military Power**
I also had the pleasure of teaching students again from the University of Notre Dame, where I joined Ambassador Joe Donnelly's class to talk about American "smart power." Joe being a former congressman, senator, and ambassador to the Holy See at the Vatican, knows a thing or two about diplomacy. One of the main issues he worked on while there was reuniting the 30K Ukrainian children who were abducted by Russian forces after the invasion.
We talked about why America's strength depends on more than our military might.
Our Defense Department has a budget approaching $1 trillion and millions of military and civilian personnel. The State Department, meanwhile, has roughly 25,000 employees and operates with a fraction of those resources. Of course, the two have very different responsibilities, but I've always believed we should invest as seriously in preventing wars as we do in preparing to fight them.
Marine General James Mattis put it memorably when he told Congress in 2013, "If you don't fund the State Department fully, then I need to buy more ammunition ultimately." Having served in combat myself, I've always appreciated that perspective. Our military needs to be ready to win wars, but we should be just as committed to preventing them in the first place.
I always love hearing from the students. They're inheriting a complicated world, but I left encouraged by their curiosity and willingness to tackle its challenges. We owe the next generation more than a list of problems to solve. We owe them the chance to help shape the future they'll inherit.
* * *
Genine and I are excited to keep building on what we've started with _Pentagon to Portfolio_. And after spending time with the students at Notre Dame, I'm more convinced than ever that we need to give the next generation a chance to lead.
Today, Americans will make their voices heard at the ballot box. Tomorrow, we'll wake up with the same neighbors and many of the same challenges. Some of us will be celebrating. Others won't. But we're still Americans, and have communities and a country to take care of.
The election will be behind us, but the work of building America's future will be right in front of us. And that is work worth doing together. It's why the windshield is much bigger than the rear view mirror.

What a week in Palm Beach and Notre Dame taught me about the people working to make America better. | | | Nov 3 | | | | | | | | | | | | There's a saying often attributed to Thomas Jefferson that I think about every election day. "We do not have government by the majority. We have government by the majority who participate." Whether Jefferson actually said this or it's a product of internet folklore is beside the point. I've long believed that democracy isn't a spectator sport. It requires us to show up. Today, Americans will show up by heading to the polls while millions of others, including my parents, have already cast their ballots. I've spent enough time in politics to know how consuming elections can be. Regardless of who wins tonight, the work of making this country stronger continues tomorrow. We all have agency to shape this country to be the best that it can be, and that's not limited to just the ballot box. That belief has shaped much of my work since leaving public office, and it was especially meaningful this week in Palm Beach, where my partner, Genine Fallon, and I hosted the inaugural gathering of From Pentagon to Portfolio: Investing in Critical Technologies for American Resilience, a new leadership series we created from the ground up to bring together leaders in national security, finance, and emerging technology. We launched this series with a conviction that America's national security and economic future are deeply intertwined. Some of the most exciting new technologies have enormous potential for both our military and the private sector. The problem is, these worlds don't talk to one another enough. Our goal is to bring these people together in the same room to help America stay competitive. From Pentagon to Portfolio: Investing in American Resilience At The Palm House, I had the privilege of moderating a discussion with four leaders who understand the intersection of capital, innovation, and national security from very different perspectives: John Dunfee, CEO of JD Group Holdings; Justin Nahama, co-founder and general partner of The Veteran Fund; Sean Drake, founder and managing partner of Stony Lonesome Group; and Kaj Larsen, a former Navy SEAL, entrepreneur, and defense innovation investor. The gathering also brought together leaders from Siebert Ventures and across the investment and national security communities, reflecting the range of perspectives Genine and I envisioned when we created the series. We had a great discussion about some of the exciting dual-use technologies changing the way we live and defend our country. We also talked about how to separate real innovation from hype, and why so many promising companies struggle to secure the funding they need to succeed, a challenge known as the "valley of death." | | ---|---|--- For Genine and me, the most rewarding part of the evening was seeing an idea we'd dreamed up together finally come to life. What started as a conversation between the two of us has grown into a leadership series we're incredibly proud to have built together. We're excited to continue the series on December 3, when we 'll return to The Palm House in Palm Beach for our next gathering. If you're an investor, entrepreneur, veteran, business leader, or someone interested in helping strengthen America's economic and national security future, we'd love to connect. After Election Day, We 're Still Americans The timing of our inaugural gathering, just days before Election Day, was not lost on me. It's easy to forget how much we actually agree on, especially when it comes to wanting a stronger country and a better future for our kids. I served in Congress as a Democrat, but before that, I served in the Army alongside Americans from every political background imaginable and at the time, was registered like most veterans - as an Independent. When you're leading soldiers in Baghdad, nobody asks whether the person beside them is a Republican or Democrat before trusting them with their life. What matters is character, competence, commitment, and the willingness to put the mission ahead of yourself. That experience fundamentally shaped how I understand leadership. It doesn't mean our differences are unimportant or that we should avoid difficult debates. A healthy democracy depends on those debates. But it also depends on our ability to recognize that the people on the other side of a political disagreement are still our fellow Americans, and that our responsibility to the country continues long after the election results are announced. Our evening in Palm Beach was a nice reminder that there's a lot of good work happening outside Washington. Every day, people are coming up with new ideas, building businesses, and finding ways to make a difference. I find that incredibly encouraging. There's so much talent and ambition in this country, and it's exciting to see what people can accomplish when they're given the chance. That work will continue tomorrow morning, regardless of who wins today. As I advise young Americans and my former colleagues in Washington DC, judgement day is more important than Election Day! America 's Strength Requires More Than Military Power I also had the pleasure of teaching students again from the University of Notre Dame, where I joined Ambassador Joe Donnelly's class to talk about American "smart power." Joe being a former congressman, senator, and ambassador to the Holy See at the Vatican, knows a thing or two about diplomacy. One of the main issues he worked on while there was reuniting the 30K Ukrainian children who were abducted by Russian forces after the invasion. We talked about why America's strength depends on more than our military might. Our Defense Department has a budget approaching $1 trillion and millions of military and civilian personnel. The State Department, meanwhile, has roughly 25,000 employees and operates with a fraction of those resources. Of course, the two have very different responsibilities, but I've always believed we should invest as seriously in preventing wars as we do in preparing to fight them. Marine General James Mattis put it memorably when he told Congress in 2013, "If you don't fund the State Department fully, then I need to buy more ammunition ultimately." Having served in combat myself, I've always appreciated that perspective. Our military needs to be ready to win wars, but we should be just as committed to preventing them in the first place. I always love hearing from the students. They're inheriting a complicated world, but I left encouraged by their curiosity and willingness to tackle its challenges. We owe the next generation more than a list of problems to solve. We owe them the chance to help shape the future they'll inherit. Genine and I are excited to keep building on what we've started with Pentagon to Portfolio. And after spending time with the students at Notre Dame, I'm more convinced than ever that we need to give the next generation a chance to lead. Today, Americans will make their voices heard at the ballot box. Tomorrow, we'll wake up with the same neighbors and many of the same challenges. Some of us will be celebrating. Others won't. But we're still Americans, and have communities and a country to take care of. The election will be behind us, but the work of building America's future will be right in front of us. And that is work worth doing together. It's why the windshield is much bigger than the rear view mirror. The Secretary's SitRep is a reader-supported publication. subject: These are my parting words.

body:
The next time you hear from me America will be different, for better or for worse

| |
---
|

In a race this tight, every voice and every vote matters. Today, November 3, Americans are voting in the 2026 midterm elections. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 seats in the Senate are being contested. The outcome could reshape the balance of power in Washington.
But this election is about more than which party wins. It is a test of public confidence, an assessment of the administration's record, and an opportunity for voters to influence the direction of national government.
Republicans currently control both chambers. Democrats are seeking to change that. Although the two major parties dominate the American political system, unaffiliated voters and candidates from other parties, including Libertarians, can influence electoral outcomes and offer alternatives to the major parties.
Reuters reports that some analysts favor Democrats to regain the House, while control of the Senate remains uncertain. Affordability, the cost of living, and dissatisfaction with the administration are among the central campaign issues. These are forecasts, not election results.
## DECODE
**Conflict -- What is at stake?**
At its core, this election is a contest over the distribution and exercise of political power.
The Constitution establishes three branches of government with separate powers and responsibilities. Congress is not an extension of the presidency. It has independent legislative authority and a constitutional responsibility to oversee the executive branch.
Who controls Congress influences which legislation advances, how federal money is allocated, and how closely the administration is scrutinized. A change in control of either chamber can alter that balance.
**Impact -- Where does this reach us?**
Decisions made in Washington reach into our families, our economic lives, our environment, and the institutions of government.
* **Familial:** Federal decisions on health care, education, immigration, public safety, and taxation affect household conditions and costs.
* **Economic:** Congressional majorities influence taxes, spending, tariffs, regulation, and the economic environment facing households and businesses.
* **Environmental:** Legislative decisions shape environmental protections, energy policy, public lands, and funding for water resources and infrastructure.
* **Political/Government:** Congressional control determines committee leadership, legislative priorities, and the capacity to investigate and oversee the executive branch.

Congressional oversight is not a partisan privilege. It is a constitutional responsibility.
**Strategy -- What are the parties seeking?**
Republicans are seeking to retain their majorities and continue advancing the administration's priorities. Democrats are seeking control of at least one chamber, creating greater opportunities to challenge the administration's agenda and exercise oversight.
Both parties are asking voters to judge the administration's performance and the direction of national policy. Unaffiliated voters and supporters of alternative parties also have an opportunity to influence the outcome and signal whether the choices offered by the major parties meet their expectations.
## AUDIT
**What should we watch?**
Political forecasts are not substitutes for verified results. The evidence will be in the official vote counts, subsequent certification, and the final composition of the 120th Congress.
Three questions deserve attention:
* Who wins control of the House?
* Who wins control of the Senate?
* What do the results reveal about the priorities and expectations of voters?

The composition of Congress matters. So does how its members exercise the authority entrusted to them.
## THE KITCHEN TABLE PERSPECTIVE
Midterm elections remind those in government that public authority is not permanent ownership.
The presidency may receive the greatest attention, but Congress is a separate branch of government. Our system was designed with divided powers for a reason. Oversight is not obstruction simply because it is inconvenient to the party in power.
The people elect representatives to serve, not to govern without scrutiny.
Today's election will establish a new political balance. Whether that balance serves the public interest will depend on what those elected do with the power entrusted to them.
**Government does not belong to the representatives who temporarily occupy its offices. It belongs to the people.**

ELECTION DAY MESSAGE FROM ALEX PLECHASH

FRIENDS,

TODAY IS ELECTION DAY!

Since May, Republican campaigns and grassroots organizations across Minnesota have reported knocking on more than 2 MILLION doors,
with the final number expected to exceed 2.5 MILLION!

And that doesn't even count the phone calls, text messages, emails and countless conversations happening across our state.

To every volunteer, candidate, campaign worker and local party leader who helped make this possible: THANK YOU!

This has been an extraordinary grassroots effort.

REMEMBER HOW CLOSE MINNESOTA ELECTIONS CAN BE.

Just four years ago, in 2022:

- The State Auditor's race was decided by just 8,435 votes.

- The Attorney General's race was decided by 20,815 votes.

name: Tim Walz
subject: Let’s go win some elections

body:
Our candidates are fighting for every last vote. Let’s have their backs until the polls close.
#
Today’s the day, Peter.
We’ve spent months showing up, knocking doors, and making the case for leaders who will put working families ahead of billionaires and special interests. _Now, let’s go win some elections._
**If you haven’t voted yet,****[find your polling place and make a plan to get there today.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/131?t=1&akid=1312%2E34582%2EU5sdOs) ****We need you in this.**
**[FIND MY POLLING PLACE →](https://act.timwalz.com/go/131?t=2&akid=1312%2E34582%2EU5sdOs)**
Already voted? Thank you. Give a friend or neighbor a nudge to do the same. You don’t win tough races by sitting back and hoping somebody else takes care of it.
Look, another two years of Republicans running Congress means another two years of Donald Trump getting a free pass while working families get stuck with the bill.
I think we’ve had more than enough of that.
We’ve got nine good people running to do something about it—teachers, health care workers, labor leaders, and public servants who know what their neighbors are up against. They’ll fight for good schools, good jobs, and health care people can actually afford.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261103-1.a2Ot4B&amount=5&refcode=em20261103-1312&t=3&akid=1312%2E34582%2EU5sdOs)
This is why we started Small Town PAC: to help Democrats compete in places too many people have written off and elect people who will fight like hell for their communities.
And thanks to everyone who’s contributed, volunteered, or helped spread the word, we’re in this fight. I’m grateful.
But we’re not done yet. **You run through the tape. You don’t slow down because you can see the finish line.**
Our candidates are still knocking doors and turning out voters. We need to make sure they have the support to keep going until the polls close.
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever works for you to Small Town PAC today to fuel this last push, help take back the House, and elect Democratic governors who will stand up to Trump?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261103-1.a2Ot4B&amount=5&refcode=em20261103-1312&t=4&akid=1312%2E34582%2EU5sdOs)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261103-1.a2Ot4B&amount=5&refcode=20261103-1312&t=23&akid=1312%2E34582%2EU5sdOs)**
Let’s finish what we started.
Tim

## **The Third-Party Game: How Both Parties Bankroll Spoilers in Tight Races**
As voters head to the polls today, political commentators are obsessing over raw turnout numbers and late swing-state polls. But there is an untold story that could determine control of Capitol Hill on election night: the quiet explosion of third-party and independent candidates funded by outside groups to siphon off crucial votes.
There has already been massive national focus on the dirty tricks in Alaska, where left-wing operatives went so far as to recruit candidate "Dan J. Sullivan" specifically to confuse voters alongside incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan on the ranked-choice ballot.
[| | | | | Fox News
---
@FoxNews
NEW: "This thing is clearly orchestrated, by the Democratic Party... This is not a legitimate candidate." Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy accuses Democrats of coordinating an alleged scheme involving a candidate with nearly the same name as incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. ...
| 3:18 PM * Oct 30, 2026 * 165K Views252 Replies * 386 Reposts * 1.7K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/b66daa35-d32e-42bc-93c1-74f3d8d03cce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Make no mistake: there is a major distinction between deliberate voter confusion schemes - like what occured in Alaska - and the traditional political practice of boosting third-party candidates to draw votes from an opponent. The Alaska case was explicitly designed to trick people at the ballot box.
However, brand-new reporting from _Axios_ reveals a much larger national effort. Across the country, pop-up super PACs tied to both major parties have dumped over $16.5 million into boosting third-party spoilers in more than 40 key House and Senate battlegrounds.
In contests decided by one or two percentage points, these dark-money pop-up groups could decide who holds the majority.

But there is an untold story that could determine control of Capitol Hill on election night: the quiet explosion of third-party and independent candidates funded by outside groups to siphon off crucial votes. There has already been massive national focus on the dirty tricks in Alaska, where left-wing operatives went so far as to recruit candidate "Dan J. Sullivan" specifically to confuse voters alongside incumbent Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan on the ranked-choice ballot. Make no mistake: there is a major distinction between deliberate voter confusion schemes - like what occured in Alaska - and the traditional political practice of boosting third-party candidates to draw votes from an opponent. The Alaska case was explicitly designed to trick people at the ballot box. However, brand-new reporting from Axios reveals a much larger national effort. Across the country, pop-up super PACs tied to both major parties have dumped over $16.5 million into boosting third-party spoilers in more than 40 key House and Senate battlegrounds. In contests decided by one or two percentage points, these dark-money pop-up groups could decide who holds the majority. We’re going to make them pay the way they’ve made **_us_** pay by making the cost of living unattainable for millions of hardworking people. We’re going to make them pay for allowing Donald Trump to make billions of dollars and attack our democracy, without lifting a finger to stop him. We’re going to make them pay for playing with people’s healthcare like it’s a game, instead of a matter of life or death. body:

It’s
Election Day. And we know Donald Trump won't want to accept the results.

In 53 of the 60 closest House and Senate races in the country, Trump’s
challenge could land in front of a Trump judge who wouldn’t admit, under
oath, that Trump lost in 2020.

Think about what that means. These judges couldn’t tell the truth about
2020. Why would anyone trust them to tell the truth about 2026?

Trump stacked the courts with loyalist after loyalist. So the courts are
on the ballot. Not by name, but every senator elected today will vote on
who gets a lifetime seat on the bench, including Trump’s nominees.

We need senators who will protect our courts, our Constitution, and our
rights. And that starts with one test: Will they vote against Trump’s
crony judges? If the answer isn’t a clear yes, that’s a problem.

The best answer is to vote in numbers so overwhelming that no Trump judge
could deny the outcome.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55887?utm_source=em20261103-61964&t=1003&akid=61964%2E1407376%2ExIBh6E ]Polls are open right now, and every vote makes the results harder to
challenge. Find your polling location, cast your ballot, and then make
sure everyone you know does the same.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55887?utm_source=em20261103-61964&t=1004&akid=61964%2E1407376%2ExIBh6E ]Find your polling location ››

When the polls close tonight, our fight won’t end. Demand Justice exists
to stop Trump’s takeover of our courts, and that means holding every
senator who votes for his dangerous nominees accountable. We’ll make sure
voters know exactly where their senators stand, every single time.

She told us her blood sugar had been 324 when she arrived. After receiving prayer, she checked again: **98.** “Has that ever happened before?” we asked. **“Not just like that.”** She described feeling heat near her pancreas as the woman prayed. As she shared what happened, we stopped to give God praise! I love seeing people respond to the prompting of the Holy Spirit. Hey everybody. Trust me, I know what Election Day jitters feel like.
It's a strange combination of anxiety and caffeine and optimism - and too often, you just don't know what to do with all that energy.
These days, it's all too easy to pull out your phone and start scrolling, looking for some indication of how the day is going. But here's the truth: **That doesn 't help win this election **(and it won't make you feel any better, believe me).
Instead, here are three things you should do instead of refreshing your news feed:
1. **Call voters who still need to cast their ballots.** Our team has up-to-date lists of supporters who we need to get to the polls before 7:30 p.m. tonight. Your call could be the nudge that gets them there. **It 's easy -- you can do it from anywhere. [Just click here to get started](https://substack.com/redirect/3a2ee079-eba3-4349-a0f3-e1ac4c63f08a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. My team will give you all the instructions you need and tell you exactly what you can say.
2. **Put our closing arguments in front of as many voters as possible.** There are several ways to do that -- I'm really proud of **[this ad](https://substack.com/redirect/fa69009c-d0dc-4175-9bc3-69e9ed06f1ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. I laid out exactly what **[my top priorities](https://substack.com/redirect/5a8e94a5-1399-4edf-81ba-fbc03fe8730c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** are the day I'm sworn in as a senator. And here's **[President Obama making our case](https://substack.com/redirect/1a68c58a-5b6e-4e84-aa05-f542643f37e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. Pass them along to someone you know who still needs to vote, or share them on your feed and tag in any Ohio voter you know.
3. **Help prepare for whatever comes next**. I instructed my team to spend every dollar that came in the door to reach voters before polls close. That means our accounts will be at zero (or maybe even a little in the red) by the end of the day. That's on purpose. But it's also taking a big risk. If the result is too close to call and this fight continues beyond tonight, we won't have the resources we need to wage it. **[If you'd like to help get out ahead of that, please make a donation right now.](https://substack.com/redirect/5d9dbc38-0cdf-4887-86c0-d968889002c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

This is what we mean by running through the tape. Don't let up. Don't take your eyes off the victory we want to deliver for Ohio. There are just a handful of hours to go -- you won't regret it.
Thank you. More soon,
-Sherrod
* * *
Before you click away!
Our resources are zeroed out. We've allocated every dollar that came in the door to reach voters before polls close tonight. That means our accounts will be empty (or maybe even a little in the red). That's on purpose. **But it 's also taking a big risk.**
If the result is too close to call and Sherrod's fight continues beyond tonight, we won't have the resources we need to wage it. Outside groups have shown they're willing to spend ungodly sums to buy this seat. We can only expect they'll do the same with Senate control still on the line.
**[If you have the means and would like to help get out ahead of that, make a donation right now.](https://substack.com/redirect/5d9dbc38-0cdf-4887-86c0-d968889002c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Good morning, friends! Election Day is here, polls are open all across the country, and if you haven’t voted yet, _**[now is the time](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142833712/658199710/-1612268846?refcode=261103em_sjj_hope&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNzM5ODhiNi1hOGQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6G0EorG6H72FfjfdGAw2MlYR5-A0yJ459iBS_iGP-64=&emci=6eec56d2-2cd7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=173988b6-a8d7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14239920)**_! I know everyone is feeling a lot of things today. Stressed, anxious, and honestly, angry. I get it — because I’m angry too. I’m angry about families being ripped apart and neighbors being taken from their communities. I’m angry that people can’t afford groceries, child care, or health care while Donald Trump uses his power to enrich himself and his family. I’m angry that for nearly two years, this administration has been testing just how much it can get away with. But here’s what I keep coming back to this morning: that shared anger is a big part of why I feel so much hope. I’m hopeful because after the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , millions of people around the country turned their anger into action and have been pushing to protect and restore reproductive freedom every day since. And in fight after fight since that day, when abortion rights are on the ballot, _we win_. I’m hopeful because when ICE and Border Patrol spread terror in our communities and attack our neighbors, more and more people are standing up and saying _enough is enough_. There is change coming — I can feel it, and I bet you can, too. When I’m campaigning around San Diego, I am constantly filled with hope because there are so many good people dedicated to making our community the best it can be, to solving problems together, and to living up to our values in everything we do. And as I’ve campaigned on behalf of great House candidates around the country in battleground states, I have been blown away by the hope I see in other people — in volunteers, in my fellow candidates, in students on campuses. We don’t know exactly what’s going to happen in this election. But I do know that no matter what, there are millions and millions of people here in San Diego, across California, and around the entire country who believe in a brighter future — who believe in freedom and protecting our rights and fighting together for what’s right. And that fight goes on — today, tomorrow, and every day after. Thank you for being by my side in this incredibly important work, and for everything you’ve done this election cycle to help support my re-election campaign and Democrats everywhere. And of course, one last reminder to go vote! You can look up your polling location or find ballot drop box locations at **[IWillVote.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142833713/658199712/-1612268846?refcode=261103em_sjj_hope&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxNzM5ODhiNi1hOGQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6G0EorG6H72FfjfdGAw2MlYR5-A0yJ459iBS_iGP-64=&emci=6eec56d2-2cd7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=173988b6-a8d7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14239920)** , and please take a few minutes today to remind the people you know to do the same. With gratitude,
Sara

I’m angry that people can’t afford groceries, child care, or health care while Donald Trump uses his power to enrich himself and his family. I’m angry that for nearly two years, this administration has been testing just how much it can get away with. But here’s what I keep coming back to this morning: that shared anger is a big part of why I feel so much hope. I’m hopeful because after the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade , millions of people around the country turned their anger into action and have been pushing to protect and restore reproductive freedom every day since. And in fight after fight since that day, when abortion rights are on the ballot, we win. I’m hopeful because when ICE and Border Patrol spread terror in our communities and attack our neighbors, more and more people are standing up and saying enough is enough. There is change coming — I can feel it, and I bet you can, too. When I’m campaigning around San Diego, I am constantly filled with hope because there are so many good people dedicated to making our community the best it can be, to solving problems together, and to living up to our values in everything we do. And as I’ve campaigned on behalf of great House candidates around the country in battleground states, I have been blown away by the hope I see in other people — in volunteers, in my fellow candidates, in students on campuses. We don’t know exactly what’s going to happen in this election. But I do know that no matter what, there are millions and millions of people here in San Diego, across California, and around the entire country who believe in a brighter future — who believe in freedom and protecting our rights and fighting together for what’s right. And that fight goes on — today, tomorrow, and every day after. Thank you for being by my side in this incredibly important work, and for everything you’ve done this election cycle to help support my re-election campaign and Democrats everywhere. And of course, one last reminder to go vote! You can look up your polling location or find ballot drop box locations at , and please take a few minutes today to remind the people you know to do the same. Peter,

Most of what we send you is strategy: states, numbers, the plan to win. This one is about why we do this work at all. And that starts with Charlie Kirk.

Charlie launched Turning Point in the shadows of the Obama re-election campaign headquarters in Chicago. He was 18 years old.

Every established political force on the Left and the Right tried to stop him.

They failed.

What Charlie started grew into what is **the most influential activist organization in modern American history**.

We were privileged to work with him and be a part of this movement.

We joined Charlie because we believed our mission was the only viable way to save this country. Charlie was willing to do what nobody else in the conservative movement would do. He went looking for young Americans who cared enough about this country to act, and he gave them a reason to fight.

Then came 2020...

Under President Biden, we saw corruption, weaponization of the government, and a government promoting values that put Americans last.

Charlie was adamant that we do everything we could possibly do to fix this in 2024. **We DID IT** , and we must continue for 2026 and 2028 to have a shot at saving this country.

Now, it is on us to continue Charlie's vision and mission.

Every single day, we work to continue his legacy of recruiting, training, and mobilizing a new generation of citizens who love this country enough to do something about it.

That work does not stop at the campus gates. It's now changing the direction of the nation.

Right now, ballot chasers supported by Turning Point PAC are in the field in **states that will determine not just 2026, but the 2028 Presidential election**.

They are meeting voters face to face. They are building real relationships in these communities. They are chasing every ballot, whether it's cast on Election Day or by mail.

This is how we build the Red Wall.

Election Day is November 3rd.

body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/144439?t=6&akid=31241%2E878179%2EtAnwei) Friend, this message is about saying goodbye. Let me explain:

Polls show Republicans have **NEVER** been closer to losing the House.
