body:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
I didn’t expect to write you an email like this again. Not on Election Day.
If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make your first gift to this campaign, this is it.
Here’s why I’m reaching out. A generous supporter has just offered to match grassroots donations up to $200,000 until polls close at 7 p.m. tonight, for one purpose: getting every last Texan who hasn’t voted to the polls.
_**That means if we raise $200,000, we’ll have $400,000 for our final get-out-the-vote push.**_ Every dollar you give becomes two.
As of today, more than 7.7 million Texans have already voted early, and the final polls show this race separated by a point or two. We feel good about what we’re seeing. But early votes only take us part of the way. **If we come up short today, everything we’ve built together over this campaign could be wasted.**
This race is going to come down to who shows up today. So every dollar of this match goes to the work that gets people there:
→ Gas money for the volunteers and staff driving across the state to reach voters
→ Walk lists, clipboards, and literature for canvassers knocking doors through tonight
→ Phone and text banks reminding voters where their polling place is and what they need to bring to the polls
→ Food and water to keep our volunteers going through long days
Greg Abbott has spent years and hundreds of millions of dollars trying to make sure Texans who are ready for change don’t show up today. This is how we fight back: door by door, call by call, text by text.
Here’s what one gift can do. Filling up a Texas-built Chevy Tahoe costs about $87.60. With the match, [**your $43.80**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/2683?c0=em_ms_gh_20261103_2_match.kftrd_&refcode=em20261103-2636&t=3&akid=2636%2E299639%2EDE9BG9) gift fills the whole tank for an organizer zig-zagging across town to reach voters.

My son and I woke up at 5 o'clock this morning, hit Dunkin', and delivered donuts to poll workers all across our neighborhood. It was a simple, humble way to kick off an Election Day where, to be perfectly honest, my nerves have been getting to me.
I'm nervous about what's going to happen today. I've heard a few folks toss around the term "nauseously optimistic," and I can't think of a better way to put it. The polls look good. The fundamentals look good. Our candidates are crushing it, our fundraising is up, and Fox News' ratings are down. It seems like Democrats are on the verge of a potentially historic midterm victory, thanks to Donald Trump's destruction of this country. And yet my stomach is in knots, because we know better than to take anything for granted.
I don't know what's going to happen today, and I won't pretend I do. There are going to be a lot of people giving you crap analysis of early vote numbers and today's turnout. Ignore them. My advice: keep your head down, do the work, go be with your family, keep your mental health in order, and be prepared for whatever comes next.
Because tonight, we will know. We'll know about the House, the Senate, the governor's races, and the state houses. By tomorrow morning, we'll most likely know the state of our union, and then we'll go from there, step by step.
* * *
**Today 's rant is sponsored by Ground News.**
And as the midterms wrap up, the flood of headlines, competing narratives, and political noise is only beginning. That's why I'll be using Ground News to cut through it all, to compare how the results are being covered, and get a clearer picture of what's actually happening.
Take this report--over 200 outlets picked up a story about President Trump threatening to ramp up vetoes in the case that Democrats win the House or Senate in the midterm elections.
**The Independent** says _If Republicans lose their majorities, Trump said he expects to issue vetoes for "a month or two" before negotiating agreements with opposition leaders._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e102acf9-bb0c-4215-8a9b-2d79d931e409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**New York Post** states _The president also agreed with[Elon Musk's recent warning](https://substack.com/redirect/b4ee3e50-6b9a-41d1-b0da-29349c17e333?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that if Democrats sweep the elections on Tuesday, the country will be "maybe forever destroyed."_

Election Day is finally here, Peter!
**All of our organizing and our collective resistance has been leading up to today. It’s time to show the strength of this people-powered movement at the ballot box.**
If you haven’t voted yet, make a plan and bring a friend! [**Click here to find your polling place.**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/55526?t=2&akid=6929%2E420207%2ELWAMrd) And remember: if you’re in line before the polls close, **stay in line**. You have a right to make your voice heard.

Lastly, if anything gets in the way of exercising your right to vote today, call or text the Election Protection Hotline at 866-OUR-VOTE.
Thank you, thank you, thank you for refusing to back down, for believing in the progressive future we’re building together, and for standing shoulder to shoulder with us in this fight every single day. **Now let’s bring these wins home!**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

---
| | | Hi Peter,
---
Today is Election Day, and I wanted to take a few minutes to reflect on how we got here.
My journey from City Council, to the State House and State Senate, and now Congress is a journey I never take for granted, and it was never just mine. Throughout every campaign, neighbors knocked doors, made phone calls, and chipped in because they believed Michigan can do better. This campaign is no different. I am immensely grateful for all of you.
Your voice has always mattered. And I’m running to protect it.
In the State Senate, where I chair the Elections Committee, we pushed forward a state Voting Rights Act to defend your right to vote after the Supreme Court gutted the federal one. Let’s take that work to Washington, stop Donald Trump’s attempts to federalize our elections, and pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act.
Michiganders want tougher, bolder, and stronger leaders. They are sick and tired of Democrats who show up to the knife fight with a pie chart. I plan to show up ready.

clean_body: | | | Hi Peter, Today is Election Day, and I wanted to take a few minutes to reflect on how we got here. My journey from City Council, to the State House and State Senate, and now Congress is a journey I never take for granted, and it was never just mine. Throughout every campaign, neighbors knocked doors, made phone calls, and chipped in because they believed Michigan can do better. This campaign is no different. I am immensely grateful for all of you. Your voice has always mattered. And I’m running to protect it. In the State Senate, where I chair the Elections Committee, we pushed forward a state Voting Rights Act to defend your right to vote after the Supreme Court gutted the federal one. Let’s take that work to Washington, stop Donald Trump’s attempts to federalize our elections, and pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act. Michiganders want tougher, bolder, and stronger leaders. They are sick and tired of Democrats who show up to the knife fight with a pie chart. I plan to show up ready. = | | | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | | = | | Thank you for everything you have done to get us here. | | Happy Election Day! First things first: If you haven’t voted yet, or if you know someone who needs one last reminder, close this email and get it done. Now that that’s out of the way — I want to thank you for everything you’ve done to defend our democracy leading up to today’s pivotal elections. It’s been a tough battle. Anti-democracy, neo-Confederate extremists in the Republican Party tried to predetermine the outcome of the midterms. They tried to cement one-party rule through racist voting maps, racist voter suppression schemes, and constant attacks on free and fair elections. But the American people have said, loud and clear, HANDS OFF OUR VOTES. We’ve already seen historic turnout in Georgia and key states across the country, driven in large part by righteous defiance from Black voters who refuse to be silenced: “Black turnout surges in South” —Bloomberg “The Supreme Court’s gutting of the Voting Rights Act is mobilizing Black voters. Look at Alabama.” —Mother Jones “Republicans' redistricting efforts fuel turnout among young Black voters” —NPR News “Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi” —The Hill None of this was a given. I’m grateful for the Democracy Champions who put themselves forward as candidates — who’ve expanded the map in races that Republicans never thought they’d have to sweat. I’m grateful for the poll workers who are giving it their all to make our elections run as smoothly as possible. I’m grateful for the voters who are making their voices heard. I’m grateful for the whole team at Fair Fight, who relentlessly push back against voter suppression, fight for equal access to the ballot box, and help elect voting rights champions. **And I’m grateful for you, for fueling this fight.** No matter what happens tonight, no matter what MAGA Republicans try to do to deny or discount the results, no matter which new voter suppression measures or rigged voting maps they try to pass, we’re not going anywhere. clean_body: | | | Happy Election Day! First things first: If you haven’t voted yet, or if you know someone who needs one last reminder, close this email and get it done. Now that that’s out of the way — I want to thank you for everything you’ve done to defend our democracy leading up to today’s pivotal elections. It’s been a tough battle. Anti-democracy, neo-Confederate extremists in the Republican Party tried to predetermine the outcome of the midterms. They tried to cement one-party rule through racist voting maps, racist voter suppression schemes, and constant attacks on free and fair elections. But the American people have said, loud and clear, HANDS OFF OUR VOTES. We’ve already seen historic turnout in Georgia and key states across the country, driven in large part by righteous defiance from Black voters who refuse to be silenced: “Black turnout surges in South” —Bloomberg “The Supreme Court’s gutting of the Voting Rights Act is mobilizing Black voters. Look at Alabama.” —Mother Jones “Republicans' redistricting efforts fuel turnout among young Black voters” —NPR News “Democrats see battleground map expand to South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi” —The Hill None of this was a given. I’m grateful for the Democracy Champions who put themselves forward as candidates — who’ve expanded the map in races that Republicans never thought they’d have to sweat. I’m grateful for the poll workers who are giving it their all to make our elections run as smoothly as possible. I’m grateful for the voters who are making their voices heard. I’m grateful for the whole team at Fair Fight, who relentlessly push back against voter suppression, fight for equal access to the ballot box, and help elect voting rights champions. And I’m grateful for you, for fueling this fight. No matter what happens tonight, no matter what MAGA Republicans try to do to deny or discount the results, no matter which new voter suppression measures or rigged voting maps they try to pass, we’re not going anywhere. We will keep fighting to defend the freedom to vote and uphold the will of the people. Together. | Peter,

_Formerly All On The Line_

But there’s nothing worse on Election Day than trying to sit still and stew in your nerves.
Taking action beats waiting around. Here are three ways you can still make an impact before polls close tonight:

body:
Let’s not wait 22 days this time. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142837451/658212565/439559405?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTY1OGRjNjQtYjBkNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xVQUVvCAqyGXDxS9_uWMbP9NxUCpBIqopYK3A0wWQ7c=)
Today’s the day. Two years ago, Derek won this seat by 653 votes, and it took 22 days to find out. This time we’d like to know on election night, and that comes down to the ballots still out across CA-45. If yours is one of them, there’s still time. Return it to any drop box or vote center in Orange or LA County by 8 PM, or vote in person at a vote center, where you can also register on the spot. Anyone in line at 8 PM still gets to vote. | **[Find a drop box or vote center near you](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142837452/658212566/-1136299304?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOTY1OGRjNjQtYjBkNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xVQUVvCAqyGXDxS9_uWMbP9NxUCpBIqopYK3A0wWQ7c=&emci=0f04d6c6-a6d7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=9658dc64-b0d7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=27336212) **
---
Once you’ve voted, take one more minute and text a friend or family member in the district to ask if they’ve voted yet. A two-line text is one of the most effective reminders there is.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: Don't get pulled into the noise
body:
| | | |
---
There's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted. Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes. I will not be distracted. Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders. — This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach. — And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades. **Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.** Election Day is TODAY. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. # [Blue wave to freeze AI centers dead on Election Day ballot](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Americans **[vote Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/36d156ce-46c3-45c3-ba26-144dfda5a508?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with prediction markets giving Democrats a 94% chance of the House and 78% of the Senate, as **[Ed Yardeni warned](https://substack.com/redirect/4fbd8e48-8f99-40b0-bcfb-8320cbe17ecc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a sweep could deliver a **[cold shower for stocks](https://substack.com/redirect/46efa87a-6a7b-4cef-ad7c-bf244841d099?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[AI data-center anger put Oracle and utilities at risk.](https://substack.com/redirect/619efb27-36b7-470d-a177-a0f082806775?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Markets not pricing the sweep** : CNBC noted stocks are not fully pricing a Democratic sweep, so a blue wave could hit shares Wednesday while a GOP hold may spark a relief rally.
* **Historical post-midterm pattern** : The S&P 500 has risen in the year after every midterm since 1982, averaging about 0.2% after a day and 1.1% after a month across elections from 1980 to 2024.
* **Yardeni cold-shower warning** : A Democratic sweep could chill equities through gridlock and pressure on valuations, unlike the usual preference for divided government.
* **AI data centers on ballot** : Voter anger over AI data centers could show up in results, putting Oracle and utility stocks in the crosshairs.

# [Ternus Apple beats but memory costs crush holiday margins](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In John Ternus's[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/028a454e-300d-4e8e-8dd3-5f9ca689c5cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[first quarter as CEO,](https://substack.com/redirect/028a454e-300d-4e8e-8dd3-5f9ca689c5cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/028a454e-300d-4e8e-8dd3-5f9ca689c5cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Apple posted record September-quarter revenue of **[$114.5 billion and $2.10 EPS,](https://substack.com/redirect/36d5324c-0f24-4623-abd9-999a872f8c7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** yet shares slid about 3% after he guided December **[gross margin to 45%-46%](https://substack.com/redirect/82a70c88-b240-42e9-99c5-a201ce3cf6b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on unprecedented memory prices.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **iPhone and services lead the beat** : iPhone revenue rose 17% to $57.58 billion and services hit a record $31.6 billion, though growth slowed to 9.8%, the lowest since 2023.
* **Margin guide trails Street** : December gross margin of 45%-46% versus 46.3% expected, driven by higher memory costs and the Siri AI ramp; Ternus called prices unprecedented.
* **Inventory and China flags** : Inventory surged 154% to $14.5 billion and Greater China missed in reports, while Duo supply timing remains hard to predict.
* **Analysts mostly constructive** : Several raised targets despite the soft outlook after the 12% revenue gain to a record fiscal year of $478.8 billion.

# [Anthropic's $17B quarter hides an $895B compute bomb](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Anthropic's **[amended S-1](https://substack.com/redirect/c17cf20b-8f9c-4e65-aa3a-6d04506a45b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** showed third-quarter revenue near $17 billion, up more than 1,100%, yet the company swung back to a $567 million operating loss while disclosing $895.4 billion in spending commitments.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4392c370-4d76-487e-8917-8fd05c87f67e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revenue explosion versus loss** : Q3 revenue of $16.96 billion rose 1,127% year-over-year, but GAAP **[operating profit lasted only one quarter](https://substack.com/redirect/d1737b61-f91b-4279-a13b-52500b4eeb3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** before the $567 million loss.
* **Compute commitments dominate** : Nearly $900 billion committed, $69.8 billion due within 12 months and extending to 2045, second only to Google, with plans to double capacity toward 7 gigawatts.
* **Valuation pressure mounts** : Investors pushed for a more cautious $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion IPO range; Dan Ives called an expected junk rating a gut punch.
* **Governance and red flags** :**[Public shareholders lack voting power](https://substack.com/redirect/10b684dc-be5b-410e-b06d-c75d96a75a65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and nine-month net losses reached $104 billion amid the growth.

# [Qeshm strike erases Monday's biggest oil drop since July](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Crude plunged Monday on hopes of U.S.-Iran diplomacy, the largest decline since July, **[then rebounded Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/0f6de420-6405-43dd-888a-b3da004f2012?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after reports of a U.S. strike on Iran's Qeshm Island renewed supply concerns.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f241fa7a-513c-41c8-ad56-a60e2b19ed28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Monday 's sharp selloff**: Brent[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/de72cd79-6f7f-4d1a-8a03-e232fd043579?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[fell about 3% to $101.54 and WTI toward $94,](https://substack.com/redirect/de72cd79-6f7f-4d1a-8a03-e232fd043579?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/de72cd79-6f7f-4d1a-8a03-e232fd043579?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with accounts of a 7-8% plunge on circulating peace drafts and Trump comments.
* **Tuesday rebound on strike** : January Brent rose 1.8% to $106.63 after the reported Qeshm Island action dimmed near-term deal hopes.
* **Goldman lifts 2027 forecast** : **[Struyven raised December 2027 Brent](https://substack.com/redirect/101dd002-7ba3-43aa-9596-2b543abdb512?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to $105 from $90, citing a larger geopolitical risk premium even as output recovers.
* **Backwardation and flows** : Brent 1-month/6-month ratio near war-era levels; some notes that reported normal flows exclude Iranian barrels and diesel/LNG shortfalls.

# [AI bounce dies as tech enters Election Day correction](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The information technology sector **[entered correction territory,](https://substack.com/redirect/7d7a569a-34c9-4b49-bf06-64f365d6e729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** down more than 10% from its recent record, after Monday's AI rebound collapsed and the **[Nasdaq fell 1.1% in its largest intraday reversal since January.](https://substack.com/redirect/50de1657-c777-4cd8-bb97-ccfe0d3b161b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7951650c-3df0-4972-8679-2cf185b0b17e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Equal-weight outperformance** : The equal-weight S&P rose 1.1% versus 0.2% for the cap-weighted index, **[showing most stocks holding up](https://substack.com/redirect/bdbdf9da-b9f7-484a-a052-b5d6ef2d61bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as megacap AI names faltered.
* **Nasdaq 100 in correction** : The Nasdaq 100 closed more than 10% below its Oct. 6 peak, with chip stocks reversing early gains.
* **VIX and calm fear** : The VIX touched its highest since April but closed at 19.4 after a near-2% S&P drop, leaving options pros noting an unreactive gauge.
* **Defensive rotation** : Buying in Walmart, Berkshire and Lilly added hundreds of billions while chips sold off; Santoli argued the bull market still needs tech recovery.

# [Marvell plunges on $115B all-stock Lumentum deal](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Marvell **[fell sharply](https://substack.com/redirect/88e360a5-771a-4d77-a82f-1c0438a0f786?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after unveiling a $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum, with the stock punished as investors digested the large AI optical bet **[amid a broader tech selloff.](https://substack.com/redirect/ed0e8f5e-9efd-4d19-a4d3-60d947424b3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/afbea0f1-67c1-4348-9ab7-90bf974c9f9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deal size and structure** : The all-stock transaction valued Lumentum at $115 billion, with exchange terms that left both names under pressure on the announcement.
* **Market reaction** : Marvell dropped about 13% and Lumentum fell hard as the AI trade faltered and oil plunged on the same day.
* **Strategic rationale** : The combination aims to expand addressable market in optical and AI infrastructure, though timing and integration risks weighed on shares.
* **Broader context** : The deal landed as chip stocks reversed earlier gains and the info tech sector moved into correction territory.

# [Palantir slides as new contract growth slows despite the beat](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Palantir **[reported strong quarterly results](https://substack.com/redirect/0170fd2f-ecac-4de5-ae7b-a0dac3503338?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** but the **[stock tumbled as new contract growth slowed](https://substack.com/redirect/4da57c06-bb6a-4878-8108-12fd279a74b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and deal lengths shortened, adding to pressure on AI software names heading into Election Day.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f7b228d0-fb2c-4d1f-84d7-89aca4bb51db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revenue strength** : The company posted solid top-line growth with commercial momentum, though total contract value growth decelerated sharply from prior quarters.
* **Contract slowdown** : New contract growth cooled and average deal duration shortened, raising questions about the sustainability of the AI software ramp.
* **Stock reaction** : Shares fell in after-hours and premarket trading alongside Apple as investors rotated out of high-multiple AI names.
* **Market context** : The drop fit a broader pattern of AI-related stocks giving back gains as the Nasdaq moved into correction territory.

# [Dow futures drop on Election Day as Apple and Palantir slide](https://substack.com/redirect/47c78771-3c19-419e-8a53-f9c0067df298?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Dow[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/336368f5-14ab-498b-b1d4-79e706f08bdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[futures fell 0.8% as Americans headed to the polls,](https://substack.com/redirect/336368f5-14ab-498b-b1d4-79e706f08bdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/336368f5-14ab-498b-b1d4-79e706f08bdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)with investors de-risking defensively and Apple and Palantir **[leading premarket declines](https://substack.com/redirect/0018ff8e-d539-4351-a28e-17caac8ded2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after their earnings reports.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/84184752-050d-44f7-84e9-feec4d123ffa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Premarket pressure** : S&P 500 futures slipped while the Dow took the brunt of selling as blue chips faced Election Day caution.
* **Earnings movers** : Apple and Palantir weighed on tech after their reports, while other names like Pfizer showed relative strength on guidance.
* **Defensive posture** : Investors reduced risk heading into results, with the broader AI trade still under pressure from the prior session's reversal.
* **Oil and geopolitics** : Mixed signals from Iran added to the cautious tone as futures traded mixed to lower.

Colorado Lottery’s third-best year: Where the $181.4 million goes

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

PRESENTED BY ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Hi friends!

🗳️ IT’S ELECTION DAY, COLORADO! If your ballot is still sitting
on the kitchen counter, today is the day. Through Sunday, 1.6 million
ballots had been returned statewide, a 39% turnout that is ahead of
the 2022 pace. Unaffiliated voters make up 43% of returns, Democrats
31% and Republicans 24%. If unaffiliated voters break 65-35 for
Democrats, that split would hand Democrats roughly a 314,000-ballot
edge statewide, so the unaffiliated vote is the one to watch, and
turnout today will decide the rest.

Don’t mail your ballot at this point. Drop it at a ballot drop box
or vote in person at a voter service center before polls close at 7
p.m. Every vote counts, so make a plan and get yours in. And don't
forget to check out our full election reporting & ballot guides below:

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

COLORADO LOTTERY’S THIRD-BEST YEAR: WHERE THE $181.4 MILLION GOES
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

The Colorado Lottery sold $887,851,993 in tickets in FY25-26, the
third-highest sales year in its history, and raised $181,424,926 for
parks, recreation and conservation programs across the state.

Sales rose $59,992,274, or 7.2 percent, over the prior year, according
to the financial audit released Oct. 19 by the Office of the State
Auditor.

Scratch tickets carried most of the sales. Scratch reached
$613,527,126, an all-time record, up 2.3 percent. The Lottery said
national scratch sales fell about 0.5 percent while Colorado’s grew,
and that Colorado ranked seventh among all U.S. lotteries for scratch
growth.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

COLORADO ELECTION PREDICTIONS: WHO ORDERED ANOTHER ROUND?
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

DENVER GAZETTE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_Columnist Jon Caldara predicts Colorado voters will wake up Wednesday
to a state further entrenched in one-party rule, with Democrats
sweeping statewide offices and socialist-aligned candidates gaining
ground._

*
A LOPSIDED STATEWIDE SWEEP EXPECTED: Caldara predicts Democrats will
win every statewide office, send John Hickenlooper back to the Senate
alongside “two young ideological socialists,” Melat Kiros and
Manny Rutinel, and add roughly four more DSA-aligned members to the
state legislature, with Secretary of State Jena Griswold facing the
closest race against challenger Michael Allen.

*
A MIXED OUTLOOK ON BALLOT MEASURES: He expects the graduated income
tax (Amendment 87) to fail but worries Proposition NN’s TABOR
override could pass, while predicting three citizen-driven measures on
child sex trafficking penalties, girls’ sports and sex-change
surgery on minors will fare well, with the third being close.

*
A BROADER ECONOMIC WARNING: Caldara frames the election as voters
failing to connect past choices to current unaffordability and
infrastructure problems, arguing Colorado’s political trajectory
will leave the state “poorer, bluer” without any check on
single-party power.

PLAYING GOD WITH THE UNBORN: THE GENESIS 3 ROOT OF THE ABORTION DEBATE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 2

_The abortion question comes down to when a human life gains moral
status. This is not a secondary detail. It is the entire dispute.
Every argument about “choice,” “bodily autonomy,”
“reproductive rights,” or “healthcare” collapses into one
prior claim: that a human organism at some stage of development does
not yet possess the moral status that forbids intentional killing._
__

THE HONOR WEAPON: MOTHER, MAY I? HONORING A PARENT, HONESTLY
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | NOVEMBER 1

_Remember Mother, May I? The childhood game where getting ahead
depended on permission? Forget to ask, and back to the beginning.
Apparently, even walking required management approval. Fun as a game.
A challenging way to spend the rest of your life. (Somebody give me an
AMEN!)_

BAUER: YOUR VOTE DOES COUNT, SO PLEASE VOTE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHIRLEY BAUER | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 30

_If you received your ballot and haven’t turned it in yet because
you think “It doesn’t matter,” believe me, it does! Every vote
is important, and we know an election was decided by only three votes
recently. This year, there are 14 ballot issues that are very
important to each and every one of us. The results will decide whether
you pay more taxes or your taxes stay the same, and also will impact
TABOR in a negative way._

If your ballot is still sitting on the kitchen counter, today is the day. Through Sunday, 1.6 million ballots had been returned statewide, a 39% turnout that is ahead of the 2022 pace. Sales rose $59,992,274, or 7.2 percent, over the prior year, according to the financial audit released Oct. 19 by the Office of the State Auditor. Scratch tickets carried most of the sales. Scratch reached $613,527,126, an all-time record, up 2.3 percent. The Lottery said national scratch sales fell about 0.5 percent while Colorado’s grew, and that Colorado ranked seventh among all U.S. lotteries for scratch growth. clean_body: If you haven't voted yet, now is the time to make your voice heard. | | | Peter, Today is Election Day! If you haven't voted yet, now is the time to make your voice heard. Colorado's future is on the ballot, and your vote will help decide who stands up for our rights, protects our state and fights for Colorado families. If you still have your ballot, return it by 7pm tonight at a voter center or drop box. You can also vote in-person at a voter center if you are in line by 7pm. And in Colorado, eligible voters can register and vote until 7pm at a voter center. If you've already voted, thank you! Please remind your friends, family, and neighbors to cast their ballots, too. It's been an honor to travel across our beautiful state and meet so many incredible Coloradans. Now let's make our voices heard. Thank you, Jena Follow Jena Online: Paid for by Jena for Colorado. # **Join Us in Los Angeles for the IPA Fundraiser**
---
|
---
| Autism Health is proud to support our friends and partners at **Informed Policy Advocates (IPA)** for their upcoming fundraiser this **Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 3:30 PM to 6:30 PM in Los Angeles, California**. As organizations committed to education, advocacy, transparency, and informed decision-making, Autism Health and IPA share a passion for empowering families and protecting the rights of individuals to make informed choices about their health and well-being. We value our collaboration and the important work IPA is doing to bring awareness to issues affecting families and communities. We invite our Southern California supporters to join us for an afternoon of connection, meaningful conversations, and fundraising in support of IPA's ongoing advocacy efforts. Your participation helps strengthen a community dedicated to making a positive impact through education and public engagement. **Event Details:** **Date:** Saturday, November 7, 2026
**Time:** 3:30 PM to 6:30 PM
**Location:** Los Angeles, California We look forward to seeing you there and continuing to build meaningful partnerships that make a difference!
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/K6CXeWlb7LB?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")

|

# **Join Us for Our Annual Gala in California!**
---
|
---
| Join us for an unforgettable evening of elegance, inspiration, and purpose at the **Transforming Lives Annual Gala: Lighting the Path to Solutions!** Hosted by Autism Health. This special event will bring together philanthropists, community leaders, healthcare professionals, and advocates who share a commitment to advancing research, education, and innovative solutions for individuals with autism and their families. We invite you to be part of this extraordinary evening at the beautiful **Sherwood Country Club in Thousand Oaks, California** , while taking advantage of our exclusive **Early Bird ticket and table pricing, available through November 30, 2026!** **Date:** Saturday, January 30, 2027 **Location: Sherwood Country Club**
[320 W Stafford Road](https://us.list-manage.com/15YGL8z8cMj?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332)
[Thousand Oaks, CA 91361](https://us.list-manage.com/JTB6q6nbrw1?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332) **VIP Reception:** 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM
**General Admission:** 6:00 PM – 10:30 PM **Dress Code:** Formal Attire/Black-Tie For a limited time, we're offering **exclusive Early Bird discounts on all tickets and tables!** Take advantage of these special savings now through November 30, 2026. **Prices increase December 1st!** **General Admission:** ~~$650~~ , **now $550**
_Save $100!_
**VIP Admission:** ~~$1,050~~ , **now $950**
_Save $100!_
**General Admission Table of 10:** ~~$6,000~~ , **now**** $5,000**
_Save $1,000!_
**VIP Table of 10:** ~~$10,000~~ , **now****$9,000**
_Save $1,000!_ **Don't wait! Secure your tickets or reserve your table today before Early Bird pricing ends November 30th!** We are honored to feature **General Michael Flynn, Del Bigtree, Nick Vujicic, Dr. Sabine Hazan, and Dr. Brian Hooker** , with additional special guests and speakers to be announced. Guests will enjoy an elegant evening featuring exceptional dining, drinks, live entertainment, inspiring presentations, and exciting **live and silent auctions** , all while supporting a cause that is close to our hearts. **Sponsorship opportunities are also available for businesses and individuals who want to make an even greater impact.** Please contact Tracy For more information at [**tracy@autismhealth.com**](mailto:tracy@autismhealth.com). Thank you for your continued support, generosity, and belief in our mission. We look forward to celebrating with you in Thousand Oaks as we light the path to solutions and work together to transform lives!
---

# **Join Us for the November Autism Support Group**
---
|
---
| You are invited to join us for our next **Autism Support Group on Tuesday, November 10th at 4:30 PM PST / 7:30 PM EST via Zoom**. Our monthly support group is a welcoming space for parents, caregivers, and families impacted by autism to come together, connect, and learn from one another. This is an opportunity to **ask questions, share experiences, hear parent testimonials, exchange resources, and receive encouragement** from a community that understands the challenges and victories that can come with the autism journey. At Autism Health, we believe families need more than information. They need **connection, support, and a community where they feel heard**. Whether your family is navigating a new diagnosis or you have been on this journey for many years, you are welcome to join us. **Advance registration is required to attend.** Once registered, you will receive the Zoom information for the meeting. We look forward to seeing you and continuing to build a strong and supportive Autism Health community!
---
| [REGISTER HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/DI0F7JT3M7_?e=3a42edfdc4&c2id=8db3279a53aa0d16c24f727ce5cda332 "REGISTER HERE")

# **Our Black Friday Virtual Silent Auction Is Now LIVE!**
---
|
---
| The holiday season is here, and what better way to give meaningful gifts while supporting an incredible cause? **Autism Health's Black Friday Virtual Silent Auction is officially OPEN** , offering a wonderful opportunity to shop for unique holiday gifts while making a difference in the lives of individuals and families impacted by autism. From one-of-a-kind collectibles and wellness packages to special experiences and thoughtful gifts, there's something for everyone! Whether you're shopping for loved ones or treating yourself, every winning bid helps support Autism Health's mission of advancing research, providing educational resources, expanding family support programs, and making meaningful care more accessible to those who need it most. **Our auction is completely virtual** , so you can browse and place bids from the comfort of your home, no matter where you live. It's a wonderful way to get a head start on your holiday shopping while giving back to a cause that truly matters. **The auction is LIVE NOW and closes Sunday, November 29, 2026, at 6:00 PM PST!** Don't wait until the last minute! Explore our auction items, place your bids, and share this opportunity with friends and family. **Click the link below to browse our auction and start bidding today!** Thank you for supporting Autism Health Inc. and helping us continue creating better solutions for a brighter tomorrow. Your generosity makes our mission possible!

---
| Autism Health is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to educating individuals, families, and communities about autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Autism Health provides educational programs, workshops, events, research, and resources tailored to meet the diverse needs of those impacted by autism and other neurological disorders.

Thank you for your support.

Across Pennsylvania—and throughout the country—Democrats are running to protect working families, defend our rights, strengthen our communities, and move us forward. This weekend, I was proud to join my colleague Senator James Malone in Lancaster to knock doors, speak with voters, and help elect Democrats up and down the ticket.
Knocking doors in Lancaster with Senator James Malone to help re-elect him and elect Democrats up and down the ticket.

subject: The Opinion Piece the Spokesman-Review Didn’t Want You To See.

body:

**Disappointment in The Spokesman-Review**
The Spokesman-Review recently ran an op-ed criticizing Michael just a week before the election, written by two Democrats, one of whom used to be a Republican. Community leader Eric Johnson - a former U.S. Air Force officer and physician - strongly disagreed with the op-ed written by the two Democrats and wrote his own opinion piece supporting our campaign in response. However, the Spokesman-Review editors refused to run the pro-Baumgartner piece saying that they don’t run election-related material in the 7 days before the election.

Unfortunately, this has become a pattern of behavior from the Spokesman. Earlier this year, when I co-wrote a guest opinion column on agricultural trade policy with highly respected Eastern Washington agricultural leader Alex McGregor, the Spokesman-Review refused to run it - instead demanding significant editorial changes reflecting their own bias.
The Spokesman’s declining editorial standards in their opinion section have become more obvious this year, coinciding with the unfortunate turmoil in their newsroom and management.

A core ethical standard in journalism is the “right to reply” - providing an individual or group with an opportunity to respond. Meanwhile, the letters to the editor and opinion section should show both sides of an argument, and supporters and opponents from all political viewpoints. In 2026, that didn’t happen.
The Spokesman Opinion sections runs a deluge of anti-Republican letters to the editor with half-truths, outright lies, and absurd headlines - including from paid Democrat campaign staff - while we know of multiple occasions where supporters who have written pro-Baumgartner statements are subjected to selective “fact-checks” or do not have their letters placed in the paper.
Criticizing elected leaders is good and in many cases very important - but the manner in which the Spokesman is being run does a disservice to our community and undoubtedly reduces the number of paying customers who subscribe.
To be clear, we will continue to work with The Spokesman-Review to help our community have news coverage they can trust.
For the good of our community, we can hope things improve.
You can read the opinion piece that the Spokesman rejected below.
-Michael & Eleanor
P.S. We’re going to win tonight. Thank you for all the support.
---
|
---
| |
**Crossing Party Lines: An Alternative View**
By Eric Johnson
The premise of the Guest Opinion “When to Cross Party Lines” (10/27/2026) - that it is important for politicians to work across party lines for our community and nation – is sound.
However, I disagree with the ensuing criticism of Congressman Michael Baumgartner, and I wish to respond to the points raised by Candace Mumm and Richard Kuhling.
This opinion was a political attack masquerading as civil discourse. It was jointly authored by Democrat politician Candace Mumm and Richard Kuhling – supposedly from “different political camps”.
I can find no evidence in Ms. Mumm’s past political life of ever “crossing party lines.” Mr. Kuhling has indeed worked on Republican political campaigns, but he left the Republican party years ago, as evidenced by his documented financial contributions to the Biden campaign in 2020, the Harris Presidential campaign in 2024, and to Ms. Conroy in 2024 in her unsuccessful bid for Congress. It is disingenuous for Mr. Kuhling and Ms. Mumm to assume a facade of impartiality. They lack standing.
I am confident that our late former Representative. George Nethercutt, who was a very close friend of mine, would be a strong supporter of Michael Baumgartner. Not just because of his conservative support for lower taxes, personal responsibility, and greater individual freedom – but also his character, family values, optimism, sense of humor, and civility. This contrasts with Ms. Conroy who began launching her political attacks on Mr. Baumgartner before he was even sworn in, and she has not withdrawn her comments about “beheading” and “decapitating” the Department of Homeland Security.
Kuhling and Mumm ask readers to “put policy issues aside” when deciding whom to support in this congressional election. Perhaps they make that request because of the unpopularity of Ms. Conroy’s positions on weighty matters related to foreign policy and to domestic matters such as illegal immigration, composition of the Supreme Court, and the way we Americans view our history.
Before Baumgartner was elected in 2024, I knew exactly who he was from his eight years as a State Senator. He is a conservative Republican who votes his conscience and well represents our district. His voting record and public comments reflect a rational understanding for the need for secure borders, public safety, support for the U.S. military, elimination of the possibility of a nuclear armed Iran, and the protection of the civil rights of all Americans.
Cultural and social issues matter to me. Ms. Conroy opposes Initiative 638, a commonsense proposal which would ensure that only biological girls compete with and against female students. Mr. Baumgartner supports the initiative. Ms. Conroy opposes a federal ban on “physical gender-transitioning drugs and surgeries for minors”. Mr. Baumgartner believes that “young people should wait until adulthood to make such decisions”.
Mr. Kuhling and Ms. Mumm are quite correct that politicians need to be able to work closely with the opposing party. I offer the following as proof that Congressman Baumgartner has a track record of doing just that as a State Senator and U.S. Congressman.
He worked closely with Democrats to bring the new WSU Elson S. Floyd College of Medicine to Spokane, and he went against his own party to secure the funding to finish the North-South freeway.
Over his first term in Congress, Rep. Baumgartner has worked side by side with Democrats on issues that favorably impact Eastern Washington. He has worked on bipartisan legislation: a new Farm Bill, forest management and wildfire prevention, support for rural communities through Secure Rural Schools, stopping Members of Congress from trading individual stocks, and along with Senator Cantwell protecting college sports.
After the recent wildfires, Rep. Baumgartner worked hand in hand with leaders in our city and state, regardless of political affiliation, to get support to our community.
Rep. Baumgartner has been a voice of civility and calm at a challenging and divisive time in our country. I read his weekly official newsletter and am impressed by his efforts to travel this large district, meeting with groups and individuals all over Eastern Washington. There are good reasons he is supported by many prominent local individuals and groups including the Washington Farm Bureau, our local tribes, timber groups, and small business advocates.
Clearly, Ms. Mumm and Mr. Kuhling are motivated by a dislike of President Trump. They seek to make Rep. Baumgartner responsible for the President’s actions and words. Their advice is misguided. We should judge people on their own merits.
Ms. Mumm’s and Mr. Kuhling’s unpleasant and unfounded advice should be ignored.
Eric Johnson, MDColonel, USAFFormer Assistant Clinical Professor, Elson S. Floyd School of MedicineSpokane.

Tonight, as the votes are counted, I want to say something personal: thank you.
Thank you for standing with me through every step of this election. Through the long days, the tough weeks, and the final sprint, you showed up. You chipped in, you knocked on doors, you made calls, you told your family and neighbors to vote. I’m proud of what we built together.
We fought for working families. We fought for immigrant communities. We fought to protect our democracy and make sure every voice is heard. I never forget who I’m fighting for, and I never forget who’s fighting alongside me.
This is the fight of our lives, but I’m not finished. Whether Democrats win or lose tonight, I’m going to keep fighting for the people who sent me here, and for the Democrats across the country working to take back the House.
For now, all that’s left to do is wait. And I’m so glad I’m waiting with you.
Thank you again, Peter.
Linda ❤️

Today's the day we've been working toward: Election Day.
When I retired from music to run for Congress in TX-15, I didn't know if I'd even make the ballot. It wasn't a sure thing. But step by step, we've created a movement that matters to people. We've restored hope to a region that's felt overlooked, cast aside by politicians of both parties.
**Now, the entire country is paying attention.**
If we win here, control of Congress will change hands. Every gift of $10 or $25 from generous donors made this possible. The quinceañeras. The ranch halls. The conversations on a front porch or in a backyard.
_All that 's left to do is vote._
Whether you're registered here in South Texas or are following along with my race from thousands of miles away, I'm asking you to cast a ballot before polls close.
**[Go to IWillVote.com to learn where and how you can make your voice heard.](https://substack.com/redirect/48883975-9701-415b-b786-deeedf35e8b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Let's all get out there and do our part.
Thanks for everything,
Bobby

## Data removal is difficult, by design
Some data brokers often bury opt-out pages where you'd never think to look. When your personal data is their business model, they're not exactly motivated to make leaving easy. Here's what you're up against:
* Opt-out pages that are hard (or impossible) to find
* Lengthy processes: email confirmations, ID verification--even phone calls
* Your data quietly reappears later.

It's frustrating by design. [And they're counting on you to give up](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskD1uwzAMhU8jbzFEyZHiQUOBwFu6djRkkUoIyFYgK3-3LxwURQ_Q8SNI4nvv6zSePCdezp9-JlefMY9IyMFXwnGhx5qoVioj-uoLzfnuE6_IMXK4pTq9cFRSmR3ATuo_l9CgmyT20JAD22ur1d6q5uK8IUXmYDx0aIFsf4BJRQkaDnZSNjTstocAUkMvodNtDHsynd7Hqfc9yU50kpBrLm29UKWnX2N65TuVNuS5Se5S63UV-kOoQagByaeWl5DPC7echRp8jGMQesgxUhkZhT4aocw2fgNou_GabyWQ0MffUJuTUOZW0s9iUxxeH5wSr8aKTp5nz-ltUf-zybtT3wEAAP__1m2Lkg). [](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskD1uwzAMhU8jbzFEyZHiQUOBwFu6djRkkUoIyFYgK3-3LxwURQ_Q8SNI4nvv6zSePCdezp9-JlefMY9IyMFXwnGhx5qoVioj-uoLzfnuE6_IMXK4pTq9cFRSmR3ATuo_l9CgmyT20JAD22ur1d6q5uK8IUXmYDx0aIFsf4BJRQkaDnZSNjTstocAUkMvodNtDHsynd7Hqfc9yU50kpBrLm29UKWnX2N65TuVNuS5Se5S63UV-kOoQagByaeWl5DPC7echRp8jGMQesgxUhkZhT4aocw2fgNou_GabyWQ0MffUJuTUOZW0s9iUxxeH5wSr8aKTp5nz-ltUf-zybtT3wEAAP__1m2Lkg)
## Data brokers profit, you pay the price
While data brokers make a killing selling your personal information, you pay the price with your privacy and security. Exposed personal information puts you at risk for:

* Doxxing and stalking
* Physical attacks
* Increased insurance premiums and loan denials
* Spam and targeted marketing

I’m a former geologist and one of the only published scientists in the U.S. Senate. I also helped open Colorado’s first brewpub, The Wynkoop, in 1988 and began the rejuvenation of downtown Denver. At The Wynkoop, there was no problem we couldn’t solve over a fresh, Colorado beer. Eventually, I found myself in public service. But I didn’t run for office for fame, or money, or power. I ran because I wanted to bring people together and actually make everyday life better for Colorado families. That’s exactly what we’ve done. (I also hated having a boss!) As Denver’s Mayor, we unified the metro area to expand and rejuvenate our public transit. We also initiated the most significant police reforms in Denver’s history, and provided high-quality Early Childhood Education for every four-year-old in the city. As Governor, we took Colorado’s economy from 40th to #1 in the nation for three straight years. And as your Senator, we wrote and passed the largest-ever effort to fight climate change, passed the most consequential housing bill in decades, and brought money and jobs back to our state. Now I’m running for re-election to help Democrats take back the Senate and bring MAGA’s ruthless agenda to a halt. And to finish fixing what we started under President Biden! * * *
If you have paid attention to my reporting since the start of the second Trump administration, then you are aware that just because our southern border is more secure and deportations are on the rise, that does not mean all illegal migration to the United States totally stopped.
Migrant caravans have been leaving southern Mexico all year. As the midterms have been approaching, however, the number of caravans forming and leaving has dramatically increased.
I went back to Tapachula, Mexico, which is on the country's southern border, to report on the latest migrant caravan leaving the city to ask if the Democrats' political momentum is encouraging more migrants to leave.
It should not be surprising that the Democrats promising to abolish the Department of Homeland Security and ICE are now a pull factor in getting migrants in Latin America to start heading north.
## _WATCH:_
[](https://substack.com/redirect/29e248c8-04e0-4a01-9d90-55c9e80d3c5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[ Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/29e248c8-04e0-4a01-9d90-55c9e80d3c5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"And really for us, if the Democrats were to come back to power, it would be...I think it would be a big help," one migrant told us as we walked with the caravan.
"Everybody [is] waiting for the Democrats to win and, I believe bro, the Democrats are going to win" the midterms, a previously deported Honduaran said.
It is because of the heavy backlash to Trump's deportation plans, migrants waiting for the next opportunity to be able to enter the United States will be sooner rather than later.
Of course, even if Democrats take back control of both chambers of Congress, not much will change with Trump's immigration policies, but it could signal the border will open again if Democrats win the White House in 2028.

This is why migrants in Mexico are willing to start the journey to northern Mexico now so they can be in the best position possible should that scenario come to pass.
Since the Biden-Harris border crisis was easily solved on Trump's first day back as president, many voters have forgotten just how big of a problem it was. Understandably, their concerns are on other topics, but the issue of immigration is ever present.
Due to Congress not codifying many of Trump's executive orders into law, a Democrat president who fulfills the current campaign promises can cause another border crisis just as quickly as Biden did. Only this time I believe the surge will be worse than before since there is precedent for the border closing for four years.
It bears repeating that Trump will not be able to totally undo the damage caused by the Biden-Harris border crisis. Illegal immigration was a problem before the over 10 million people illegally entered in a short amount of time. That said, a lot of progress has been made and it will be up to the voters if they want to continue that momentum or signal to the rest of the world to be ready.

body:
| | | [ ](https://www.tanyafortx27.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn11JJNENg30eeUPXVkqayxCfDLIkkjdPcC_U3XuHRoCIwMELeQenzQ2oHmoOYJU340&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=tyvm&n=1)
---
Dear Peter,
---
When we started this campaign, a lot of people wrote us off as an R+16 district. Some did so kindly, some bluntly, and plenty just gave us a polite shrug, as if to say, thanks for trying, but obviously you don't have a chance. However, so many of you saw my vision, and you showed up. Together we found that path at the doors we knocked and in the conversations we had with swing voters. You knocked doors in the heat. You put signs in your yards in red counties and drove more signs across the district. You hosted events, made calls, gave when it meant something to give, and talked to neighbors who hadn't been asked for their vote in years. Statewide candidates came to stand with us. Friends brought friends. People I had never met became people I will never forget. Whether our scrappy little campaign had the time and resources to travel all of that path this year is another question. The path is there, and now more people can see it than ever before. Whatever happens when the votes are counted, I want you to know what we have built together. We laid groundwork in this district that hasn't existed in a very long time. We forged real relationships, lasting ones, some of them lifelong. We proved that people here are hungry for someone to show up, listen, and fight for them. None of that groundwork disappears on election night. It is the foundation the next fight gets built on. There are moments in this campaign I still can't quite believe. Seeing my name on a sign in someone's yard is surreal every single time. Not because it's my name, but because every one of those signs means someone decided to stand up and be counted. Those signs are the most humbling thing I have ever experienced. I don't know that there are enough words to express how grateful I am. This campaign has been a blessing, and the greatest part of it has been you. Your spirit, your stubbornness, your willingness to believe when everyone said not to bother. You inspired me every single day. Thank you. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. With love and gratitude, Tanya

clean_body: | | | Dear Peter, When we started this campaign, a lot of people wrote us off as an R+16 district. Some did so kindly, some bluntly, and plenty just gave us a polite shrug, as if to say, thanks for trying, but obviously you don't have a chance. However, so many of you saw my vision, and you showed up. Together we found that path at the doors we knocked and in the conversations we had with swing voters. You knocked doors in the heat. You put signs in your yards in red counties and drove more signs across the district. You hosted events, made calls, gave when it meant something to give, and talked to neighbors who hadn't been asked for their vote in years. Statewide candidates came to stand with us. Friends brought friends. People I had never met became people I will never forget. Whether our scrappy little campaign had the time and resources to travel all of that path this year is another question. The path is there, and now more people can see it than ever before. Whatever happens when the votes are counted, I want you to know what we have built together. We laid groundwork in this district that hasn't existed in a very long time. We forged real relationships, lasting ones, some of them lifelong. We proved that people here are hungry for someone to show up, listen, and fight for them. None of that groundwork disappears on election night. It is the foundation the next fight gets built on. There are moments in this campaign I still can't quite believe. Seeing my name on a sign in someone's yard is surreal every single time. Not because it's my name, but because every one of those signs means someone decided to stand up and be counted. Those signs are the most humbling thing I have ever experienced. I don't know that there are enough words to express how grateful I am. This campaign has been a blessing, and the greatest part of it has been you. Your spirit, your stubbornness, your willingness to believe when everyone said not to bother. You inspired me every single day. Thank you. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. With love and gratitude, Tanya | | | ---|---|--- Pol. Adv. body:
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=9970%2E582294%2EhMcvIr)
Thank you.
Tonight I’m honored beyond words to be elected as New Hampshire’s next U.S. Senator.
Voters said, in a resounding voice, that America needs a course correction. Washington needs a new generation at the table to fix things. And New Hampshire needs independent leadership to stand up and get things done.
Voters in New Hampshire and all across the country have simply had enough and are demanding a change in direction. **And I’m ready to fight with everything I’ve got to deliver the change we need.**
New Hampshire, we must be clear-eyed about the scale of the challenges we face and the work it'll take to move forward.
Whether it’s building the housing Granite Staters need, expanding access to health care and child care, saving Social Security, protecting our planet, restoring reproductive freedom, rooting out corruption, or holding the administration accountable, we don’t have a moment to waste.
There will be moments ahead that test our resolve, and there will be times when we hit roadblocks and get frustrated with the pace of progress.
But we can never give up, and we must be committed to renewing the purpose of American democracy and working with persistence and urgency every day.
I’ll be honored to stand shoulder to shoulder with you, to work with anyone willing to deliver for the people of New Hampshire, and to stand up to anyone who tries to set us back.
**Across the state Granite Staters are showing the fighting spirit, resilience, and determination we're known for.**
That’s how we do things in New Hampshire. We step up, we roll up our sleeves, and we make it happen. And that’s the spirit I’ll bring to my work in the Senate.
_This was a hard-won victory._
Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and the corporate special interests threw money, attack ads, and outright lies at us for months. _$67 million worth of it._ But we beat them anyway.
Whether you chipped in, made phone calls, knocked on doors, talked to your friends and neighbors about what’s at stake, or simply kept up with our campaign by reading emails like this one. _Thank you._ I wouldn’t be here without you.
So as we celebrate tonight, let’s think about the brighter future that we will build together. Let’s remember what’s possible when we join with a common purpose to fight for a freer, fairer New Hampshire.
Today we all did our part to put our state and country on a better path. Tomorrow we get to work to fight for what’s right and deliver the solutions we desperately need.
Let’s keep going.
Thank you,
Chris Pappas

clean_body: | | Peter, Election Day is finally here. It's hard to believe this amazing movement we built together with so much grit and heart comes down to the next few hours. Today, I am reminded of what Robert F. Kennedy told the world less than three years after his brother was murdered in Dallas: Each time a man stands up for an ideal, he sends forth a tiny ripple of hope. For over a year, Texans across our district have been standing up for liberty, justice, dignity, and respect for all people. You stood up at food drives, community service events, and organizing parties that proved everyday people want their government sane and serving its neighbors again. Today those ripples become a wave. I believe that wave will wash away the hate and prejudice infecting our politics. | Keith Self and his extremist allies can feel it coming, and they are panicking. This week President Trump himself tried to rescue Self’s sinking campaign by attacking me by name in another unhinged Truth Social post. He dusted off every tired insult in his collection for a veteran who gave this country 20 years in uniform. | I take none of that personally. Infantile name-calling and insults are the desperate throes of small men, and you don’t send in the president to rescue a race you’re winning. Keith Self and Donald Trump spent this race trying to turn our neighbors into monsters. We spent it meeting neighbors and building a new Texas majority out of everyone they tried to divide. The extremists bought attack ads with a billionaire’s money. We built a wave out of front porches in McKinney, kitchen tables in Allen, and folding chairs from Fairview to Sulphur Springs. I believe our vision of service will carry us past Keith Self and deliver Collin County for James Talarico. If you still need to make your plan, Then call your neighbors, your friends, and your family and get them to the polls. I will have much more to say about my gratitude for every one of you in the days ahead. Right now, my team and I are getting back on the doors until the last poll closes. One more chance to make your stand. I know a lot of you saw that number and felt what I felt: we can actually do this.

But since then, the polls have moved in the wrong direction. Today, the average has me trailing Abbott by 2.7 points.

Here’s what I need you to hear: 2.7 points is not a lost race. This is one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, and it will be decided by turnout, by organizing, and by what we do in these final days.

clean_body: We turned a long shot into a dead heat. Now we need to finish it. | | | | I want to be straight with you, because you’ve earned that. Back in April, I was down almost 7 points to Greg Abbott in the polling average. Political insiders wrote this race off. Then you showed up: you chipped in, spread the word, and proved that people all over the country believe Texas can be taken back. By October 7, we had cut that gap to just 1.3 points. I know a lot of you saw that number and felt what I felt: we can actually do this. But since then, the polls have moved in the wrong direction. Today, the average has me trailing Abbott by 2.7 points. Here’s what I need you to hear: 2.7 points is not a lost race. This is one of the most competitive governor’s races in the country, and it will be decided by turnout, by organizing, and by what we do in these final days. Two weeks ago, we were closer to beating Greg Abbott than anyone thought possible. If we let up now, we could lose this race by a margin we could have closed. I need you in this fight with me. = Early voting is already underway, and every dollar we raise right now goes straight into reaching the voters who will decide this thing. We can’t get comfortable. Not for a single day. We have to make sure every voter hears the truth about Greg Abbott before they cast their ballot. Here’s just one example: a watchdog investigation just found that Abbott’s much-hyped “pause” on data center permits was never a pause at all. Dozens of projects kept moving forward. That’s Greg Abbott: a press release for voters, business as usual for his corporate allies. Your donation could be the difference between winning and losing. In most of America, the deal is simple: use less electricity, pay less. In Louisiana, regulators have spent over a decade perfecting a different arrangement -- one where your utility gets paid for the power you _didn 't use_. Not a rebate. Not a credit. A charge, collected right on your bill, for the profits the company says it lost because you had the nerve to conserve.
The mechanism has a boring name -- the "lost revenue adjustment mechanism," or in Louisiana's rules, recovery of the "lost contribution to fixed costs." Here's the plain-English version. Utilities argue that poles, wires, and power plants have to be paid for whether you flip a switch or not. Fair enough -- that's a rate-design debate older than most of us. But Louisiana's Public Service Commission went further. When an efficiency program actually works -- attic insulation, LED retrofits, an HVAC tune-up -- and your kilowatts drop, the utility doesn't just keep its guaranteed return on those fixed assets. It files to recover the sales it never made. You use less; the invoice uses more. Utilities call it revenue stability. Critics call it a charge for lost profits. Both are describing the same line item.
This has been a long game. The commission opened its energy-efficiency docket in 2011 -- the Louisiana Illuminator, summing things up in April 2025, called it a statewide energy efficiency program that it spent 14 years creating. In June 2013 the PSC voted to give the utilities a year to propose programs. In November 2014, Cleco, Entergy Louisiana, and Southwestern Electric Power launched their Quick Start efficiency programs -- and from day one, the rules let those utilities recover their lost contribution to fixed costs from the very customers the programs were supposedly helping. The American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy's review of lost-revenue mechanisms lists all three utilities and the 2014 arithmetic for doing it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72d443da-4999-4abe-ac3a-5146f7b01be7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
By July 2024, it was out in the open. The Illuminator's Wesley Muller published a story headlined: "Customers who save on electric bills could be forced to pay utility company for lost profits." The commission was weighing bids for a third-party administrator to run the statewide program, and the utilities wanted their lost revenue protected. Advocates -- including the Alliance for Affordable Energy -- pointed to the uncomfortable math: even under the existing setup, when efficiency worked, utilities still got paid for it, to the tune of roughly $6 million a year.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.QmAHAXBRBFCOXQbh5o0vIE2Poz4dOcEP7wjN6EId2_E?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=218822413)
Then came the twist. On April 16, 2025, the commission voted 3-2, along party lines, to kill the statewide program before it could launch in 2026. Republican Chairman Mike Francis proposed the termination, citing administrative overhead; Commissioners Eric Skrmetta and Jean-Paul Coussan joined him over Democrats Foster Campbell and Davante Lewis. Efficiency advocates howled that Louisianans would pay the price. But nobody should have mistaken the vote for the end of the money. One month later, the commission created its own "Louisiana Public Service Commission Energy Efficiency Program," and on August 28, 2025, it adopted rules that -- per the commission's own filings -- "maintain the structure initially created under the Quick Start program," eliminated the old $75-a-month cap on what large customers could be charged, and raised program budgets. The utilities collect through a rider on your bill, the Energy Efficiency Cost Recovery Rider. It shows up as real dollars on real statements.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/969ab62b-e2b3-4efa-8a55-324321cc8355?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And where did the earlier money go? The Illuminator reported in June 2025 that the programs had amassed an $80 million pot of ratepayer cash with little to show for it -- including $400,000 that Skrmetta steered toward energy-efficient stadium lighting. A conservation fund, in other words, that conserved nothing but found money for ballparks.
All of this is happening as Louisiana's utilities court their new favorite customers: **data centers**. In August 2025, the commission approved Entergy's deal to serve Meta's massive Richland Parish campus, 4-1 -- negotiated terms, special treatment, the promise of jobs. Note the asymmetry. When the biggest power users in state history come knocking, the utility cuts bespoke deals. When a household cuts its own usage by ten percent, the utility recovers its "lost profits" from the neighbors.
The steelman deserves its say: fixed costs are real, and roughly twenty states decouple utility revenue from sales volume so that conservation doesn't bankrupt the wires-and-poles business. But Louisiana managed the worst of both worlds -- a charge for conservation, attached to programs that barely existed, administered by a commission that spent fourteen years promising a statewide program, killed it a year before launch, and then rebuilt the collection machinery anyway.
Fourteen years. Eighty million dollars. One dead program. One resurrected bureaucracy. And the single feature that survived every vote is the charge for using less. Louisiana has, in the end, achieved exactly one true decoupling: utility profits from performance.
So the next time you switch off a light to save money, enjoy the moment. Somewhere in Baton Rouge, a rider is being calculated -- and in this state, turning out the lights comes with a surcharge.

In most of America, the deal is simple: use less electricity, pay less. In Louisiana, regulators have spent over a decade perfecting a different arrangement -- one where your utility gets paid for the power you _didn 't use_. Not a rebate. Not a credit. A charge, collected right on your bill, for the profits the company says it lost because you had the nerve to conserve.
The mechanism has a boring name -- the "lost revenue adjustment mechanism," or in Louisiana's rules, recovery of the "lost contribution to fixed costs." Here's the plain-English version. Utilities argue that poles, wires, and power plants have to be paid for whether you flip a switch or not. Fair enough -- that's a rate-design debate older than most of us. But Louisiana's Public Service Commission went further. When an efficiency program actually works -- attic insulation, LED retrofits, an HVAC tune-up -- and your kilowatts drop, the utility doesn't just keep its guaranteed return on those fixed assets. It files to recover the sales it never made. You use less; the invoice uses more. Utilities call it revenue stability. Critics call it a charge for lost profits. Both are describing the same line item.
This has been a long game. The commission opened its energy-efficiency docket in 2011 -- the Louisiana Illuminator, summing things up in April 2025, called it a statewide energy efficiency program that it spent 14 years creating. In June 2013 the PSC voted to give the utilities a year to propose programs. In November 2014, Cleco, Entergy Louisiana, and Southwestern Electric Power launched their Quick Start efficiency programs -- and from day one, the rules let those utilities recover their lost contribution to fixed costs from the very customers the programs were supposedly helping. The American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy's review of lost-revenue mechanisms lists all three utilities and the 2014 arithmetic for doing it.

name: Aaron Day
subject: Eleven Senate races nobody's watching, live tonight
body:
** THE AARON DAY SHOW
------------------------------------------------------------

Defending Free Will in the Age of Technocracy
S3E28 • Nov 3

** Who Controls the Senate? Live Results Tonight
------------------------------------------------------------
https://us.list-manage.com/15yntWhysGX?e=938a87a89b&c2id=c1b996ddd6cdaaf4cddb384f099ac837

Thirty-five Senate seats are on the ballot tonight. Most networks will cover a handful of marquee races. Eleven of them could actually be decided by a third-party or independent candidate holding the balance of power: New Hampshire, South Carolina, Ohio, Kansas, Michigan, Texas, Arkansas, Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, and Alaska. Ohio also has its governor's race on the ballot tonight, New Hampshire has races of its own down the ballot, and so does the full U.S. House.
https://us.list-manage.com/_4FniHwI3HA?e=938a87a89b&c2id=c1b996ddd6cdaaf4cddb384f099ac837

We go live tonight with music videos before the results. Election results start at 6:00 PM ET and I'm staying on until the Senate results settle. That could run past 1 AM ET. Alaska's polls don't close until midnight ET, later than that in its western time zones.

Here's who's joining me tonight:

6:00 PM, Ernie Hancock. He hosts Declare Your Independence on talk radio out of Phoenix, publishes Freedom's Phoenix, and is the man behind the 2008 Ron Paul rEVOLution logo.

6:30 PM, Patrick Wood. He wrote Technocracy Rising, edits Technocracy News and Trends, and co-authored two books with the late Antony C. Sutton.

7:05 PM, Eric Brakey. Executive Director of the Free State Project, host of The Porcupine Report, a former three-term Maine State Senator, and author of Maine's Constitutional Carry law.

8:15 PM, Carla Gericke. President Emeritus of the Free State Project. Author, artist, and attorney.

9:05 PM, Chris Martenson. Founder and CEO of Peak Prosperity, author of The Crash Course (Wiley, 2011), with a PhD in Pathology from Duke and an MBA from Cornell. Elected to the Chester, Massachusetts Select Board this year.

About 9:15 PM, Jeff Wadlin. The Libertarian candidate for US Senate in Arkansas.

About 9:35 PM, Edmond Laplante. The Constitution Party's candidate for US Senate in New Hampshire.

About 10:20 PM, Ted Brown. The Libertarian candidate for US Senate in Texas.

clean_body: THE AARON DAY SHOW Defending Free Will in the Age of Technocracy S3E28 • Nov 3 Who Controls the Senate? Live Results Tonight Thirty-five Senate seats are on the ballot tonight. Most networks will cover a handful of marquee races. Eleven of them could actually be decided by a third-party or independent candidate holding the balance of power: New Hampshire, South Carolina, Ohio, Kansas, Michigan, Texas, Arkansas, Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, and Alaska. Ohio also has its governor's race on the ballot tonight, New Hampshire has races of its own down the ballot, and so does the full U.S. House. We go live tonight with music videos before the results. Election results start at 6:00 PM ET and I'm staying on until the Senate results settle. That could run past 1 AM ET. Alaska's polls don't close until midnight ET, later than that in its western time zones. Here's who's joining me tonight: 6:00 PM, Ernie Hancock. He hosts Declare Your Independence on talk radio out of Phoenix, publishes Freedom's Phoenix, and is the man behind the 2008 Ron Paul rEVOLution logo. 6:30 PM, Patrick Wood. He wrote Technocracy Rising, edits Technocracy News and Trends, and co-authored two books with the late Antony C. Sutton. 7:05 PM, Eric Brakey.
